Dungeon Defenders.  While the name may be remniscent of the classic tabletop fantasy RPG many of us know and love, Dungeon Defenders offers an entirely different world and a completely unique game experience.
A hybrid between tower defense and action RPG, Dungeon Defenders places you in the role of one of four young warriors left home alone while the Heroes of the Realm are away in battle.  When a mishap threatens to unleash the diabolical Old Ones from their imprisonment within the Eternia Crystals, however, it's up to you to devend the Eternia Crystals and save the world from a new age of darkness!
The gameplay of Dungeon Defenders is deceptively simple: find choke points you can use to defend the Eternia Crystals, build your towers in the Build Phase, and fight alongside and manage those towers during the Combat Phase.  But the simplicity of this system belies its incredible depth.  The real strategy of the game comes from upgrading your characters and equipment, allowing you to tackle increasingly-difficult challenges and difficulty levels, all the way up to the dreaded Nightmare Hardcore mode.
While the content included in the base game is great, it pales in comparison to the array of incredible DLC available for the game.  The opposite-gendered Heroes offer speed boosts and different abilities compared to the original four, the Barbarian allows for incredible DPS-oriented gameplay, the Series EV offers a number of variable-cost beams to buff and protect your towers, the Summoner brings forth minions and can even transform his play experience into a full-time RTS, and the Jester can move towers, run and upgrade speedily, deal incredible damage, and (with luck) control the battlefield with her Wheel of Fortuna skill, a true jack of all trades.  Each of these heroes comes with their own map that highlights their skills while offering new and innovative gameplay mechanics.  However, the ultimate challenge comes in the Quest for the Lost Eternia Shards DLC, which not only includes an entirely new campaign with even more difficult enemies, but also unlocks the aforementioned Nightmare and Hardcore options for all of the game's levels.
Still not enough for you?  Each level, once completed, offers Pure Strategy and Survival modes, where you can pit your tower-building skills against increasingly-difficult waves of enemies for increasingly powerful rewards, as well as a number of special Challenges that range from holiday celebrations to complete inversions of the core gameplay experience.  There are literally hundreds of hours of content available in Dungeon Defenders, and the experience is worth every one of them.
The game does have its problems.  The menus can be rather clunky, the Eternia Shards maps are an incredible difficulty spike from the campaign levels even on the easier difficulties, and the loot dropping mechanics are a little obtuse.  Additionally, while they don't overshadow the original characters, the DLC hero classes tend to be a requirement rather than an option on some of the more difficult maps, and the DLC map packs tend to drop better reward loot than the originals.  Still, the problems don't really get in the way of the fun, and the developers at Trendy Entertainment are always responsive to feedback.
On that note, I'd like to point out that Trendy Entertainment (the people who make the game) are incredibly open and helpful, and always willing to help people out in a pinch.  These are some of the most hardworking game developers I've seen, and they engage with the Dungeon Defenders community on an almost unprecedented level--even rivaling Mojang of Minecraft fame.  If you haven't done so yet, be sure to visit the Dungeon Defenders forums, which, in addition to offering numerous helpful guides and trading opportunities for the game, also serve as home to the Trendy blog, which provides and open window into the development of Dungeon Defenders, as well as into their current developments of Dungeon Defenders' upcoming sequel.  This is a studio incredibly devoted to their art, and they have a bright future ahead of them. :)

I don't recall the last time I've ever had so much fun on an SP only game. I want to start this review off by saying that the developers released a patch for the game to use DirectX11 and better support for 64-bit systems, about two years after it's release. These guys deserve your money.
Now, like many fans of the old Shadow Warrior, I was a little worried because I heard about all the changes from the gameplay to Wang's character himself, but the game still does have some "old-school" elements. While the levels are much more linear than the original, exploring and going off trail is still worth it as there are many secrets to be found and the gameplay is still very fast, intense and immersive. You can still find hentai chicks bathing themselves and singing, and even find secrets taking you back to levels from the old-school Shadow Warrior.
You're gonna use that katana a LOT. It's just so damn fun to use! Throughout the game, you'll be upgrading your katana and learning new attacks for it which will keep the sword feeling fresh. If you want to try out something new, in the pause menu you can change what kind of Katana you can use, including some laser/lightsaber thing and even the Excalibat from Rise of the Triad!
The guns are a lot of fun to use as well and you'll be upgrading those too. It has some of the same weapons from the original, such as the demon heart, demon head, rocket launcher (which freakin' kicks♥♥♥♥♥in this game), Uzi's (and dual wielding of course), a tearing♥♥♥♥♥shotgun (which gets a 4-shot chamber just like the original) as well as some added ones like a sexy and powerful Revolver, a big crossbow that can be upgraded to detonate explosions at will, and more.
Aside from weapons, you can also upgrade Wang himself and gain some other special powers that you will find out for yourself.
And obviously, there's Lo Wang. Duke Nukem's bother from another mother. I don't think this was intended, but I like to think of this as Lo Wang when he was younger and how he became so wise and powerful. The way he shaves his head and gets tattoos later on in the game makes him look like the classic Wang we know, so that was pretty sweet too.
Lo Wang is still an♥♥♥♥♥(he even claims to be in the game) and he's still full of awesome one-liners that you'll want to remember and use on people later on in real life because it's cliche. His voice acting is just great, from the cutscenes, to his trash-talking enemies, to his occasional scream from swinging the Katana so hard, to his screams and cursing when taking damage. It makes you feel like you're Wang almost.
Oh yeah, the cutscenes. I'm never a fan of cutscenes, or even stories in video games in general, but I did not skip a single cutscene in this game. The story is solid and will suck you in! (the cutscenes are skippable if you don't want to watch them.) Lastly, the graphics in this game may be the best I've seen yet. The normals, bumpmaps and lighting in this game is insane, very impressed on how it keeps the framerate so fluid especially with hordes of enemies attacking you in these overwhelmingly beautiful worlds.
There's so much I want to say, but so much that I don't want to spoil for you. You must try this game for yourself. If it means waiting for a sale, fine - but this game is worth more than it's usual $9.99 when it's 75% off (which is usually the discount it has). So if you want a modernized throwback of one of your favorite old-school games, grab this, you won't be disappointed. If you want a throwback to an old-school game that still keeps the old-school non-linear fast gameplay but with modern and pretty graphics, then grab Rise of the Triad. Wang is there too!

One of my favourite first-person shooters, Shadow Warrior is a reboot/remake of the classic Build Engine game, Shadow Warrior. While the original is perhaps best known for distastefully racist humour and annoying sword combat, this fresh take by veteran developers Flying Wild Hog (made of People Can Fly ex-pats, of Painkiller fame) is made distinct by large combat areas and refreshingly good sword combat.
It's an arcade shooter through and through, with audacious weapons, ridiculous enemies, and too many explosions. It combines with really satisfying slice-'em-up mechanics and a sense of weight and urgency not found in lighter "retro" shooters like Rise of the Triad, a distinctly stupid plot that lends the game a purpose (and a sense of humour) beyond dispatching wave after wave of slobbering ghouls, and fantastic graphics backed up by a gorgeous art direction. It's a "best of both worlds" scenario, with the impact and fidelity of modern shooters, backed up by the cornball antics of days gone by. I think it's exactly how Shadow Warrior deserved to be reincarnated - staying true to its "old-school" roots, while knowing exactly what to jettison to make this take on the title unique, instead of merely faithful.

'Do you recommend this game,' Steam asks me. I do, emphatically. I hope this anecdote from an in-game multiplayer experience I had will explain why. Prepare yourself for
Spring, 2011; early in my ARMA career, first tour of duty after a Steam Sale. I'm a fairly fresh recruit, seasoned with a couple dozen game-hours spent trudging through an expansive and swampy learning curve. Spent today at work, drove home, made dinner, cleaned up; it's Game-O'clock. Steam. ARMA2. Launch. Menu surfing, looking for multiplayer. Server browser hits my face with lists of information. -AWP-Warfare
mode looks appealing tonight. Played it a couple times before, and I feel comfortable with the basics by now. Server connection established.
Click! I'm in, filling the boots of a digital NATO badass. Apparently, international treaty organisations occasionally require the service of men with guns. Disturbing thought, but I'm no politician. I'm just a nobody with a rifle, taking orders that filter down the food chain. Those orders fill my mind now. Objective: town. Location: nearby...as the crow flies. Heh, the team's commander
have airborne technology unlocked, I just don't have the cash to buy a lift yet. Looks like I'm taking the scenic route. A quick check of my map tells me I'm at one of our hidden frontier bases and that there's two whole mountains between me and the nearby town. Great... I'll be taking the scenic route to the scenic route. The map tells me more: several of my team members and their A.I. controlled task forces are currently approaching the town. I'm already late for the party :(
Might as well bring the fireworks.
The base I'm at has only an armour factory and infantry barracks, but both will well suit my rapidly forming battle plan. I'm thinking heavy calibre fire support from high ground, overlooking the town. The topographic information in the map shows that the road I'll be taking is nestled around a minor hill as it approaches the town. Perfect. I'll park two BMPs there and they'll provide overwatch of the whole area while my comrades finish their capture of the town. An LAV will ferry me and one squad of A.I. infantry to the combat zone. I spend the required funds and set the plan in action.
Wait a tick, BeatYourHeadIn, are you telling me you actually have to plan how you’re going to get your troops and equipment from point A to point B in ARMA2? Logistics in a game!? Yes, actual logistics...in a game with a map so FRIGGIN’ big you need to employ logistical planning skills to see any sort of success. And it's not boring!
Back to the story. Formation of a military convoy. A few orders issued to my A.I. controlled task force later and the BMPs are on point while I lounge in the command chair of the LAV at the rear of the column. I man the turret-mounted automatic grenade launcher, a devastating weapon. Its barrel is ominously pointed at and tracking a lollygagging friendly player as my convoy departs base.
Though itching to test the power of my new toy, I decide it's not worth getting banned over.  I let my teammate live, for now.
The A.I. drivers of my convoy are as dim as a new moon, but I can fine tune my plans and keep up with current events while they drive. It's an 10 to 15 minute (realtime) drive that negotiates a winding mountain pass through an elegant evergreen forest. These are backroads, unpaved; enemy forces unlikely to be using this route. I feel secure enough that I spend most of the trip looking at the map, reading topography, lanes of fire, positions of friendlies. I smile when I realize I could probably minimize ARMA2 and play a few rounds of Counterstrike while my convoy travels.
Dying immediately is certainly the last thing I'm worried about as I crest the peak of the second mountain.
Suddenly: EXPLOSION..DEAFENING SOUND..FROM BEHIND..MASSIVE DETONATION..JESUS H. CHRIST WHERE IS THAT VOLUME KNOB! What is going on here!?
My turret pans to the rear of the LAV. The sight, what a sight...I'll never forget. Fire. Wall. 60? 70 feet tall? A wall. Of fire. Taller than the trees in the forest, literally FILLS my view from left to right. There is nothing in view except the fire. I'm in awe. Confused. Shaken. I've seen 'splosions in this game before, BUT NEVER LIKE THAT! Did somebody tried to nuke me FFS!? I know there's no nukes in this game mode, so...
Over the cacophany of destruction: the scream of jet engines. Very close. As the flames die down, a large shape traverses the air over the crest of the crag. Airframe, Sukhoi configuration. Enemy. Wing tilted down slightly; canopy visible. I know he's surveying the carnage below him. Hunting me. Cursing his aim when he sees the LAV still intact. I feel small, molecule small; what I just witnessed was caused by his war machine. Napalm bombs. Heavy ordinance. Whatever it was, it dealt complete destruction to that forest.
Understand this, readers: in this game, air superiority is a literal phrase. Air is SUPERIOR in this game. This isn't your Battlefield "oh look I can shoot a few rockets from my jet fighter and maybe kill one or two goofs on the ground and then reload (because reloading rockets on a flying jet makes a lot of sense) and kill a couple more goofs" experience. No! In ARMA your aircraft can have a payload of more than a hundred devastating rockets and you can fire 'em full auto like a machine gun and destroy an entire town worth of goofs on the ground if you wanted to. Ha! Forget about balance! This is the real life Shiznit. Modern air forces don't invest heavily in war planes because they're "balanced". They invest in them because they can kill a hell of a lot of people quickly! ARMA2 knows this. Simply put, the developers have a big Bohemian boner for air power.
But BeatYourHeadIn, what happened next? Tell us! Okay, I'll tell you. A miracle happened. My convoy survives the 'splosion to end all 'splosions. My battle plans go up in smoke like the forest around me. My current objective is to live through the next 30 seconds. The LAV is the only reason I'm still alive. It is damaged, but drivable. I order my drivers to haul♥♥♥♥♥in a forwardly direction. I track the Sukhoi as the convoy labours onward. The receding bogey performs a wide highspeed U-turn. He's heading straight for me again. Relentless much? He's the UPS guy we all wished was real: the one who comes back after he missed you the first time, instead of leaving a note telling you to pick up your package at the office near the airport!
Then, from beyond the first mountain I had passed: a smoke trail racing skywards. Anti-aircraft missile! Ha! RETURN TO SENDER, A-HOLE! Two vectors intersect in a puff of smoke and light. Direct hit! Booyah! Wait, uh... he's still flying at me. HEY! HE'S STILL FLYING AT ME!
With black smoke billowing out of his engines, this topgun is still determined to deliver my severance package. Frantically, I order the BMPs to target the limping jet. Cannon rounds arc through the sky in attempt to smite the airborne menace. Sukhoi Dude is getting closer, but he's losing altitude. Fast. He's now descending below my level on the mountain, looking up at me through the trees as he approaches. None of the BMP fire connects, but it doesn't matter. THIS GOOSE IS COOKED BOYS! Relief. Now, his desperation salvo of rocket fire is way off-target; falls harmlessly some distance away. I watch him frantically yaw right and nose up as his fighter loses the last of its life-sustaining lift and plummets in a sideways cartwheel into the trees. The inferno he leaves behind is a feast for the eyes. There was nothing left but a dark crater.
Now, I can start thinking about that town again...
What, are you apes gonna dig him a grave!? We got our own mission to die for! Forward march!
All that's left to say is: play this game!

"For want of a Nail....the kingdom was lost...."
Only you can unlock the mysteries of Hallownest, your Nail to save the kingdom, or not, as you choose.
PROS:
~The soundtrack. It is not only splendid in its own right, but also serves a clear purpose to every aspect of the game. You change areas? Awesome, the music changes. You're near certain enemies/situations? Fantastic, those have unique themes as well.
~The graphics. At a glance, they may not look like much. But the painstaking detail that was put into these hand-rendered scenes and animations. The dedication and adoration that was put into this is clear in every line and curve.
~The gameplay. You want to just hack-n-slash through? You can. You're the type that likes to find those hidden nuggets? Those are here, too. You want to talk to everyone, learn every secret? Cool, you practically can.
~The story. You have to find it, want it, work for it. Every piece of the puzzle. You aren't spoon fed. This isn't your hyper-linear RPG of modern day. This is classic, wanna-learn-gotta-earn lore delivery.
~The bosses. No two boss fights are the same. No two are even really similar (with special exceptions, not spoiling that, however). The mechanics, movements, patterns, attacks, everything is absolutely unique to each BBEG.
~The enemies. There's always a twist. That little challenge, or tweak. That hint of danger even when you think its past.
~The NPCs. Some are obvious, and helpful. Some are hidden, and secretive. Some you have to buy off, some freely give you all they know. Friends? Enemies? You may or may not learn, but none will leave your feelings untouched.
~The world. This map is vast, varied, and beautifully joined. The intermingling of areas, the crossing from A to B to C with a matter of baby steps, while other times may take you half a lifetime to see the next area. There is no shortage of world layout.
CONS:
~The vast world size could be considered cumbersome, if you have to go from one end to the other. (As a note, I did not find it so, but my experiences in Super Metroid have innoculated me against frustrations of these types.)
~The ability spread. There is that early-game-hump. Your money is sparse, and hard to get. Your abilities seem just a touch too weak, and you feel like everywhere you go is somewhere you need to revisit later, for one small section. It passes, but the frustration is justified.
Personal review:
This storyline is one of the most heart wrenching I have experienced, while at the same time housing a kernel of uplift that leaves the whole experience as one of nostalgia, longing, and a strong desire to play again (and again....and again....).
I have had to pause this game to wipe tears. Actually shouted at my screen. Stared in horror, awe, or despair. Genuinely covered my mouth in an attempt to suppress emotions I cannot define.
I love working this out, finding the breadcrumbs and following them. I am enamoured of the need to know still more, and the balance of light and darkness. Balance. Delicate, and wrought with heartache, forged in hope, and etched in loss, this game fulfils everything I have been waiting for for more than two decades....when I didn't even know I was waiting.
Do I recommend this game? ABSOLUTELY. But be warned. Be prepared. Hours, days, weeks. This game deserves them. And replayability is a no-brainer. Steel Soul mode or no, this is my new go-to for its genre, possibly even for my library as a whole. I encourage anyone, everyone, to buy this game. Give it a chance. There's still more to come, and I cannot wait. Join me in giddy anticipation, a journey through the world of Hallownest, down the path of discovery, and beyond the edges of memory.

One of my favourite first-person shooters, Shadow Warrior is a reboot/remake of the classic Build Engine game, Shadow Warrior. While the original is perhaps best known for distastefully racist humour and annoying sword combat, this fresh take by veteran developers Flying Wild Hog (made of People Can Fly ex-pats, of Painkiller fame) is made distinct by large combat areas and refreshingly good sword combat.
It's an arcade shooter through and through, with audacious weapons, ridiculous enemies, and too many explosions. It combines with really satisfying slice-'em-up mechanics and a sense of weight and urgency not found in lighter "retro" shooters like Rise of the Triad, a distinctly stupid plot that lends the game a purpose (and a sense of humour) beyond dispatching wave after wave of slobbering ghouls, and fantastic graphics backed up by a gorgeous art direction. It's a "best of both worlds" scenario, with the impact and fidelity of modern shooters, backed up by the cornball antics of days gone by. I think it's exactly how Shadow Warrior deserved to be reincarnated - staying true to its "old-school" roots, while knowing exactly what to jettison to make this take on the title unique, instead of merely faithful.

Hollow Knight is a stunning game. Its utterly beautiful to look at, with tons of atmosphere. The traditional animations are simply fantastic, up to the standard of any animated film.
Its world building and lore are fantastic and are communicated piecemeal in a similar to dark souls; through small comments, environmental story telling and cryptic clues that add up to create a mystery that you'll want to solve.
Gameplay and controls are tight. The platforming is similar to other metroidvania's and the skills are pretty typical for the genre: wall jumping, double jump, dashes, ground stomps etc. Personally I think the platforming side of it was great, very much like Ori and the Blind Forrest (only without the annoying momentum thing that made landing on small platforms such a chore in Ori).
The combat is a bigger focus than with some other metroidvania's and has some nice touches. Timing your attacks and dodges is essential with most of the mid-late game enemies, who thankfully telegraph their attacks in an easy enough to read way that if you get hit, its your own fault. Getting hit or hitting an enemy has knock back (on both ends) which can be used to your advantage or can ruin you if you're not paying attention.
The Boss battles are great, they're nicely varied and super satisfying. They can be frustratingly hard at times however; this is often due to the non-linear nature of the game and you being underprepared. If you are really struggling with a boss, you can turn this non-linearity to your advantage and simply go do something else and return when you're stronger.
The checkpoint system is similar to Dark Souls in that they're fairly far apart, replenish your health but also respawn all the enemies. Finding a bench in a new area gives a real sense of relief.
Personally I think its the single greatest metroidvania I've ever played. Its tough, but in a relatively fair way. It doesnt hand hold which does mean you feel a bit "in the dark" for the first hour or two, but I personally love that.

This game is not for people who queue solo. I'm a solo player. I just downloaded the game a couple of days ago. I'm still trying to get used to it because I've never played a top down game like this before. I'm not gonna lie, I suck at this game and I'm not having the best time playing it.
I'm noticing that underneath my name it says, "Placement" while others say, "Founder" and "Contender." I'm also noticing that while I'm solo I'm being paired against people who are in groups. You can tell who's in a group by the way they play. We get split up. They stay together.
My problem is the fact that I'm a solo/new player playing with randoms getting paired against premades with experience. We're at a disadvantage because we're not communicating as well as they are and we didn't pick our characters to coincide with one another. They almost always have a healer, we don't. Also, why are people who are new and still learning like myself being paired against people with more experience? Once again, we're at a disadvantage because I'm still learning. I can understand if there's not enough people playing to put premades against premades but there should be enough people in the same category to keep "placement" people with their own skill level.
I also feel the characters are unbalanced. Some characters are far more powerful than others. For instance, while playing the frog guy I noticed that I spend the entire match trying to catch up to the healer with the pet. I feel like this is not how it's supposed to be because the frog's kit is full mobility.
When you first start playing you don't notice the toxic community but once you enable chat the toxicity begins. Because I'm new and I'm still learning I get harassed a lot. This is a buzz kill because I'm still trying to get the hang of things. I don't need to be told the obvious like, "God you're bad." I already know that. You telling me is just killing my vibe. So if you're a new player keep the chat disabled. Trust me. You'll have more fun.
At the end of the day I think this isn't the game for me. I'm not enjoying it. I find it very difficult for me to get used to the camera angle. I don't like any of the characters they have available (I've tried them all). I wouldn't recommend this unless you're used to playing games like Dota 2 or League of Legends and want something more fast pace. I also wouldn't recommend this if you play alone a lot like I do.

I have a really hard time giving this game a thumbs down, but after the time I've spent with it, (mostly cursing and being disgusted with the spotty controls, borderling ridiculous platforming challenges and overall lack of direction) I can't see any other way.
I think my biggest problem with Hollow Knight is that it has SUCH GOOD IDEAS and really awesome areas to explore. I love the atmosphere and the art direction. The problems with platforming probably stems from engine limitations. The Unity Engine is easy to work with so many developers flock to it, but I find more often than not that the engine itself has issues with consistent frame rate, even on more than capable machines. There are small hitches and hiccups in gameplay, and jumping often feels problematic and can downright frustrate the hell out of you when you're tasked to perform jumps, dashes and other tricks in a lenghty and ludicrous platforming section, which demands 100% of you, and there is no room for mistakes. Mistakes ofen mean repeating those sections again. Dying and not reclaiming your soul means losing your currency, which is tedious to make in general.
Combat begins slow, and ends up ramping up in difficulty and becomes a chaotic and somewhat frustrating exercise later in the game. Boss battles will test your patience with their erratic behavior and seemingly relentless attack patterns, especially after dying frequently and having to trek back from the last save spot.
I genuinely love challening games, but Hollow Knight is the wrong kind of challening. It takes annoyance and tries to call it challenge. It takes tropes from the 8 and 16 bit era and tries to mask that as challenging, such as incredibly annoying enemies that occupy your space, to projectile spitting enemies that seem to have dead aim, and then add entire screens of these all at once and let the curse words fly.
There is just so much that I love in this game that is completely pushed aside for so much that I utterly hate. I can't see myself finishing this game becuase it honestly makes me mad. I don't get mad in games much anymore, but this game easily makes me want to puke. Every great piece of this game is buried in a pile of rubbish that has to be sorted through meticulously to be found, and that just isn't enough to redeem it.

The original Shadow Warrior (1997) was a crass and quick cash-in on the popularity of Duke Nukem 3D released a year earlier. What Duke 3D’s Duke was to casual sexism, Shadow Warrior’s Lo Wang was to casual racism. This reboot isn’t as heavy on the corny cliches and stereotyping, but it’s still able to offend the more sensitive types.
Thankfully, beneath the oriental trimmings and plot centered around themes of eastern mysticism, is a first-person shooter that excels at being what it is. Flying Wild Hog knows their stuff, as was proven by their excellent yet overlooked cyberpunk shooter Hard Reset (2011). Unlike the recent Rise of the Triad and Duke Nukem reboots, this one nails it. It’s the run-and-gun hard-boiled action 90s first-person shooter fans crave, but with modern trimmings to keep it fresh.
Using money, karma and ki crystals you find throughout levels, you can upgrade Lo Wang’s guns, buy attachments, and purchase powerful spells. The gunplay works well in conjunction with the spell system, letting you do both at once, for some nice combo moves. After each fight, you get scored based on how creative you were with your bullets, katana and mystical powers. The corny plot even manages to hold it together all the way to the end.

14 hours worth of game time so far after beating the game on normal and this has been one of the best games that I have played in a long time, I really do hope to see more from Flying Wild Hog.  The style, the sound track, the player movement, story, characters, VOs, combat, upgrade and RPG elements of the game and more combine to create one of the best FPS games that have come out in years.  A good story driven by a comic book, still picture images as well as the in game narrative which was good all the way to the end credits, a sad but good ending.  Honestly the only times that I didn’t have fun was when I died trying to get into some secret areas that were across water, pro tip the by way, Lo Wang is hydrophobic in this one soooo look for alternate paths if you’re hunting for secrets, that and the last mini-boss fight, man infuriating, but doable.
The game environment is very lush and varied; there are certainly colors in this game rather then generic brown or muddy colors and textures.  At times you might have too much stuff flying around, artifacts, effects and so on floating around which may distract you, however all enemies pop out and are very well contrasted between them and the background.
The sword and combat system are just so sweet I really didn’t think I would like it this much as I’m more of a gun kind of guy I surprised myself by favoring the sword over firearms, most of the time anyway.  However that’s this games major claim, the rpg element to this game is very well done allowing you to choose what your style of combat, whether it’s aggressive, defensive, healing, loot, or range, the skill trees are well done in that respect as well.  The gore is so sweet, dismemberment is fairly accurate and satisfying as are the special Ki moves that you gain and use.  That is one problem I had with the button combination system in this game, in later harder levels you will be hard pressed to do the button combos while in direct combat with mini bosses plus hordes bitting at your heels, I found that sometimes the system would not register my frantic button pushing for regeneration and I would just continue trying to dodge fire while attempting to problem solve.  Another problem that this game currently has is the weapon damange, even with full upgrades you will be hard pressed to rely on anything BUT your sword, everything short of the rocket launcher is needlessly weak.  This can cause problem in the higher difficulty settings since most enemies have higher hit points then they do in say easy or normal.  There are some points in this game that scream bad design, a few mini boss fights, some enemy units and the second to last large fight are just a few that make me wonder what the developers were even thinking.  With the added bonus of the Special Edition I still have 2 other melee weapons to choose from and as I understand this game one beaten has an extra mode where you keep your level and powers and continue on.  You probably will not get all of your skills and powers leveled up to the max on the first run, if you have a loot and secret guide you may but I like it, making going through the game on another run, possibly on a harder difficulty palatable and possible to me.
The sound track was very good as it sets the pace well for each fight and calm moments, I rather liked it.
Honestly I’d say buy this game when you can, either on sale or full price because right now, it was well worth the money and only later did I start to get more used to the combo system, I’m pretty sure on my second play through I’ll enjoy it just as much or even more.  I would say support Flying Wild Hog, as for me, they have earned it.

Arma 2: Operation Arrowhead/Combined Operations is a excellent military simulator that can be easily modded to fit the players' needs and can be a good Tactical Realism game when utilized to its fullest potential. Not a game recommended for players who expect aspects from Call of Duty, Medal of Honor, Battlefield, or other popular First-Person Shooters. In this Mil-Sim game, players are to think before they act; playing through the multiple scenarios in their head before executing their tactics. Communication is highly recommended since this game generally requires teamwork, collaboration, and team playing in order to accomplish missions. In addition, new players are highly recommended to play the "Boot Camp" scenarios in single-player mode until they feel confident enough to play on multiplayer servers. This includes, but not limited to Infantry Combat/Warfare, Controlling AI, *Flying Aircraft*, Driving Ground Vehicles, Understanding Logistics/Support, etc... The few flaws of this game are:
1) HACKERS & Team Killers. Indeed, hackers tend to lurk in multiplayer servers and to reduce the amount of gameplay from being ruined, join a server with an active admin. Team killers are an often occurance since new players do not identify targets before they shoot.
2) Poor AI. Although there are many mods that can fix this problem, the default AI behavior can be irritating for certain situations (e.g. piloting aircrafts, driving ground vehicles, infantry combat).
3) Bugs/glitches. There are low chances that bugs/glitches may occur and can happen in the wrong place and wrong time. This is especially hazardous when you are flying an aircraft. Players tend to have to restart/reboot the entire game/computer to fix this problem.
4) Lag and Frames Per Second issues. This common if you do not have a high-preformance computer, poor internet connection, or playing in a server hosted on the other side of the world (e.g. you live in the US but play on a server in the UK). Another common cause of lag is smoke and explosions. Smoke grenades, demolishing buildings, firing high volumes of Hydra rockets, explosions from artillery/mortars, and others can cause a significant decrease FPS which can reduce gameplay performance like player movement, camera panning, and others.
Conclusion: Overall, this game is best Mil-Sim game avaiable to the public.

At first, I was hesitant to purchase this game simply based off the premise of it being a risk to purchase indie games you don't know a lot about. I can honestly say however, that this game blew away my expectations in every way. The game is a masterpiece, for all the following reasons:
1. Basic Combat/ Directional Movement: The combat in this game is perfectly set up to make the game challenging, yet never feel unfair. You can slash in any four directions, that being up, down, left, or right. This has been something I've felt has been left out of most games properly in the past, and was done very well in this game. Since the width of the strikes covers pretty much the majority of the side being slashed in, there will be few times where you can't hit an enemy since they are diagonal from you. The movement (for the majority of the game) will consist of walking, jumping, wall climbing, or dashing. Each of these works perfectly in tangent with one another, not to mention the fact that you can still slash in any direction while in the air.
2. Abilities/ Charms: While the basic combat will never really change, the charms do a great job in adding plenty of variety to everything about your play style. It is very much customizable, which lets you take on any situation, with your own twist. There are only a handful of abilities to find, but each of them is useful in their own way. The charms can also effect your abilities, going so far as to conpletely revamp what the abilities do in the first place.
3. Difficulty: The game is hard, no questions asked. The first portion of the game does a good job in preparing you for the later sections, but when that difficulty spike hits, it hits hard. There are a number of things in this game which are made perfectly difficult, to teach you new things about the game, without making you feel its too easy, or too hard. Then out of the blue, it strikes. All of a sudden you start to fail a lot more, on certain bosses, and 1 challenge in particular.
for an average player, this would be a huge problem, but for my fellow gamers who enjoy unbearable difficulty (Dark Souls), we will find some strange enjoyment out of these immensly hard games. So take this as a warning, if you want to 100% it, or see the true ending, be prepared to die, alot.
4. Platforming: Before you purchase this game, you should know that there is a ton of platforming. It is done in a "Super Meat Boy" esque style, with its original varieties, which makes for a very solid platformer. Not to mention that you will be fighting enemies while trying to do difficult platforming, which can be very difficult. Be prepared to be almost perfect in later parts of the game, when it comes to timing your jumps, and mastering the parkour entirely to complete the "ultimate challenge". If you enjoy difficult platforming, then this game is for you.
5. Level Design/ World: Don't think that just because it is difficult that the game is not properly built. The level design is top notch, and is made so that the parkour in question is difficult, but never impossible. Enemies are placed in perfect ways that doesn't feel like they just stuck them randomly to add some challenge. The world as a whole is huge, filled to the brim with secrets, collectables, enemies, and a load of bosses. It never feels boring, or repetitive, since every section feels very different from the last. You can find a number of optional areas throughout the game, that you never need to find in order to beat the game. It has to be one of the best, and most varied worlds in any metroidvania i've ever played.
6. Length: When you go into this game, you may be worried that it will be a few short hours of exploring, then the game is over. Do not be mistaken, you can easily pool 40-50 hours in this game, just trying to get the true ending. I feel that this game has the perfect length, not too short, and not too long. When it comes to open-world games with tonnes of content, they tend to become repetitive, and boring the longer you play them. with an endless barrage of things to do, that all feel the same. While some games can have lots of variety, but are beaten in only a few short hours, leaving you dissapointed, and wanting more. This game is lengthed perfectly, lots of stuff to do to keep you comign back, but not so much that it becomes tedious. I would recommend the game purely on this fact alone, yet it just keeps giving.
7. Emotional feel: The game is gloomy, with its primary story arch being the deaths of thousands of bugs on a massive scale. Fighting against the reanimated corpses of dead bugs, and trying to discover the truth behind it all. It is a sad story, which is consistent throughout the entire game from beginning to end. The level design is perfectly dark and twisted, with the occasional happy level to break the tension. You can also expect a Dark Souls esque story, which is a little bit easier to understand.
Final Remarks: Having played the game for over 50 hours, and beating 100% in 40 hours, I can honestly consider this game not only my current favourite of 2017, but also one of the best metroidvania's ever made. The artstyle is award winning, and the soundtrack has the perfect mix of sad tones, and happy songs all sharing the same style which adds so much to the game as a whole. I would recommend this game a thousand times over, for full price. I am excited for whatever it is that Team Cherry does in the future, and will be keeping my eyes open for what they create.

This game is loads of fun. It brings back the feeling of old-school shooters like the classic Duke Nukem games. No waist-high cover shooting here. You'll be running and gunning against hordes of demons, all of which can be reduced into tiny chunks via katana, bullets, or explosives. Speaking of explosives, if you like killing enemies using the environment you will be very happy to know that there are plenty of explosive barrels, arcade machines, lamps, generators, etc. Another welcome classic shooter feature is secrets. Those who wander off the beaten path will find helpful items as well as retro areas that are a throwback to the classic Shadow Warrior game.
It's not just an old-school shooter with a fresh coat of paint though. There's quite a bit of character progression via skill and power upgrades, and all weapons have purchaseable upgrades, some of which make a fairly normal guns into something quite a bit more ludicrous.
There's also a system where each encounter is rated based on how stylishly you murder the waves of demons in an area. You get points via a score system similar to Bulletstorm's. Kills attained with different weapons and different methods will earn you a variety of bonuses. And the bonus you get goes toward upgrading your skills, so it pays to go for skillshots.
The health system is an interesting hybrid. It doesn't have regenerative health like many modern shooters, but it isn't soley a health-pickup system either. You have a demonic power to regenerate your health, but it's not passive. You have to activate it yourself and it only heals up to 65% of your max HP. Skills and powers can change how effective it is, but they can also improve what you get out of health pickups.
Most surprising though is how good this game looks. I wasn't expecting much since it's not a AAA release, but some of the effects and environments are really nice to look at. Another surprise is that there's actually a pretty decent plot amongst all the demon slaying. It's delivered in bits through chats with your demon buddy, and through above average quality animatics. In general there are a lot of little details that didn't really need to be there. Pressing the reload button with a full magazine plays a cool little animation, and a lot of insignificant items in the world are fully destructable.
The game has a good sense of humor too, and I enjoyed playing a shooter that didn't take itself too seriously. There are many wang jokes to be had, and the conversations between the main character and his snarky demon sidekick are pretty entertaining. The fortune cookies scattered throughout the levels all contain amusingly absurd messages too.
All in all, if you are sick of modern military shooters and want an over-the-top shooter where the final weapon in your arsenal is a rocket launcher, this is the game for you.

Allow me to start by saying, I'm not a fan of the original Shadow Warrior.  To be honest, I don't even know what it was that got my attention.  But I'm glad it did.  For those not interested in a long winded review, then I'll just say if you're a fan of Serious Sam or Painkiller, then you'll like this game, and that's all you really need to know.
For the more in depth review, I'll start with the gameplay, as that's the most important aspect of this game.  Over the course of the game you'll pick up 7 different upgradable weapons, 2 consumable non-upgradable demon weapons, 3 different special attacks for your Katana and 4 different Ki abilities (2 offensive and 2 defensive) in addition to a tree of Karma abilities that are mostly passive bonuses.  All of this comes together almost seemlessly, I say almost because the overall gameplay is good, but not great.  Nearly all the weapons feature iron sights, but shooting they tend to be very inaccurate without the assistance of the crosshair, but in the end it didn't matter because using iron sights limited your field of view and slowed your movement.  Neither of these things are useful during the high action fights.  Each of the weapons are useful throughout the entire game, each has an area where they excell over others, but none end up feeling useless by a certain point in the game.  If I had any greviences with the overall gameplay (outside the inaccurate iron sights), it would be I found getting the Ki and Katana abilities  were a bit finnicky to pull off once the action really started to ramp up.  I found the charge up abilties on the Crossbow and Rocket Launcher could be a bit unresponsive.  More than once had I been dancing around waiting for the perfect moment to unleash my charged up bolt or rocket only to discover I had nothing charged and ready.  This was the only real issue I had during my 15 hours of a game that was in the end extremely fun to play.  To me that's the most important thing, the game is still a blast to play inspite of the minor issues.
The story starting off and throughout most of the game is fairly basic.  It's not until near the end when the reveals you expect to happen don't actually happen.  Even though the first three quarters of the story is predictable, the last portion isn't and it's in that last quarter that I felt the story got interesting and it all culminated in a surprisingly emotional ending.  Not Season 1 Walking Dead emotional considering everything that came before.  Like with the gameplay part, I can't be down on the first three quarters of the story because while it is on the predictable side, it's never boring.  The banter between Wang and Hoji is at the least entertaining and at the most downright funny.
I highly recommend this game because it's entertaining, funny and great mindless action without ever getting repetitive.  This is the game Bioshock Infinite wishes it was.

This is a game I can't beleive I did not play sooner.
I personally thought it would be something a la Salt & Sanctuary, and didn't feel like playing a souls game at the moment.
Turns out its actually more of a METROIDVANIA style game, a genre I grew up with, playing Metroid specially, and ONE OF THE BEST ON ITS GENRE.
Now, I haven't beaten the game yet, probably around 30-50% of it? Hope its more towards the former since I want this game to last as long as possible. I'll omit the story since I don't know enough of it yet for obvious reasons, but do know so far it's looking great. Really Dark Souls-y, piecing together the story from what you find out and talking to people, which i personally love.
Summed up briefly,
THE ANIMATION & CONTROLS
Fantastic. Solid controls, really responsive, and with a bit of depth on the things you can do, and how to tacle enemies, specially since its melee oriented, so you have to be up close to the Enemies.
Also love the small details in the animations, how for example you see bugs and stuff moving on the background and foreground, how your character opens a map when you look at the map ingame, etc...
DESIGN & ATMOSPHERE
I'm not exaggerating when I say this is one of the MOST BEAUTIFUL games I've played in recent years. The bug-world design is beautifully crafted to the smallest details. It honestly feels like what a Bug-society might look like if it became intelligent and developed further.
The design of each area is individually stylised and crafted, with its own music, and theme, lots of interactive elements (grass rocks posts,...) that make you feel there. Speaking of posts, they ACTUALLY GUIDE YOU to places in the area. From the unique little things to the general composition of the areas, the world is Immersive and beautifully crafted, and all INTERCONECTED a la Dark Souls or any good Metroidvania game.
The CHARACTERS are also really unique, really well designed, and their voice acting is just great haha. It reminds me of the kind of characters you met in dark souls, how you find them around the world doing their own things with their own goals. They are all somewhat cute, but really fitting into the world, some being more dark, some just downright adorable, like the worms you rescue and their papa-worm.
MUSIC & SOUND
Just, buy the soundtrack. It's worth it. Music is fantastastic in this game, it's just on point. It takes you into this world, sucks you in visually and with its music aswell. The Voice acting is also adorable, but really well done too. They speak some unknown made up language, but it perfectly fits the characters and tone of the game.
OVERALL, this game is a masterpiece. I know it sounds like I might be exaggerating, because I mostly say positive things, but so far there is not a single drawback i could come up with. Maybe the slight movement when attacking on tight platforms but there are ways to deal with that too. Everything you would want, is there. It's a great package and apparently its easy a 20h+ game, FOR 15€ ITS A STEAL.
If you like:  METROIDVANIA, DARK SOULS, or just beautifully crafted worlds, do yourself a favour, and buy it. This game deserves it, don't even wait for a sale at its base price its a fantastic deal. And its made by an 3-person indie studio. It is insane what people with passion can craft.

A fantastic game and my personal favorite metroidvania. A few things that I particularly enjoyed about the game:
. Beatiful art and animation (obviously)

. Atmosphere. The game has mad style. The dark gothic setting will no doubt conjure up thoughts of Dark Souls for many but the ancient bug kingdom of Hallownest feels unique and refreshing to me. The game world never feels too grim or oppressive thanks to the charming and cartoony characters
. Variety. There is a diverse array of environments in this surprisingly huge game world. I was also pleasantly surprised by the wide variety of enemy types and bosses
. RPG mechanics. While there isn't really any character customization to speak of, you do become more powerful as you progress through the game and you also obtain equippable items with various benefits called "charms." The number of charms you can equip at one time is limited and you can mix and match charms to fit your playstyle. On more than one occassion I was stuck on a boss but later was able to best it easilty, simply by equipping a different set of charms. This type of thing is something I personally really enjoy from RPGs

Okay just to start off, this game requires Uplay. I know thats an issue for some people so take that as you will.
Anyway more imprtantly to the game itself and i was quite happy to find there's been an improvement over the last couple of AC games particularly the awful AC3.
In this game you play Edward Kenway who's a pirate in the Carribbean and it makes for a great setting and experience. Edward is the best lead character since Ezio and is a likeable guy with plenty of personality. The games setting is fantastic as well with loads of beautiful tropical environments with the oppurunity to sail around the Carribbean and explore. You've got Havana,Nassau and Kingston as your 3 main cities though these are a bit dissappointing particularly Nassau and Kingston as they are pretty unimpressive compared to some of the great cities of the older games.
As for the gameplay it's also improved. All the pirate stuff you can do like attack and board ships and sail around looking for treasure is a lot of fun. The assassin stuff almost feels boring in comparision. There is also a lot of "follow" missions in this game as i've always hated these missions the most in AC games and this one is littered with them. That said there still is a lot to do and explore and you will get your moneys worth from this game.
Surprisingly the music in this game is probably one of the best parts of this game. As you sail your crew will sing sea shanties which is brilliant and really gives it that pirate atmosphere. I've found myself humming the tunes after playing. You can also collect more shanties which will be unlocked for your crew to sing.
The Good:
- Great interesting protaganist in Edward Kenway and a few more interesting characters as well
- All the pirate activities are a lot of fun.
- The Carribbean looks great in this game and you've a big area to travel and explore in.
-The music in this game is brilliant.
The Bad:
-The story isn't particularly interesting and a bit hard to follow at times
- The assassin stuff is pretty boring and there's way too many "follow" missions
-Controls still feel awkward and fiddly at times
-Game can be fairly buggy at times
Overall this is a step in the right direction again for the AC series and probably my favourite since AC2. It gets an 8/10 from me.

Okay I have to say, this was one of the most frustrating games I've played. First let me highlight the good bits:
* Lots of humor, lots of swearing, totally doesn't take itself seriously. Shadow warrior makes fun of itself just as much as it makes fun of other games, and that's great. Lots of callbacks to pop culture and other games.
* The boss fights are really, really cool and on a huge, epic scale, they're very reminiscent of the "classic" boss experience and it's fantastic.
* Lots of variety in weapons.
* Interesting level design.
* The design and graphics, and the style, seem to work as long as you don't look too hard at any particular thing. Which you can't anyway because it's really fast paced and I like that.
* SWORD COMBAT!!!! (there's no blocking but you kind of don't need to)
* The little details, like chopping up demons into little bits after they're dead and seeing how the devs carefully managed to make the models separate in a realistic way with plenty of gore and blood, and I think that sort of thing is really fun.
Okay. This is all my personal opinion, I've read lots of reviews and heaps of people did like it. My main, big big issue with this game is how annoying it was. It dragged on and on and on and kept making me repeat bits of the same level over and over, fighting the same enemies again and again. It's not fun when it's so repetitive! It felt like a goddamn chore to keep playing but I really wanted to see the ending. You fight through a level only to find your path blocked and you need the key, so you go back, find it, go back towards the gate and whoops, there are the same enemies again. I felt myself asking every time I killed them all "are we done yet?" Apparently not because they come in identical waves and waves, and they throw more and more minibosses at you like they're regular enemies.
It is not fun to make players do the same thing over and over again with very little variety. There are some enemies (particuarly the minibosses) that are really tricky to kill and apparently the devs' idea of fun is to toss you in a small room with multiple of these like "here, try this!" and when you win it's like "okay, now do it again!" It's so frustrating! And every now and then it's like they remembered, "oh they haven't seen this particular enemy in a while, let's just like, flood an entire room with them, that's fun right?" And it just gets boring after a while, and that boredom leads to frustration when it's so relentlessly repeated over and over.
There were some really cool unique bits, and I was totally hooked from the very beginning, it was cheesy and hilarious but about halfway through I just felt like I was going through the motions. It really takes you out of the immersion and reminds you that you're pressing buttons on a keyboard and clicking a mouse over and over. I reckon the best kind of game lets you forget what you're doing and really engrosses you in the whole setting and story, but I didn't feel it here. Maybe if it were shorter, or if there were more variety, then it would have been totally terrific.

This game is not for people who queue solo. I'm a solo player. I just downloaded the game a couple of days ago. I'm still trying to get used to it because I've never played a top down game like this before. I'm not gonna lie, I suck at this game and I'm not having the best time playing it.
I'm noticing that underneath my name it says, "Placement" while others say, "Founder" and "Contender." I'm also noticing that while I'm solo I'm being paired against people who are in groups. You can tell who's in a group by the way they play. We get split up. They stay together.
My problem is the fact that I'm a solo/new player playing with randoms getting paired against premades with experience. We're at a disadvantage because we're not communicating as well as they are and we didn't pick our characters to coincide with one another. They almost always have a healer, we don't. Also, why are people who are new and still learning like myself being paired against people with more experience? Once again, we're at a disadvantage because I'm still learning. I can understand if there's not enough people playing to put premades against premades but there should be enough people in the same category to keep "placement" people with their own skill level.
I also feel the characters are unbalanced. Some characters are far more powerful than others. For instance, while playing the frog guy I noticed that I spend the entire match trying to catch up to the healer with the pet. I feel like this is not how it's supposed to be because the frog's kit is full mobility.
When you first start playing you don't notice the toxic community but once you enable chat the toxicity begins. Because I'm new and I'm still learning I get harassed a lot. This is a buzz kill because I'm still trying to get the hang of things. I don't need to be told the obvious like, "God you're bad." I already know that. You telling me is just killing my vibe. So if you're a new player keep the chat disabled. Trust me. You'll have more fun.
At the end of the day I think this isn't the game for me. I'm not enjoying it. I find it very difficult for me to get used to the camera angle. I don't like any of the characters they have available (I've tried them all). I wouldn't recommend this unless you're used to playing games like Dota 2 or League of Legends and want something more fast pace. I also wouldn't recommend this if you play alone a lot like I do.

I can't remember the last time a 2d game thrilled and challenged me this much, it's almost overwhelming.  The game is a masterpiece.  It has everything thing.   Beautiful art, music, sounds, gameplay, style, value, variety and fun.  I have to say the challenge is so amazingly well ramped from the easy breasy start to the heart racing white knuckle hard-mode boss fights SO many games get that wrong and this game nails it.  The death mechanic is brilliant, when you die a dark vessel comes out of you.  Then you must return to your death point from a save point and defeat the vessel!  It's so good!
Basically if you like modern games in the 2-d metroid/castlevania style (like axiom verge) get this game immediately.
If you like dark souls and wish there was something similar but in 2-d.  Get this game.
If you're a "premium games only" gamer, this is one of those premium top notch games.  Get it.
There are just a few issues with the game that you may encounter - it should not stop you from buying the game if you're interested but I have to disclose them to be fair.
-You really need a controller.   I used a xbox 360 wireless controller and it was fantastic.
-The game is quite large, and even though there's some fast travel options backtracking and looking for secrets/extras can be really time consuming.
-There are a few parts of the game that were for me just insanely hard - BUT They are almost ALL OPTIONAL.  So, if you want the hard ending put on your dark souls hat and get ready to die and retry, or look up some tips if you get frustated because you're going to get pushed.  However just getting the regular ending provides a fair challenge without the frustration so you can always take that route first and then go back if you really want to do the hard stuff.
I'm so happy I played this game and I look forward to future games by the developer Team Cherry.

Okay I have to say, this was one of the most frustrating games I've played. First let me highlight the good bits:
* Lots of humor, lots of swearing, totally doesn't take itself seriously. Shadow warrior makes fun of itself just as much as it makes fun of other games, and that's great. Lots of callbacks to pop culture and other games.
* The boss fights are really, really cool and on a huge, epic scale, they're very reminiscent of the "classic" boss experience and it's fantastic.
* Lots of variety in weapons.
* Interesting level design.
* The design and graphics, and the style, seem to work as long as you don't look too hard at any particular thing. Which you can't anyway because it's really fast paced and I like that.
* SWORD COMBAT!!!! (there's no blocking but you kind of don't need to)
* The little details, like chopping up demons into little bits after they're dead and seeing how the devs carefully managed to make the models separate in a realistic way with plenty of gore and blood, and I think that sort of thing is really fun.
Okay. This is all my personal opinion, I've read lots of reviews and heaps of people did like it. My main, big big issue with this game is how annoying it was. It dragged on and on and on and kept making me repeat bits of the same level over and over, fighting the same enemies again and again. It's not fun when it's so repetitive! It felt like a goddamn chore to keep playing but I really wanted to see the ending. You fight through a level only to find your path blocked and you need the key, so you go back, find it, go back towards the gate and whoops, there are the same enemies again. I felt myself asking every time I killed them all "are we done yet?" Apparently not because they come in identical waves and waves, and they throw more and more minibosses at you like they're regular enemies.
It is not fun to make players do the same thing over and over again with very little variety. There are some enemies (particuarly the minibosses) that are really tricky to kill and apparently the devs' idea of fun is to toss you in a small room with multiple of these like "here, try this!" and when you win it's like "okay, now do it again!" It's so frustrating! And every now and then it's like they remembered, "oh they haven't seen this particular enemy in a while, let's just like, flood an entire room with them, that's fun right?" And it just gets boring after a while, and that boredom leads to frustration when it's so relentlessly repeated over and over.
There were some really cool unique bits, and I was totally hooked from the very beginning, it was cheesy and hilarious but about halfway through I just felt like I was going through the motions. It really takes you out of the immersion and reminds you that you're pressing buttons on a keyboard and clicking a mouse over and over. I reckon the best kind of game lets you forget what you're doing and really engrosses you in the whole setting and story, but I didn't feel it here. Maybe if it were shorter, or if there were more variety, then it would have been totally terrific.

This has to be one of my favouite games that I have played recently.  Just about everything in it exceeds my expectations to no end.
First up, the gameplay.  The weapons just feel right.  Each one has impact when you hit the buttons.  Each one is distinct enough to be useful in certain situations and less so in others, but they're all good enough to get the job done.  There are a ton of little details that just work so well, like the 'throw shuriken' button becoming the 'quick melee' attack when you're wielding a gun.  It just makes sense that way, and using it is second nature.  Then there's the way that if you reload with a full clip while standing still, the MC will check the gun's amunitions to show you that it is, in fact, full.  It's a visual effect, so that you know that the game registered your button press, instead of just ignoring it.
The swordplay deserves a whole paragraph unto itself.  While the game never tells you this directly, sword swings are influenced by your movement, and also by the movement of your mouse.  If you want to swing from right to left, move your view in the same direction.  It also works for up and down and even diagonal.  This can be useful against certain enemies, or when you're aiming for headshots.  It's just really nice and flows really well when you're playing.  Again there are a ton of small details in the swordplay as well, such as if you are wielding a gun and there is an enemy up in your face and you pull out your sword, the MC does a draw-attack.  And why not?  He's got the animation for it, it's the normal quick attack when you're wielding a gun, but instead of re-sheathing the sword, he puts the gun away.  Little details that make so much sense.
The next amazing thing is the visuals.  Even on my few years old laptop the graphics still look very impressive, particularly the lighting and physics.  Explosions will throw around glowsticks, which cast long shadows of the bones they go flying past.  The only things which I think could have done with some improvement were the smoke and the fabrics, and I suspect that was simply because the advanced physics were turned off on my machine.
Even better than the mechanics of the visuals is the art direction of the game.  Reality and plausability are put as secondary concerns next to visual impact and design.  Scenes are set with strong colours and excellent choice of palette, making each level feel both memorable and distinct.  Even when a location is revisited then the subtle changes of lighting recast it in a new light and make it feel like things have changed.
Which leads us onto the next, and perhaps single most impresive fascet of the game:  The level design.  The level designers here need a raise.  I don't care what they were paid, it simply isn't enough.  I don't even know where to begin.  Each level follows its own progression, usually through three or four distinct areas.  But the areas aren't always simply in order.  Quite often you find yourself doubling back, once new paths have opened up, and each time enemys respawn, making the once-prisine arenas battle scarred, and then bloodstained a second time.  But the destruction you wreak upon the landscape is permanant, and lasts between fights, even if they happened at the start and the end of the level.
The level's aren't overly large, but they tend to wind back over themselves, you will enter a room and be shot at from the overlooking walkway, and then three or four rooms later you will be fighting on that very same walkway and admiring the view of the room you were in from a new perspective.  The game has a habit of showing you where you are going and where you came from repeatedly, so even when I was treking through the maze of corridors or platforming up a winding mountain path I never feel particularly lost.
In terms of progression, there are three simultanious upgrade paths throughout the game.  First is money, which is collected throughout the world, and spent to upgrade your ranged.  Second is Karma, which is awarded for doing well in combat and finding some secrets.  Karma is spent to upgrade skills and improve your stats like health and stamina.  Third are the Ki Crystals, which are interspersed throughout the game and unlock ki powers, supernatural abilities that can be used with any weapon equipped to give you an extra edge.  The mix of upgrade paths means that the player is encouraged for exploring and doing well and ensures that there is always a new upgrade just on the horizon to look forwards to.
Even the plot, which I expected to be classic B grade terrible, turned out to have a fair amount of naunce to it.
The game is not too long, but it's not short either.  You can expect to actually finish the game in a reasonable amount of time, which is refreshing after playing through some recent releases that have level upon level of filler in the middle.  While when playing it sometimes felt like I wasn't sure where the overarching plot was going, each level worked to forwards the goal at hand.
There is basically no reason why I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a first person action game.

Hollow Knight is one of the best games I have ever played. The game has about 30 hours of play time, depending on how much of it you actually want to complete. Not to mention it's an amazing game for only $15.
The gameplay is challenging, but incredibly rewarding. The progression is structured in a way where you immediately understand new mechanics. Once you master these mechanics it feels so natural, and you often find yourself having moments where you're amazed you "actually pulled that off." There are a healthy amount of bosses, each with extremely elegant mechanics. There weren't any bosses I found easy to beat, with quite a few taking a lot of attempts. The combat is incredible well done, requiring very quick but precice actions.
I immediately fell in love with the world the game takes place in. Every character and enemy are bugs living in a kingdom destroyed by a mysterious infection. The story is somewhat vague, but in a way that you still feel like you understand what is happening. The named characters have a wonderful charm to them where you want to learn everything about them, which you can do periodically throughout the game when meeting them.
All in all, if you're a Metroidvania fan or a big fan of the Souls games I could not recommend Hollow Knight enough. I would be surprised if another game passed up this one as my 2017 GotY.

Simply put, one of the most amazing experiences you'll have in an FPS this side of the new millenium. It effortlessly blends humor and serious storytelling, a worthwhile plot and meaningful characters and development of their stories and personalities, and incredibly fun, pulse pounding combat that will have you on the edge of your seat more often than not. The combat is very well done, wth numerous skill combinations and weapon types available in your arsenal, and the ability to specialise and upgrade them how you wish. The Art of this game is positively stunning, and the graphics are downright gorgeous. It may be demanding specifications wise, but not on the level of say Crysis or the like, and its impressive how well the game runs on a middling system like mine with so many of its settings maxed or near maxed.
All in all, a game that seriously restored my faith in a genre I had given up to stagnation and endless CoD clones, and managed to provide a full package (Lo Wang would laugh at that line, I'm sure) that included every single thing short of multiplayer that you could ask for. Indeed, the lack of multiplayer is the only real design flaw this game has in my opinion. And even that can't keep me from looking fondly upon the hours I spent hacking away at demon hordes, nor can it overshadow the surprisingly deep story and characters. Seriously, try to play this game through without developing some form of liking towards Lo Wang and Hoji. They'll make you laugh, and they may even tug at your heartstrings at times. It's almost magical how alive they feel as the story progresses.
10/10 in my book, an excellent game few, if any, should pass up, even if it isnt completely perfect, its perfectly enjoyable and a blast from the past that will have you glued to your PC from start to finish.

Hollow Knight is a stunning game. Its utterly beautiful to look at, with tons of atmosphere. The traditional animations are simply fantastic, up to the standard of any animated film.
Its world building and lore are fantastic and are communicated piecemeal in a similar to dark souls; through small comments, environmental story telling and cryptic clues that add up to create a mystery that you'll want to solve.
Gameplay and controls are tight. The platforming is similar to other metroidvania's and the skills are pretty typical for the genre: wall jumping, double jump, dashes, ground stomps etc. Personally I think the platforming side of it was great, very much like Ori and the Blind Forrest (only without the annoying momentum thing that made landing on small platforms such a chore in Ori).
The combat is a bigger focus than with some other metroidvania's and has some nice touches. Timing your attacks and dodges is essential with most of the mid-late game enemies, who thankfully telegraph their attacks in an easy enough to read way that if you get hit, its your own fault. Getting hit or hitting an enemy has knock back (on both ends) which can be used to your advantage or can ruin you if you're not paying attention.
The Boss battles are great, they're nicely varied and super satisfying. They can be frustratingly hard at times however; this is often due to the non-linear nature of the game and you being underprepared. If you are really struggling with a boss, you can turn this non-linearity to your advantage and simply go do something else and return when you're stronger.
The checkpoint system is similar to Dark Souls in that they're fairly far apart, replenish your health but also respawn all the enemies. Finding a bench in a new area gives a real sense of relief.
Personally I think its the single greatest metroidvania I've ever played. Its tough, but in a relatively fair way. It doesnt hand hold which does mean you feel a bit "in the dark" for the first hour or two, but I personally love that.

Shadow Warrior is a action packed single player that offers the best katana gameplay I experienced. Wang is the protagonist, a bodyguard of Zilla Enterprises, looking to collect parts of a sword and assemble it to create a very powerful weapon. Unravel the mystery of the demons who are invading the human world. The sirens who protect the sword from the demons, and the guardians who protect the sword pieces from being gathered.
The companion that follows you around is actually pretty amusing and the dynamic between him and Wang work well. Constantly making jabs at you throughout the game really adds humor that actually works with the game rather than against since it doesn’t feel out of place. An example of this is on chapter 12, you teleport into a new area, nearly fell off the mountain and lived by grasping onto a broken bridge.
Wang: You suck!
Wang: Do you enjoy dropping me like that?
Companion: Just trying to land you in the air, it beats materializing a couple of feet underground
Wang: Your logic is sound
The katana and powers are far more effective against enemies than guns except in some instances where having distance between you and a mini-boss is beneficial. Guns are mostly used for bosses even though they could be used for interesting combos to get a higher score during fights for more karma and better position in the leaderboard. I highly recommend using the crossbow, rocket launcher, and shotgun throughout the game.
Be constantly on the move or you are going to take quite a bit of damage. The game has enough enemy variations and threats to make you constantly have to be on the move to avoid being hit.
The jumping in this game is pretty average which in case you're wondering means its bad. The dashing is far superior in this game which you will always use in combat since its far more effective for getting away from enemy attacks. The jumping I found was only useful when i used explosives near me to blow up groups of enemies i threw down when using the tiger skill. Overall movement in this game is a big step up from the previous game this engine was used for Hard Reset.
The level design itself is not as complex as others would like however there are many areas to explore which rewards you with money. There are also secrets that have a retro graphic theme style to it which pays tribute to the game the remake is based on. The only issue I have with the level design itself is that certain maps have elements which can be incredibly annoying like the platforming level where you can fall if you are not precise about where you jump.
The variety of enemies mixes up the gameplay and allows the player to come up with interesting ways to deal with multiple enemies at once or certain types that would otherwise kill you. What makes the enemies really stick out is their ability to rage. Their rage ability makes them go much faster and hit for more which means you need to either take them out fast or calm them down before they strike you down.
People tend to use the Divider of Heaven for most enemies seeing as how you can kill enemies in a row with its  piercing effects while being in constant movement.
The bosses are towering impressive looking monsters of death with nice animations and environments that you fight them in. Ultimately the bosses feel boring as a result of their ability to regenerate armor back on the weakness spots exposed. It really becomes a chore to constantly take down the armor off bosses just to hit the crystal which has a iffy hitbox.
Heroic mode offered a great challenge of having to clear a whole level without dying once, or you would be reset to the start of that level. It was quite hard at times considering that the staircases could kill you if you dashed down them too fast. The chapter 12 was particularly bad since there were many gimmicks like limiting your vision and spamming tons of suicidal monsters to attempt to kill you while you were limited in movement since you were stuck on a train.
If you are a fan of games that are like quake,painkiller,serious sam, look no further for another dose of crazy action just don't expect the bosses to be climatic...
