VIDEO VERSION:
INTRO:
From Stunlock, the creators of Bloodline Champions, one of my teenagehood games next to League of Legends and World Of Warcraft, comes an Arena based PvP game with fast-paced combat, well-designed champions and a mix of what we most love of the best games out today.
Battlerite comes as a new promise that has already conquered passionate fans among all kinds of communities. From comparing it to World Of Warcraft’s famous Arena system, it has already hooked many that were looking for a similar experience. But does it really pay off as such? Let’s take a look first.
CHARACTERS:
From being an Early Access game, BattleRite initiates with a quite big variety of characters. 15 different champions divided in 3 different roles: Melee, Ranged and Support. These champions can be EVEN separated by its own mechanics, Ranged characters can go from Archers to Casters, Melee from Tanks to Assassins and Supports can go even further, from Melee, Archers and Casters! Which means that mastering a role, isn’t going to pay off for all heroes! AMAZING!.. What? It’s not something new to you?
Oh, so what if you add into this mix a Talent Tree system for each round of the match? That means that countering an opponent is not just picking the right composition but also choosing wisely the buffs that you want to apply on your own abilities! Talents, or what they call “Battlerites”, will appear in front of you every round, right at the beginning. Champions can choose up to 3 talents and every round is a different talent, similar to Heroes Of The Storm talents system, but instead of in-match leveling it is earned every round. The first round talents will differ from the second, and up until fifth round, where you choose up to 2 talents to power up your ultimate ability. Overall, characters can be built into more aggressive, defensive or even mobility depending on each encounter you face.
OH, and LET ME TELL YOU about these encounters!
GAMEPLAY:
I agree that comparing Battlerite’s Arena to World Of Warcraft is not a bad thing, but I believe it went beyond that point! As an experienced retired WoW player… cof cof- I know, I’m old. I’ve played on a daily basis it’s arena and it feels very nostalgic to play a game that reminds me of that, but it goes beyond my expectations when it brings talents into the middle of the match!
It’s also important to mention it’s MoBA camera, what we could call over the top point of view. Clearly for moba players it is easier to play that way, but it also affects how the combat works. Even though some WoW players were used to drag their camera away in a similar way, watching the whole battleground from above and being unable to see what is out of your line of sight, “fog of war”, changes the whole game, you have no option but to get used to it and appreciate this new way of battling.
Another interesting change for Moba and WAW players is the Aiming and Movement system. Basic Attacks, some abilities and ultimates are cast where your cursor is, like a OverTheTop-Shooter game. Which means that pointing and clicking won’t work if you are used to that like me! You might struggle, but it feels so well balanced with the pace of the combat that you will easily master in 2 to 3 AI matches. Considering the movement system, as a MoBA-like game, it might blow your mind. It follows FPS PC logic, you move your character with WASD keys! We all know it’s not something new, but it is a MUST for this fast-paced arena game. For some players, another mechanic to adjust.
JESSICA: BUT KHNOK WHAT IF THE ENEMY TEAM PICKS 2 HEALERS AND WE CAN’T FINISH THEM OFF! IS IT AN ENDLESS BATTLE?
Don’t be afraid little Jessica, BattleRite has everything planned with their Suddendeath system! Back when I played WoW, some arena matches could go up to 40 minutes! NO KIDDING, some compositions consisted of 2 tanks who could self-heal too much, 2 healers or even kiters who would kill you of boredom! But here, after 2 minutes of combat the arena enters a Suddendeath mode where a circular fog engulfs the whole arena! DELIGHTFUL!
SKINS, CHESTS & CURRENCY:
As expected from most games since the OUTSTANDING FEVER OF TEAM FORTRESS 2 HATS, this game has skins for every character and brings also special skins for their weapons. The best way to obtain those are by leveling your account, champions and doing quests. Wait… for those familiar with Overwatch and Heroes Of The Storm, Chests and Quests to earn something are their territory of BUSINESS! HOW DARE YOU, STUNLOCK! It’s fine! They implemented both systems in a way that only benefits it’s players. From doing quests you earn chests and from chests you get skins, weapons, poses and icons! The chests goes from Silver to Gold. Silver guarantees a Rare item out of it, and Gold guarantees a Epic drop.
Also, some people might ask if there are microtransactions on this game, and the answer is yes, but it works the same way as Overwatch, you can buy packs of Gold Chests. So, NO PAY 2 WIN strats here!
Battle Coins and Tokens can be earned by winning sequences of matches and getting duplicate items, also, like Heroes Of The Storm, you get bonuses from leveling your specific champion, which rewards you on mastering it.
CONCLUSION:
**Considering that I played this game for something close to 5 hours, and that I will definitely play hundreds of hours more with 1 to 2 friends. The 25 dollars equivalent of the time spent, is totally worth  compared to Battlerite’s 20 dollars price. **
In my opinion, Battlerite became a must on my steam the moment Stunlock recreated such beloved style of arena game and, by evolving it into its own original piece, they showed the world that a smaller studio, great ideas combined and an accessible price can ALSO develop a STEAM HIT!

## Brief overview
Dungeon Defenders is an excellent action/rpg/tower defense with multiple characters each with different abilities and playstyles. More characters are available as DLC, 4 of which are male or female counterparts to the initial 4 characters, the rest are unique however.
The core game is very enjoyable even without the additional dlc which mostly adds new levels to the end-game.
While certainly designed for co-op play the majority of the levels are possible with just 1 person, only into the very late game do the maps tend to become huge and the number of enemy spawn locations become many. Eventually, the hardest level you can complete on your own will not drop good enough gear for you to progress without purchasing gear from other players. This shouldn't be a problem when playing in co-op fortunately.
## Strange difficulty curve:
The difficulty curve and the difficulty options available are rather bizarre as a choice of easy/medium/hard is possible for the first couple of levels (insane is completely impossible for new players with new characters), then easy/medium start to become your only doable difficulties until you complete the campaign for your first time.
You should then be able to go through the levels again, doing insane difficulty for the first 1 or 2 levels and hard difficulty for the rest.
Once you've completed all the default campaign levels on hard, you should then be able to do the rest of the campaign on insane difficulty.
## Online/offline play
There are 3 main ways to play Dungeon Defenders, Ranked (online), Open (online) and Local (offline).
Local play functions basically identical to Open play, just with all multiplayer elements done locally.
Open and Local play allow you to play custom levels, custom mods, load and play somebody elses characters and basically do whatever you want within the game (you can cheat to your hearts content if you really want).
Ranked play is more restricted, attempting to hack is obviously not allowed and the pool of levels/items/characters/etc. is limited to what Trendy Entertainment has officially published to the mode. If you are intending to play through the game normally, I would strongly suggest that you start in Ranked mode as there is an option to export your ranked characters to Open/Local, but not the other way around.
## Hacker Problems and Super Late Game Balance
Unfortunately, despite Trendy Ent.'s best efforts and VAC, ranked play has been riddled with hackers modifying items and spawning vast quantities of mana (the game's currency) into the game, thus greatly inflating the prices of late game gear purchased from players.
Further adding to this, it's almost seemed to me that Trendy Ent. have either chosen to support hackers or have no understanding of difficulty curves. The newest and most difficult levels (which are almost all DLC) on their hardest difficulties (nightmare) are so ludicrously difficult in comparison to the previous levels that the only way it seems possible that these levels can be beaten is with gear that would usually be obtained from completing the level you are attempting to beat.
The way this has seemed to work for the majority of players is that they've been forced to purchase gear off of others to beat these levels. Gear that was most likely originally gained by hackers putting their received gear into player shops, allowing players who buy these items to complete the new level in question and distribute even more of this gear to other players.
## Conclusion
Dungeon defenders is a fantastic game and it's ugly features shouldn't ever concern the average player who has a group of friends to play with.
Playing without friends however can be a lot more frustrating, as you're either playing on your own, which is possible for the most part, but becomes practically impossible into the end-game without the help of gear from player owned shops, or you end up playing with a bunch of random people in a game where all loot drops (with the exception of that upon completing levels) are available for any player to pick up and deny the others of.

I have been playing Assassins Creed 4 for 11 hours now and here is what I have to say about the single player campaign.
The game is a 3rd person action adventure game just like the previous three before it. Developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.
Assassins Creed 4 has surprised me with how the game starts off. It begins with a good build up to your character and then you find yourself beached on a shore with a fellow sailor and then chasing after him.
When I first started playing the game I was very surprised on how it started off with pirating and adventuring. After a bit of playing the game started to feel like Assassins Creed with the climbing up a tall tower to sync you to your surroundings.
Eventually I got to get my own ship and sail the seas. Finding small little islands and other larger islands to explore for treasure chests, messages in bottles and treasure maps. You also get to chase after sea chanty songs for your crew to sing as your sailing. Other artifacts like Aztec monuments you climb and get to orientate a marker with your surrounding to find where the buried artifact will be is a cool idea in the game. This all makes this game a joy to play and a break away form the old flag hunting that is meaningless.
The game play is the same as previous Assassin Creed games with the climbing and combat style. I like that you can run up to a person and assassinate them, get into tavern fights to open the tavern up to you.
There are places in town when you first begin where you need to save some pirates from the authorities who later join you and are your crew on ship. You also get to save people adrift on the seas and they become crew members.
Once you upgrade your ship to include harpoons you will be able to go whaling and get that big white whale! Along with whaling you can go shark hunting as well.
Eventually you will get to a point in the game where you will get control of your own island and call it home. Upgrading it to provide a tavern, shop, ship repair store and an estate home as well.
This game was played with an Xbox360 controller and I can say that its really made to accommodate this type of game play. I appreciate it when developers make a game compatible with a controller.
I am very impressed with Assassins Creed IV Black Flag and happy that I picked up the Deluxe Gold Edition for $30 during the 2014 Summer Sale.
If your planning to buy this game or not sure if you want to play another Assassins Creed game I would recommend this game, check out the video below. Assassins Creed 4 is worth a play.

VIDEO VERSION:
INTRO:
From Stunlock, the creators of Bloodline Champions, one of my teenagehood games next to League of Legends and World Of Warcraft, comes an Arena based PvP game with fast-paced combat, well-designed champions and a mix of what we most love of the best games out today.
Battlerite comes as a new promise that has already conquered passionate fans among all kinds of communities. From comparing it to World Of Warcraft’s famous Arena system, it has already hooked many that were looking for a similar experience. But does it really pay off as such? Let’s take a look first.
CHARACTERS:
From being an Early Access game, BattleRite initiates with a quite big variety of characters. 15 different champions divided in 3 different roles: Melee, Ranged and Support. These champions can be EVEN separated by its own mechanics, Ranged characters can go from Archers to Casters, Melee from Tanks to Assassins and Supports can go even further, from Melee, Archers and Casters! Which means that mastering a role, isn’t going to pay off for all heroes! AMAZING!.. What? It’s not something new to you?
Oh, so what if you add into this mix a Talent Tree system for each round of the match? That means that countering an opponent is not just picking the right composition but also choosing wisely the buffs that you want to apply on your own abilities! Talents, or what they call “Battlerites”, will appear in front of you every round, right at the beginning. Champions can choose up to 3 talents and every round is a different talent, similar to Heroes Of The Storm talents system, but instead of in-match leveling it is earned every round. The first round talents will differ from the second, and up until fifth round, where you choose up to 2 talents to power up your ultimate ability. Overall, characters can be built into more aggressive, defensive or even mobility depending on each encounter you face.
OH, and LET ME TELL YOU about these encounters!
GAMEPLAY:
I agree that comparing Battlerite’s Arena to World Of Warcraft is not a bad thing, but I believe it went beyond that point! As an experienced retired WoW player… cof cof- I know, I’m old. I’ve played on a daily basis it’s arena and it feels very nostalgic to play a game that reminds me of that, but it goes beyond my expectations when it brings talents into the middle of the match!
It’s also important to mention it’s MoBA camera, what we could call over the top point of view. Clearly for moba players it is easier to play that way, but it also affects how the combat works. Even though some WoW players were used to drag their camera away in a similar way, watching the whole battleground from above and being unable to see what is out of your line of sight, “fog of war”, changes the whole game, you have no option but to get used to it and appreciate this new way of battling.
Another interesting change for Moba and WAW players is the Aiming and Movement system. Basic Attacks, some abilities and ultimates are cast where your cursor is, like a OverTheTop-Shooter game. Which means that pointing and clicking won’t work if you are used to that like me! You might struggle, but it feels so well balanced with the pace of the combat that you will easily master in 2 to 3 AI matches. Considering the movement system, as a MoBA-like game, it might blow your mind. It follows FPS PC logic, you move your character with WASD keys! We all know it’s not something new, but it is a MUST for this fast-paced arena game. For some players, another mechanic to adjust.
JESSICA: BUT KHNOK WHAT IF THE ENEMY TEAM PICKS 2 HEALERS AND WE CAN’T FINISH THEM OFF! IS IT AN ENDLESS BATTLE?
Don’t be afraid little Jessica, BattleRite has everything planned with their Suddendeath system! Back when I played WoW, some arena matches could go up to 40 minutes! NO KIDDING, some compositions consisted of 2 tanks who could self-heal too much, 2 healers or even kiters who would kill you of boredom! But here, after 2 minutes of combat the arena enters a Suddendeath mode where a circular fog engulfs the whole arena! DELIGHTFUL!
SKINS, CHESTS & CURRENCY:
As expected from most games since the OUTSTANDING FEVER OF TEAM FORTRESS 2 HATS, this game has skins for every character and brings also special skins for their weapons. The best way to obtain those are by leveling your account, champions and doing quests. Wait… for those familiar with Overwatch and Heroes Of The Storm, Chests and Quests to earn something are their territory of BUSINESS! HOW DARE YOU, STUNLOCK! It’s fine! They implemented both systems in a way that only benefits it’s players. From doing quests you earn chests and from chests you get skins, weapons, poses and icons! The chests goes from Silver to Gold. Silver guarantees a Rare item out of it, and Gold guarantees a Epic drop.
Also, some people might ask if there are microtransactions on this game, and the answer is yes, but it works the same way as Overwatch, you can buy packs of Gold Chests. So, NO PAY 2 WIN strats here!
Battle Coins and Tokens can be earned by winning sequences of matches and getting duplicate items, also, like Heroes Of The Storm, you get bonuses from leveling your specific champion, which rewards you on mastering it.
CONCLUSION:
**Considering that I played this game for something close to 5 hours, and that I will definitely play hundreds of hours more with 1 to 2 friends. The 25 dollars equivalent of the time spent, is totally worth  compared to Battlerite’s 20 dollars price. **
In my opinion, Battlerite became a must on my steam the moment Stunlock recreated such beloved style of arena game and, by evolving it into its own original piece, they showed the world that a smaller studio, great ideas combined and an accessible price can ALSO develop a STEAM HIT!

Battlerite is fun. It is a simple game in concept: a brawler in which only skill matters. And yet, the gameplay is perfect, fast, demanding and enjoyable.
About skill.
There are 5 basic skills that works with cooldowns. Two of these skills have a enhanced or alternative version you can use spending energy. Then you got an special skill you can use with energy and an ultimate.
So, each character have up to 9 skills. The ammount doesn't make the game impossible for new players, you can do fairly well with the basic till you got  mapped all the skills in your brain. But due the many skills you have there are plenty of strategies to consider. And the decisions have to be made in less that a second.
Battlerite has a very newbie friendly skill floor, but then it goes up and up and up, because of taht the more hardcore gamers will find there is a lot of resources to make great players shine.
Battlerites
Battlerites are very much like buffs you get in a moba when you level up, but they are tied to rounds. I like this aspect because it makes each round a little different from the previous one. Powers act in a different way and some combos ans strategies can suddenly appear.
Aesthetic
Battlerite has a great character design. I am not very fond of the look of the characters when i see the profiles, or when i see a picture on Internet. It seems to me too simple, too cartoonish. But here is the thing, when you put those models in the arena, when you are playing, they look great. It is an scale thing.

At first I really liked the game. It's atmospheric, the music is nice, the graphics are great. But over time it stopped being fun but became a rather frustrating experience. The reason being bosses that are (nearly) impossible to kill. Some of them very well crossed the line to unfairness for me. There's a difference between a challenge and needing luck that the boss won't choose the destination you're in at the moment to make you beat him. Plus, there doesn't seem to be any clues about which boss is essential and which isn't. And sometimes you have to cross difficult sections from the save-points to the boss, which minimizes your chances to beat it even further. All that adds to frustrating gameplay.
So if you're happy with wasting hours trying to beat some guy that may or may not be necessary for getting further in the game, you may like it. Otherwise, stay away from it.

Absolutely one of the best metroidvanias ever. Up there with Sympony of the Night and Super Metroid as one of the most expertly crafted side scrollers of all time. The world is enormous with a plethora of secrets to find along the way. The visuals are astounding, the soundtrack is haunting and beautiful, there are over 30 unique bosses to be discovered, and the combat is swift and invigorating throughout. The amount of side content that may never seen by many is staggering. It is evident that this game was an absolute labor of love by Team Cherry.
Rarely do I immediately hop back into a game after completing it, but I ended up spending an additional 10 hours finding secrets and unlocking achievements, simply because I couldn't leave the world behind. It grabbed me in the first few minutes and had me for close to 40 hours. It's that good!
Three additional notes.
First. The game is compared to Ori and the Blind Forest a lot. Do not let this comparison prevent you from diving into the world of Hollow Knight. There are so many more bosses, secrets, and unorthodox level design scenarios to be marveled over. It's a shame the two are being compared to one another. While I loved Ori, I think this game stands head and shoulders above it.
Second. Yes there is a lot of backtracking. BUT! Once you've unlocked most of the map, most areas can be accessed within 2 - 3 minutes. Backtracking is a staple in games like these and continually invites the player to explore every nook and cranny in this beautiful world. Not sure why so many write this off as a negative for the game - it felt right at home in this genre of game.
Third. There is a performance glitch that will temporarily lock the game from time to time. It does happen, but it's never for more than a second and rarely happens in the middle of combat or platforming. Don't let other reviews convince you that the games' not worth playing because of it. It's just a minor imperfection.

I love this game.  I really do.  But at this time I cannot recommend it.
Look up reports about the game freezing on actions like hitting an enemy, entering water, etc.  There are tons of them.  Some were resolved when the devs pushed out a specific update, but a lot of people are still having problems.
My system is MORE than qualified to handle this game, and I've done everything I can--made sure physx was running on my NVdia GTX 960M, made sure Hollow Knight was running on my graphics card and not my integrated, tried -noheap for launch options, turned off v-sync, verified game integrity, set my intel/windows graphics options to maximum performance, etc.
None of it works.  No matter what I do, I get tiny little lag stutters when I hit an enemy, break certain pieces of background, get hit, or do certain jumps.  This results in me falling into acid pits I should have never been near, getting combod or hit when I wouldn't have in the first place normally, and all around getting frustrated.
If not for this, the game would be damn near perfect in my book.  It's fantastic.  I like metroidvanias so I don't mind the backtracking one bit.
It's fun, has a good progression, a sense of wonder and explanation, a great art and music identity, and feels alive.  I just can't recommend it until the devs fix a 2D game stuttering on systems that can handle much more graphically intense games.
If they fix this, I'd be happy to recommend it.

Battlerite is good. Really good. Of course, I would say that, given Bloodline Champions was my favorite game, ever. If you want a fast-paced multiplayer battling game, Battlerite is for you. Tired of forty-minute-long matches that are decided at the twenty minute mark? Tired of last-hitting minions for ten minutes? Tired of squabbling over farm and kills with your teammates? Well, Battlerite's for you. This game is played in short rounds. (1-2 minutes.) You will play best of five rounds. So even a whole match is much shorter than a game of your favorite MOBA. Also, the two game formats are 2v2 and 3v3, so it's easy to put together a team. Because the game is divided into rounds, if your team makes horrible mistakes, instead of sitting there for twenty minutes suffering, you can just figure out what you did wrong, then go and win the next round. Also, instead of an overall slow pace but with moments that are almost too fast to follow, Battlerite has a relenetlessly quick pace.
Really, though, the reason to like Bloodline Champions is how the core gameplay works. You move with WASD and aim all your abilities. Because of this, there are a lot of mind games. You have to guess where your opponent will be a fraction of a second from now. Also, there are lots of counter moves, intensifying the need to predict your opponents. In this game, you can't just get in range and land guaranteed damage. It's much more fighting game-like than those games where you right click your opponent. If you want a game that's really action-y, this game is for you. If you just want to battle, this game is for you. If you want a game full of depth and subtlety and room to grow as a player, this game is for you.

The first enemy miniboss introduced is the Ogre, noted for its brutish form and high hp. He was not of much difficulty, but when web-shooting spiders began falling from the sky while buffed mages shot fireballs around my head as I jumped over a kamikaze kobold that nearly 1hit k/o'd me, I knew I had gotten somewhere in the game. Thankfully, my heal aura fills my hp in 5 seconds flat. Good thing the game allows you to employ all of your characters in a single game!
The updates bring endless new content, and I was lucky enough to recieve this copy as a gift including them all. I perosnally enjoy playing them all. All it takes to beat them is better gear. Once you have the strategy down, all the maps play out the same, but watch out! A single goblin might eek by your defenses unless you keep a watchful eye, oneshotting your crystal on the hardest difficulties..
If that's not good enough, go figure that it lets you host your own shops in an intuitive manner that facilitates real economic activity and sets price standards for stable economic interaction as well. The online play is fundamentally necessary to beat difficult maps and challenges. It is crucial to have a compotent partner with good communication to beat the game, which is something I like personally to see. Dungeon Defenders 2 gets an A+ by my standards in terms of multiplayer features, weapon generation functions, and game progression.

I held off buying Black Flag for quite a while because I was dissappointed with how little the series and game mechanics  were progressing with each game (Brotherhood, Revelations and III were the most 'meh' in my eyes) but Black Flag honestly surprised me.
Good Points:
Much better as a free-roam game than the last few, you can sail anywhere - discovering and exploring random islands you spot inbetween.
Tools and weapons - even though the weapon variety is lacking (no dagger), there is some nice new features, such as a sleep dart, 2-4 pistols carried at once and also dagger, when picked up, will now a throwing knife (one which actually kills most targets first hit, for once)
Edward - the main character is a far more likeable Kenway than Connor or Haytham, who isn't as naive or annoying as Connor but not as pretentious as Haytham. He's quite down to earth but also has questionable morals - but you can see glimpses of a better man underneath. He's more interesting because he's not as gleefully serving to the Assassin's as the other protagonists in the series, and actually develops as a person over the course of the game.
Bad Points:
More bugs than an ant farm - AC III was pretty buggy (falling under docks, dyed clothes not appearing in cutscenes) but Black Flag has some spectacular bugs. Kenway's ship is notorious for bugs (just look up the Acsension of the Jackdaw) and happens quite often (I've had the acension bug and one when I kept falling through the ship,, alongside my crew mates, on my first play through). Other annoying bugs exist as well: I personally dislike the bug where characters' eyes are often shaded in red, blue, yellow, etc, all over the whites of the eyes and the pupils, in pretty much every cutscene.
Keyboards are for losers - this game, as a terrible PC port, is havoc to play with keyboard controls. While I got used to it, initially, it became more and more irritating - especially in one big stealth mission near the end of the game where I had stealthed through most of the fort and tried to synchronise on a tower.... I thought I needed to get on top of this little bit sticking out the top and pressed Shift + Space to get on top, only for th game to decide I probably wanted to jump off the tower to my death instead..... -.- the replays of that mission were plagued with similar issues as well - I attempted to air assassinate my target, who was in range and I was pointing at them (plus they were highlighted) and instead Edward assassinated some random guard far to the right of him (i was at a slight angle, and WASD keys seem to decide who you assassinate rather than the mouse) There are other little issues with the freerunning that wil just infuriate you if you use a keyboard so for your own sanity: use a Xbox 360 controller - I've also struggled to set up non-X360 controllers with it and the buttons have been all muddled up :(

Hollow Knight is a fantastic game.
This is a game that perfectly executes style, gameplay and even soundtrack to fit a theme.
This game is strangely peaceful, a world that you can truly get lost in. The level design allows the player to seemingly explore aimlessly, while having purposeful and well designed areas, all of which go towards the goal.
What is especially impressive is the progression, as at first the player simply loses themselves exploring game mechanics and enjoying the well-tailored level design, before giving them a more focussed challenge as they progress with the storyline, discovering new areas and abilities, never failing to provide new content, while gradually allowing the player to complete previous areas in a COMPLETELY new way, due to some new ability, such as the dash.
The level design is amazing, the incredible amount of detail and extra interest added to such a simple concept is impressive, for example the background aethsetics that the player can interact with, to no consequence. The characters are simple and charming, and reasurring.  Visuals build a mysterious but darkly picturesque world for the player to explore, with astounding variation in look and feel considering the setting. The layout of enemies, use of soundtrack and simply the location of platforms masterfully contribute to the overall atmoshpere of each section, which is probably my favourite aspect of the game.
Gameplay is satisying, simple but very effective combat systems built upon throughout, all based on a good, reasonably imaginative core game mechanic. The game life is also seemingly extensive, as there always seems to be another huge challenge to overcome. It is appropriately challenging, with a large range of difficulty in terms of area, which contributes, as I said before, to the overall atmosphere of the area.
Any cons worth mentioning are the inevitable sections of walking far back to an area after death, but the length of this increases as the stakes do, as areas become harder, making the game's overall journey hard but certainly worthwhile. Revisting areas is also neccessary to see all the secrets the world has to offer, however the gameplay changes so much due to the addition of new abilities that it is like playing it for the first time.
I highly reccomend this game.

edit:
since i think this game got overlooked and it deserves more attention heres a more in depth review of the game:
great controls, the bright one's controls are on point. its never the game fault if you fail. i failed a lot because rushing things, being sloppy, not being concentrated but never because the game felt floaty!
controls are tight af
great musik, very moody, very fitting, never sticks out too much, reminded me in a good way of other soundtracks
nice graphics, its a 2D jump and fight and thus the backgrounds are very detailed and create a great atmosphere. sometimes it is hard to distiguish between foreground/background and actual platforms but up till now i had that problem maybe 2 or 3 times in 25h of playtime. so its negligible... although it is a very big game it never feels empty, theres always a lot of stuff around to smash and lots of secrets to discover. and i love the look of the enemies (very cuphead'ish)!
great map that gets updated slowly but surely by buying pins from the vendor, cleverly done!
progression is very tangible, you constantly find new stuff, learn new abilities and get new charms. and the charms are actually worth looking at and changing them out from time to time, maybe for a boss fight, maybe because you are short on money etc.
combat is very interesting, there are a lot of different enemies with very distinct attack patterns. so you have to 'learn' each enemy individually if you want to avoid taking lots and lots of damage. this is especially true for the boss fights that are a challenge but never felt unfair up to now (havent finished the game yet).
save points are fair but sometimes can feel a bit too far apart, most of the time thats because you havent explored all of the map (after finding and buying the map from the cartographer in each new section).
the platforming never felt boring or 'samey' nor did it feel obstructive or artificial. it gets more and more complex as you get more abilities but since the controls are very tight i get around the place very well - but it stays challenging!

Or how about trying to defend a Portal in a Town that is slowly being flooded while you have to solve riddles to lower the water levels ? All that and much more is waiting in this game.
This pretty much sums it up so far, again, I can highly reccomend this game. It's extremely addicting, has a cute graphic style, an amazing soundtrack and lots of replayability... and the added Steam Workshop feature only adds to the latter!

The most impressive thing about Hollow Knight is the incredible design and thought that has gone into it. I have never before played a game were every thing seems so well thought out in its design.
This is a 2D platformer all about the exploration, you have a map (that you need to buy) that you can update while playing. Normally this is were 2D platformers choose either a) no map or b) a map. The drawback of no map is obvious, no way of keeping track of where you have been or where you are. The drawback of having a map is that you can keep checking it to see if you have missed something. You enter a room, instead of exploring it you can check your map to see how many exits it has so you don't miss anything. The map in Hollow Knight doesn't update until you are in a resting area, its just a small detail but it really effects the gameplay a lot. When exploring new areas you can never look at the map because it hasn't been written yet. When you rest it gets updated, hella clever.
There are tons of seemingly small design decisions throughout this game that comes togehter to make a spectacular game.

This is an interesting little british-comedy first person perspective game with exceptionally simple controls and over 18 possible endings. The script writers for the narrator also appear to have thought of witty responses to almost everything you might decide to do in this short game. While mostly funny and thoughtful this game can get unexpectedly creepy at times as you wander around the empty labyrinthine office building complex which is what this game's environment largely consists of. This game may be taken many different ways (indeed each ending consists of a slightly different interpretation of what this game is) though overall this game is essentially a thought experiment into the nature of linear games (Half Life 2, and Portal are good examples of what I mean by "Linear") and the "choices" or non-option options which such games tend to give you. The game does have several weaknesses though, foremost among them is that it becomes repetitive quickly even with the quirky british humor and witty narration. From a purely intellectual standpoint this game is Part Matrix Reloaded, part Stranger than Fiction, part Choose Your Own Adventure book and part Run Lola Run and yet not any of these either. This game portrays a deep set dissatisfaction with games which force you on a very linear path and which do not let you choose (or affect) the ending in any more than a very minor way illustrating that something else (or at least a lot more endings than just the 1 to 3 which most games have designed into them these days) is very, very possible to create. If you have a lot of trouble learning or handling FPS controls then this game is a perfect game to use to learn the fundamentals. There is nothing to shoot and there are no enemies (other than the narrator whom you will never meet).
Go home, Heroes of the Storm.

It's not a game.  It's video irony, and the joke is on you for playing.
This is the story of Stanley, who witnessed the end of video games and didn't know what to do with himself.  Mostly he heard a disembodied voice in his head telling him what to do.  And mostly, Stanley died in a number of unfortunate ways.  Even when he lived, he basically died.  Since he just returned to that point in time where there were no more video games.
And you, the gamer, are an even bigger loser than Stanley is.  Why?  Because Stanley is the result of a creative process... an intellectual activity that crafted irony from nothing and breathed life into it with controls, graphics, and a story of some sort.  You just occupy Stanley's body, drag him around uselessly up one cooridor and down another, all toward certain death.  And when you get to one of the end conditions, you post about it on Facebook.  But really, you are just pushing buttons at the mercy of someone else's creativity.   Oh, and you paid actual money for this.  Money that you probably earned actually doing something creative and interesting; something that added value for other people.  Or maybe your mom gave you the money.   And she did something creative and valuable to earn it.  But you are just going to sit listlessly at your desk, pushing buttons the narrator tells you to push.  Or the ones he doesn't tell you to push.  And none of it matters one bit.  Not at all.
Loved this game.... it is literature and social commentary turned into a video game.  Bravo!

TLDR:
If you like the team fights of MOBAs, or WoW arenas - but don't like the grinding to get there: You will probably like this game.
~~~~~~~~~~
2v2/3v3 team-based twin-stick skill-shot fantasy-themed arena combat.
Payment Model:
Currently all characters are unlocked, and there is no equipment, levels, or other boosting methods.
A fresh account has the exact same combat ability of a verteran.
Purchases bring cosmetic items, and there is a founders DLC that gives +10% xp to you and your party - but levels only reward cosmetics anyway.
The game is going free to play, and if they stick with this shop model - they're off to a good start.
Gameplay:
Combat is fast paced, 100% skillshot.
Players are placed at opposite ends of a mirror arena, best of 5 rounds wins.
Between rounds, each player is offered an upgrade - that puts a different spin on an existing skill.
These modifications are chosen from a predetermined pool per character per round - increasing in power as the rounds go on.
These can offer more uses, extra effects, more damage, etc. This allows players to customise their character to their playstyle - with an extra skill in choosing modifications that counter your opponents.
There's more active abilities than the average MOBA, with each character having at least 7 skills. Some are on cooldown, some consume charge generated by using other abilities.
Beware if your internet isn't great, or you live in a remote area - since even small amounts of latency will cost you matches. (Rejoice Australians, there are AUS servers!)
Progression:
Since combat is skill-based, there's a high skill ceiling to each character, with use of skills and positioning being crucial to success.
In early access, no characters are unlocked over time, but cosmetic items are earned by leveling characters and completing daily missions (to use characters from certain pools).
There's no gear treadmill to grind here.
Story:
Nearly non-existant, giving only short backstories on characters, no single player campaign.
Graphics:
A high fantasy art style, combat animations are clear in purpose.
The top down shooter view means you rarely get a close look at the models, but they are good enough.
Sound:
Music is enough to get the point across without being distracting, and the sound design doesn't have any jarring misses.

Absolutely one of the best metroidvanias ever. Up there with Sympony of the Night and Super Metroid as one of the most expertly crafted side scrollers of all time. The world is enormous with a plethora of secrets to find along the way. The visuals are astounding, the soundtrack is haunting and beautiful, there are over 30 unique bosses to be discovered, and the combat is swift and invigorating throughout. The amount of side content that may never seen by many is staggering. It is evident that this game was an absolute labor of love by Team Cherry.
Rarely do I immediately hop back into a game after completing it, but I ended up spending an additional 10 hours finding secrets and unlocking achievements, simply because I couldn't leave the world behind. It grabbed me in the first few minutes and had me for close to 40 hours. It's that good!
Three additional notes.
First. The game is compared to Ori and the Blind Forest a lot. Do not let this comparison prevent you from diving into the world of Hollow Knight. There are so many more bosses, secrets, and unorthodox level design scenarios to be marveled over. It's a shame the two are being compared to one another. While I loved Ori, I think this game stands head and shoulders above it.
Second. Yes there is a lot of backtracking. BUT! Once you've unlocked most of the map, most areas can be accessed within 2 - 3 minutes. Backtracking is a staple in games like these and continually invites the player to explore every nook and cranny in this beautiful world. Not sure why so many write this off as a negative for the game - it felt right at home in this genre of game.
Third. There is a performance glitch that will temporarily lock the game from time to time. It does happen, but it's never for more than a second and rarely happens in the middle of combat or platforming. Don't let other reviews convince you that the games' not worth playing because of it. It's just a minor imperfection.

As a long time Assassins' Creed player, it saddens me knowing that the series is probably going downhill from this point on. Such is the difficulty and struggle with holding on to a series and hopes of managing in making a successful sequel. It's the same problem I notice in the latest Batman series, Arkham Origin. On one hand, the developers want to maintain the blend of stealth and combat, on the other hand, they want to add new gadget for our hero, new toys to the sandbox. And neither Arkham Origin nor AC4: Black Flag handle this adequtely. The problem with AC4: Black Flag is that it has reached critical mass in terms of content and bug. The graphics are really nice, but what isn't these days. The music is there, but even though I'm writing this review less than an hour after just finishing the game, I'm already drawing a blank. However, my biggest issue isn't with the graphics or soundtrack so I'll leave them at that.
Traditionally, Assassin's Creed is kind of like the Hitman series in which the game encourages you to silently approach your target and then disposing them as quietly as possible, you can charge in and stab your target with a sword, but you'll have to spend a lot of time fighting guards in and out. Firearms and rope dart was added later on, both are fairly noticeable and doesn't effect the stealth mechanics. When they added the blow dart, specifically the berserker darts, that's when the stealth falls apart. Once you acquired  berserker darts, the game might as well just jump straight to the ending cutscene because for the rest of the game (except one short section where the game took away all your weapons and tools except your hidden blade) will consist of you shooting your target with a berserker dart and leave. And maybe perhaps the developers suspect that the player might resort to range weapon so that they added a optional objective to "air assasinate" just about every single one of your target. SERIOUSLY DEVS!? almost every single one of the templar must be air assasinate for full synchronization? did the Devs write down ideas for optional objective after a binge drinking contest? Can't the Devs at least pretend to be creative and added a few assassinate from crowd or with firearms just to add a little flavour to the game? The worst offender of them all is the "Kenway's fleet" part of the game in which you must sit through an automated simulation again and again to clear a shipping route in order to safely makes a profit (or more importantly unlock other city and collectables). If I wanted a game in which the game can do all the playing by itself, I'll go play on of those farming games on Facebook. Making the whole automated process unskippable should be a capital offense punishable by death. Why would some people believe that making the game earn fictional resources while you're not playing it is a good idea!? Wouldn't it be simpler to reduces the prices on in game goods to the point that people can grind for moderate ammount to buy those in game item?
As mentioned earlier, while some game may have too few content, I think Black Flag have too many, the Pirate plundering sounds fun at first, but quicky grows old and become tedious. Like a stack of paper work on the inbox waiting to be sorted. And for those completionist who wanted to finish upgrading their ship, that'll take a lot of repetitive plundering, ship or warehouse. The ship raiding is always an all out battle which ties back to my previous point in regards to how the new element wercks the stealth in AC4. And the underwater wreckage idea sounds interesting on paper until you realizes that navigating is a pain because you don't have the command to swim down which means your only option is to aim your camera downward in order to swim down; that wouldn't be such a problem if the camera angle is done from a first person perspective, because while you're going through confined spaces such as the interior of the ship or a narrow tunnel the camera have this curious tendency to swing around and find the most uncomfortable angle for you to work with. A particular scene came to mind when I'm going through a under water current segment where the camera decided to swing around 180 degrees to my front, away from the obstable that's in front of me. And lastly, I didn't know I will miss the red cross indicating that you've breached the optional objective, but I really misses it now. Having a red X telling you that optional objective is lost helps me keep track of what I need to accomplish. I see no reason to change that already working system but the Devs do it anyway. Even though all of this is nothing more than a tiny annoyance but it's annoyance like this that build up over time.
This next complaint is the killer, it's what got me reconsidered in following the series. Assassin's Creed has been a long running series, not in terms of years but in terms of releases. At least 6 major releases and another half dozens or so small releases bringing the total to at least a dozen or so associated title. At this point there shouldn't be any major bugs in the game but AC4: Black Flag has really slipped up as far as debugging goes. At least twice thoughout my playthrough the game forgot to spawn my target (once during the capture of the cove/Man of War, another during the naval battle of Hornigold where the game should have transition to the island), which is game breaking. Several other times I've also notices that the game failed to spawn in ships leaving a rather parculiar void in the water. There are at least two bug that I've notices which ruins stealth, one in which the guard will for no warning or reason suddenly becomes  hostile toward you while you're hiding in the bushes; the guards isn't alerted or searching in the bushes, they just suddenly turned on you while you're trying to sneak up on them from a bushes behind them. Secondly, there is this weird teleportation bug in which trying to shoot a guard from a distant may sometimes trigger a assasinate target on ground sequence (the one where the player kicks a target that's on the floor) and teleports the player instantly to a neutralized guard on the floor, thus exposing the player and ruined the stealth. Occasionally a deseased guard will resurrect on the spot with slightly paler complextion (like the palette when a player blends in with the crowd), this is more evident in AC4's DLC Freedom Cry.
Last but not least, the writing, specifically the wording for certain optional mission objective where the game listed "don't kill anyone" but what the game really means is "don't harm anyone" because even silently disarming a guard from behind will lose the optional objective. And several of the dialogue feels like it was written by a six year old. It's like the developers decided to save money on hiring a writter and just go with whatever conversation they can gather from their kids or something.
Assassin's Creed 4 could be a good game. The sandbox is just as pretty as the critics said it is. Traversing the Caribbean and the jungle really feels like a treat, it's as if I'm in the Caribbean bathing under the sun and swimming in the caressing ocrean wave with the ocrean breeze in my face and not in a souless concrete forest. But the Developers are clearing rushing their deadline, and as a result their quality suffers tremendously. Unbalanced gameplay, numerous bugs are all testament of that. So
For anyone else who's interested in sandbox or pirates, unless you got money, you should wait for a sale. Cause personally I don't see 40 ~ 60 dollars worth in this game.

Hollow Knight is a fantastic game.
This is a game that perfectly executes style, gameplay and even soundtrack to fit a theme.
This game is strangely peaceful, a world that you can truly get lost in. The level design allows the player to seemingly explore aimlessly, while having purposeful and well designed areas, all of which go towards the goal.
What is especially impressive is the progression, as at first the player simply loses themselves exploring game mechanics and enjoying the well-tailored level design, before giving them a more focussed challenge as they progress with the storyline, discovering new areas and abilities, never failing to provide new content, while gradually allowing the player to complete previous areas in a COMPLETELY new way, due to some new ability, such as the dash.
The level design is amazing, the incredible amount of detail and extra interest added to such a simple concept is impressive, for example the background aethsetics that the player can interact with, to no consequence. The characters are simple and charming, and reasurring.  Visuals build a mysterious but darkly picturesque world for the player to explore, with astounding variation in look and feel considering the setting. The layout of enemies, use of soundtrack and simply the location of platforms masterfully contribute to the overall atmoshpere of each section, which is probably my favourite aspect of the game.
Gameplay is satisying, simple but very effective combat systems built upon throughout, all based on a good, reasonably imaginative core game mechanic. The game life is also seemingly extensive, as there always seems to be another huge challenge to overcome. It is appropriately challenging, with a large range of difficulty in terms of area, which contributes, as I said before, to the overall atmosphere of the area.
Any cons worth mentioning are the inevitable sections of walking far back to an area after death, but the length of this increases as the stakes do, as areas become harder, making the game's overall journey hard but certainly worthwhile. Revisting areas is also neccessary to see all the secrets the world has to offer, however the gameplay changes so much due to the addition of new abilities that it is like playing it for the first time.
I highly reccomend this game.

It's not a game.  It's video irony, and the joke is on you for playing.
This is the story of Stanley, who witnessed the end of video games and didn't know what to do with himself.  Mostly he heard a disembodied voice in his head telling him what to do.  And mostly, Stanley died in a number of unfortunate ways.  Even when he lived, he basically died.  Since he just returned to that point in time where there were no more video games.
And you, the gamer, are an even bigger loser than Stanley is.  Why?  Because Stanley is the result of a creative process... an intellectual activity that crafted irony from nothing and breathed life into it with controls, graphics, and a story of some sort.  You just occupy Stanley's body, drag him around uselessly up one cooridor and down another, all toward certain death.  And when you get to one of the end conditions, you post about it on Facebook.  But really, you are just pushing buttons at the mercy of someone else's creativity.   Oh, and you paid actual money for this.  Money that you probably earned actually doing something creative and interesting; something that added value for other people.  Or maybe your mom gave you the money.   And she did something creative and valuable to earn it.  But you are just going to sit listlessly at your desk, pushing buttons the narrator tells you to push.  Or the ones he doesn't tell you to push.  And none of it matters one bit.  Not at all.
Loved this game.... it is literature and social commentary turned into a video game.  Bravo!

great map that gets updated slowly but surely by buying pins from the vendor, cleverly done!
progression is very tangible, you constantly find new stuff, learn new abilities and get new charms. and the charms are actually worth looking at and changing them out from time to time, maybe for a boss fight, maybe because you are short on money etc.
combat is very interesting, there are a lot of different enemies with very distinct attack patterns. so you have to 'learn' each enemy individually if you want to avoid taking lots and lots of damage. this is especially true for the boss fights that are a challenge but never felt unfair up to now (havent finished the game yet).
save points are fair but sometimes can feel a bit too far apart, most of the time thats because you havent explored all of the map (after finding and buying the map from the cartographer in each new section).
the platforming never felt boring or 'samey' nor did it feel obstructive or artificial. it gets more and more complex as you get more abilities but since the controls are very tight i get around the place very well - but it stays challenging!
playtime can be as high as 40h and this seems to be true since i am 25h in and it feels like i am a little over half way through the game atm.
in conclusion the game feels like a complete package, very very well crafted! it is a true metroidvania in the sense that you need different abilities to progress different stages of the game (and NOT in the sense: red shot -> opens red door). but in the same way the game never holds your hands or tells you what to do or where to go next. this can sometimes be a little frustrating but starting the game the next day i always found a new area i havent been to very quickly. so its more a 'blinded by the options' instead of a 'nowhere to go'...
as in what this game promises and tries to be ill rate this a 10/10! i dont like 'perfect scores' and rarely see them making sense and maybe my rating is influenced by the fact that i have been promised a 'real' metroidvania experience too often and got disappointed...
but heck yeah, this is a very good game indeed!

Hollow Knight is a fantastic game.
This is a game that perfectly executes style, gameplay and even soundtrack to fit a theme.
This game is strangely peaceful, a world that you can truly get lost in. The level design allows the player to seemingly explore aimlessly, while having purposeful and well designed areas, all of which go towards the goal.
What is especially impressive is the progression, as at first the player simply loses themselves exploring game mechanics and enjoying the well-tailored level design, before giving them a more focussed challenge as they progress with the storyline, discovering new areas and abilities, never failing to provide new content, while gradually allowing the player to complete previous areas in a COMPLETELY new way, due to some new ability, such as the dash.
The level design is amazing, the incredible amount of detail and extra interest added to such a simple concept is impressive, for example the background aethsetics that the player can interact with, to no consequence. The characters are simple and charming, and reasurring.  Visuals build a mysterious but darkly picturesque world for the player to explore, with astounding variation in look and feel considering the setting. The layout of enemies, use of soundtrack and simply the location of platforms masterfully contribute to the overall atmoshpere of each section, which is probably my favourite aspect of the game.
Gameplay is satisying, simple but very effective combat systems built upon throughout, all based on a good, reasonably imaginative core game mechanic. The game life is also seemingly extensive, as there always seems to be another huge challenge to overcome. It is appropriately challenging, with a large range of difficulty in terms of area, which contributes, as I said before, to the overall atmosphere of the area.
Any cons worth mentioning are the inevitable sections of walking far back to an area after death, but the length of this increases as the stakes do, as areas become harder, making the game's overall journey hard but certainly worthwhile. Revisting areas is also neccessary to see all the secrets the world has to offer, however the gameplay changes so much due to the addition of new abilities that it is like playing it for the first time.
I highly reccomend this game.

*MY EARLY ACCESS/BETA REVIEW* Battlerite is in essence a moba, but don't think "Oh so it's like League of Legends/Dota?" No no no, it's more than that. It's some of the fastest most entertaining combat I've ever encountered (Besides Bloodline Champions of course which is the game this is based off of) The skill ceiling of this game is ridiculously high to the point where no two matches feel the same. The cast of characters is somewhat small as of now, yes but the devs are working to add more and it's exciting. To all of my friends or anyone who is thinking about buying into the early access, I'd say go for it. It was more than worth my money(Especially seeing as how the value of the early access pack is really high since you get all characters current and future.)
Edit: I normally don't write huge reviews but for this game I kind of have to so here we go.
This game is fantastic there's nothing else to really say that does it glory. The idea of the game is magnificent in the fact that it shows potential to be a great esport after some balance patches and etc. There's a reason the game wasn't released to the public as of yet. The game does need some polish. There's some strange bugs a not that great ranking system, no normal games and a whole slew of things that would turn so many people off right away. But don't let that stop you. The devs are constantly working and constantly listening to the complaints of the community to make a great game for everyone. The content seems boring at first sight (According to some people I've tried to show it to.) But it's quite interesting since the game never feels like the same game. After one round is completed you have a set of options that allow you to play the game with as much freedom as you want. The whole idea is to give players options that are all good and all useful. Plus the skill ceiling makes it all the better. You can play the game and constantly improve. Grasping the basics WILL be a little tough. You WILL hit into every counter. You WILL miss a lot. There's no saying you'll pick up this game and be a god at it instantly. But there's so much more to the game. Push through the frustration of sucking and a whole world is opened to you. combat is very interesting, there are a lot of different enemies with very distinct attack patterns. so you have to 'learn' each enemy individually if you want to avoid taking lots and lots of damage. this is especially true for the boss fights that are a challenge but never felt unfair up to now (havent finished the game yet).
save points are fair but sometimes can feel a bit too far apart, most of the time thats because you havent explored all of the map (after finding and buying the map from the cartographer in each new section).
the platforming never felt boring or 'samey' nor did it feel obstructive or artificial. it gets more and more complex as you get more abilities but since the controls are very tight i get around the place very well - but it stays challenging!
playtime can be as high as 40h and this seems to be true since i am 25h in and it feels like i am a little over half way through the game atm.
in conclusion the game feels like a complete package, very very well crafted! it is a true metroidvania in the sense that you need different abilities to progress different stages of the game (and NOT in the sense: red shot -> opens red door). but in the same way the game never holds your hands or tells you what to do or where to go next. this can sometimes be a little frustrating but starting the game the next day i always found a new area i havent been to very quickly. so its more a 'blinded by the options' instead of a 'nowhere to go'...
as in what this game promises and tries to be ill rate this a 10/10! i dont like 'perfect scores' and rarely see them making sense and maybe my rating is influenced by the fact that i have been promised a 'real' metroidvania experience too often and got disappointed...
but heck yeah, this is a very good game indeed!

Battlerite is good. Really good. Of course, I would say that, given Bloodline Champions was my favorite game, ever. If you want a fast-paced multiplayer battling game, Battlerite is for you. Tired of forty-minute-long matches that are decided at the twenty minute mark? Tired of last-hitting minions for ten minutes? Tired of squabbling over farm and kills with your teammates? Well, Battlerite's for you. This game is played in short rounds. (1-2 minutes.) You will play best of five rounds. So even a whole match is much shorter than a game of your favorite MOBA. Also, the two game formats are 2v2 and 3v3, so it's easy to put together a team. Because the game is divided into rounds, if your team makes horrible mistakes, instead of sitting there for twenty minutes suffering, you can just figure out what you did wrong, then go and win the next round. Also, instead of an overall slow pace but with moments that are almost too fast to follow, Battlerite has a relenetlessly quick pace.
Really, though, the reason to like Bloodline Champions is how the core gameplay works. You move with WASD and aim all your abilities. Because of this, there are a lot of mind games. You have to guess where your opponent will be a fraction of a second from now. Also, there are lots of counter moves, intensifying the need to predict your opponents. In this game, you can't just get in range and land guaranteed damage. It's much more fighting game-like than those games where you right click your opponent. If you want a game that's really action-y, this game is for you. If you just want to battle, this game is for you. If you want a game full of depth and subtlety and room to grow as a player, this game is for you.

The Stanley Parable. It sounds so simple, but get's more complicated once you get past the name.
You play as Stanley, a rather ordinary and boring man who works in an office building every day, pushing buttons on his computer's keyboard. But one day he realizes that everyone else in his office has disappeared, and he sets out on a bizarre adventure to find out what happened to them.
Everything in this game is based on choice. Whether you follow the story from start to finish, or derail it entirely, it's all down to what you choose.
The game is rather impressive, considering it started out as a mod for another game entirely. The whole thing is based on the players choices, which lead down different routes to different possible endings. Finding the endings is entertaining enough, but they aren't the best part of this game.
What is the best part you ask? Two words. Actually, a name: Kevan Brighting.
Brighting is the voice actor for the narrator, a bodyless voice who...well, narrates. And by god, he makes this game as good as it is. The best thing about this game is hearing Brighting's voice as he reacts to your various choices, sometimes helping you, sometimes insulting you, and sometimes trying to get you killed.
The game looks nice enough, and the play is fairly smooth.
Warning: If you are a completionist, this game is NOT for you. Not only is it difficult to figure out how to get every ending, but three of the achievments are stupid to get. One requires you to not play the game for five years, one requires you to play for the ENTIRE durration of a Tuesday, and one is called the Impossible Achievment. It's description literally says: You cannot get this achievment. Granted, there are five other achievments that are easy to get by comparison, but those three could give a completionist nightmares.
Also, this game isn't worth $15. $5? Yes, but not 15.
So it it entertaining, yes, but mostly for Kevan Brighting's voice work. If you decide to get it, I would wait for a sale, and for the love of god, don't become obsessed with getting every achievment. I would also recommend playing the Demo first, so you can get a feel for the game without actually spoiling it for yourself, and decide if it's for you.
For myself, I would give it a 7.5/10, but again, mostly because of Brighting. So I recommend it, but only provisionally.
But in the end, whether you get it or not...is your choice.

The original Shadow Warrior was a bit like Duke Nukem 3D with Kung Fu movie tropes and racism mixed in. The new one goes for a more tasteful route, and it works. The story is surprisingly interesting. I was expecting something more basic like the original, but it's impressive. There's twists and turns, and pulls you in. Your character, Lo Wang, is a refreshing action hero. He's a dynamic and likable tough guy with his own moments of laughter at his expense.
The sound is pretty solid. The music keeps up with the flow of gameplay well. The voice acting is remarkably good as well. And any game with the song "The Touch" in it gets points from me.
It also looks great. There's some great variety with the levels and some nice details the models. The menus of the game also clearly had a surprisingly high amount of work put into them. My only complaint here is that the lip syncing for voice acting can be wonky at times.
The gameplay rocks. The sword-play made me believe melee can work in games by doing more than just clicking. Each swing's angle can copy the angle you move the camera or Lo Wang. It's fluid with a small learning curve. This game's a great example of older mechanics mixed with new ones in a good way. You have the frantic run-and-gun gameplay and complex levels of the past with modern polish. However, the difficulty suddenly spiking and disruptive glitches are rare but frustraing problems. Nonetheless, this game is amazing.

This game has a lot of features that you rarely see, and sometimes make a game worse but somehow work in this one.
Pros:
Essentially a walking simulator that doesn't suck (never thought I'd say that.)
The antagonist is largely the narrator as he tries to convince you to follow his commands.
One ending requires you play an immensely boring game about pressing 2 buttons to save cardboard cutouts for 4 freaking hours. (Look it up online cause yeah....)
Great comedy that has self referencing, breaking the 4th wall, etc...
The game changes at random like loading a different office to start, or having papers on the floor, or even just having different dialog play so you can't tell if the game is new or if your restart triggered some new strange events.
Cons:
Basically the only point is the achievements, jokes, and endings all of which can be look up online to see what they entail.
Not much replay once you've done all the endings.
It has the full spectrum of ridiculous events in it. The game is about an office employee Stanley whos job is to mindlessly follow commands, the game then proceeds to have the narrator cough up commands for you to blindly follow. It has multiple endings and the "True ending" (the one you get the achievment for beating the game) is the one where you do as he says. That said it doesn't so much have multiple endings as the game IS multiple endings. They vary depending on when/if you disobey the narrators instructions, and the journey to the endings is often crazy enough to involve false game resets, slightly altered areas (Though the areas and dialog alter slightly at random times too just so you can never tell if it's part of the ending from last time.), and self referencing commentary.
The game also has crazy achievements, some as easy as turning the ability to earn achievments on or spamming 8 on the numberpad in the bosses office. To insane request, like not playing the game for 5 years (or just changing your computers date) and one that has a list of randomly generated requirements to unlock.
It's worth a buy but definitely wait for a sale I'm not sure it's worth the $15.

This game is fantastic there's nothing else to really say that does it glory. The idea of the game is magnificent in the fact that it shows potential to be a great esport after some balance patches and etc. There's a reason the game wasn't released to the public as of yet. The game does need some polish. There's some strange bugs a not that great ranking system, no normal games and a whole slew of things that would turn so many people off right away. But don't let that stop you. The devs are constantly working and constantly listening to the complaints of the community to make a great game for everyone. The content seems boring at first sight (According to some people I've tried to show it to.) But it's quite interesting since the game never feels like the same game. After one round is completed you have a set of options that allow you to play the game with as much freedom as you want. The whole idea is to give players options that are all good and all useful. Plus the skill ceiling makes it all the better. You can play the game and constantly improve. Grasping the basics WILL be a little tough. You WILL hit into every counter. You WILL miss a lot. There's no saying you'll pick up this game and be a god at it instantly. But there's so much more to the game. Push through the frustration of sucking and a whole world is opened to you. The original Shadow Warrior was a bit like Duke Nukem 3D with Kung Fu movie tropes and racism mixed in. The new one goes for a more tasteful route, and it works. The story is surprisingly interesting. I was expecting something more basic like the original, but it's impressive. There's twists and turns, and pulls you in. Your character, Lo Wang, is a refreshing action hero. He's a dynamic and likable tough guy with his own moments of laughter at his expense.
The sound is pretty solid. The music keeps up with the flow of gameplay well. The voice acting is remarkably good as well. And any game with the song "The Touch" in it gets points from me.
It also looks great. There's some great variety with the levels and some nice details the models. The menus of the game also clearly had a surprisingly high amount of work put into them. My only complaint here is that the lip syncing for voice acting can be wonky at times.
The gameplay rocks. The sword-play made me believe melee can work in games by doing more than just clicking. Each swing's angle can copy the angle you move the camera or Lo Wang. It's fluid with a small learning curve. This game's a great example of older mechanics mixed with new ones in a good way. You have the frantic run-and-gun gameplay and complex levels of the past with modern polish. However, the difficulty suddenly spiking and disruptive glitches are rare but frustraing problems. Nonetheless, this game is amazing.

TLDR:
If you like the team fights of MOBAs, or WoW arenas - but don't like the grinding to get there: You will probably like this game.
~~~~~~~~~~
2v2/3v3 team-based twin-stick skill-shot fantasy-themed arena combat.
Payment Model:
Currently all characters are unlocked, and there is no equipment, levels, or other boosting methods.
A fresh account has the exact same combat ability of a verteran.
Purchases bring cosmetic items, and there is a founders DLC that gives +10% xp to you and your party - but levels only reward cosmetics anyway.
The game is going free to play, and if they stick with this shop model - they're off to a good start.
Gameplay:
Combat is fast paced, 100% skillshot.
Players are placed at opposite ends of a mirror arena, best of 5 rounds wins.
Between rounds, each player is offered an upgrade - that puts a different spin on an existing skill.
These modifications are chosen from a predetermined pool per character per round - increasing in power as the rounds go on.
These can offer more uses, extra effects, more damage, etc. This allows players to customise their character to their playstyle - with an extra skill in choosing modifications that counter your opponents.
There's more active abilities than the average MOBA, with each character having at least 7 skills. Some are on cooldown, some consume charge generated by using other abilities.
Beware if your internet isn't great, or you live in a remote area - since even small amounts of latency will cost you matches. (Rejoice Australians, there are AUS servers!)
Progression:
Since combat is skill-based, there's a high skill ceiling to each character, with use of skills and positioning being crucial to success.
In early access, no characters are unlocked over time, but cosmetic items are earned by leveling characters and completing daily missions (to use characters from certain pools).
There's no gear treadmill to grind here.
Story:
Nearly non-existant, giving only short backstories on characters, no single player campaign.
Graphics:
A high fantasy art style, combat animations are clear in purpose.
The top down shooter view means you rarely get a close look at the models, but they are good enough.
Sound:
Music is enough to get the point across without being distracting, and the sound design doesn't have any jarring misses.
