Warning, SPOILERS:
I bought this game on sale for 3.74 USD during the Summer 2015 steam sale. It is a meta game where you walk around making simple choices like which door to walk through or which button to press while a narrator talks. The main entertainment of the game comes from choosing to obey or disobey the narrator and hearing his reactions to your choices.
The game starts with a mystery about why Stanley is alone at his work. The controls are simple; you walk around and you click on doors or buttons. Everything you do is narrated. If you follow everything the narrator says, you can finish the game in less than 5 minutes. There are, of course, many opportunities to disobey the narrator, which are essentially the other 21 'storylines' of the game.
You might enjoy the meta humor and narrative reactions to all of your choices. There are 22 different endings. Many of them can be discovered within a few minutes, but one ending takes 4 hours of repetitive button clicking to achieve. If you're the kind of person who enjoys replaying a game to discover all of the different endings, this game is definitely for you. If you're looking for a game with action, you could simply google "stanley parable endings" instead to spoil the game's many endings.

This game is just something else. A fun, cute but menacing metroidvania that doesn't hold back in its difficulty. A twisted Dark Souls 2D crossover, which definitely punches above its weight considering its small budget (a ~$45,000USD kickstarter), and very small team of three developers. With a unique and charming hand drawn art style, along an almost Lovecraftian vibe, the atmosphere is something unlike any other game. Its exploration, secrets, map, and combat are all very well constructed. Creating an amazing world for an equally incredible story to take place in. Again, it is very Dark Souls-esque in its storytelling, much of it implied by the environment and the short interactions with the various NPC's. The writing is fantasic, with characters changing and evolving as the game progresses, creating connections and interest in everyone you meet. Its accompaning soundtrack is nothing short of its previous successes either, soft orchestral music giving off an aesthetic not unlike a Studio Ghibli movie in the cities, intense drums in the midst of a boss battle, and beautiful ambient sounds when traversing the world.
With an incredible story, amazing soundtrack, beatiful art design, fluid combat, and a deep world to explore, this game is a must play and is definitely on my personal Game of the Year shortlist.

Hollow Knight is honest to god one of the best games I've played in recent memory and manages to combine my favorite aspects of Dark Souls with a classic 2D metroidvania in an incredible fashion. While the game is not without a fair amount of flaws, and design choices that may not appeal to
, what it does do well it absolutely accels at, and the incredibly vast world of Hollownest always presents new areas to explore and items to collect, which only had me playing for more hours on end. The comparisons to Ori and the Blind Forest are not invalid, but I feel Hollow Knight picks up the ball for me in areas where I felt Ori dropped it into a ditch.
Since I feel it's one of the best ways to sum it up, here's a list of Pros/Cons regarding the game:
So, I would highly reccomend this game if you are either a fan of the Metroidvania genre, enjoy exploration of a vast and detailed world, enjoy gameplay of 2D sidescrollers or can appreciate a good challenge through solid and responsive combat mechanics/controls.
On the other hand, Hollow Knight is a fairly difficult game; the main story, maybe not so much, but the high amounts of postgame/optional content is VERY difficult and I don't feel the game is properly done justice without it. As such, if you are not sure if you would be good I would advise you be cautious with purchasing. As well, if you hate consistent backtracking, possible grinding (Geo costs lul) and may get frustrated with punishment mechanics (losing Geo, breaking fragile charms) you may want to steer clear of Hollow Knight.
All in all, an absolutely amazing experience. While moderate information regarding enemies/locations may not mean much, as with many things, the experience is best blind, and you should only turn to a guide IF needed.
Do you enjoy meta-humor and walking simulators? If so, buy this game.

Every once in a while, it's nice to come across a game that you weren't expecting, the kind of game that creeps up on you and then stays with you long after you've finished playing.  The Stanley Parable was originally developed as a Source engine mod back in 2010. Its creator Davey Wreden said that he set out to discover something about video games that hadn't been explored yet. More specifically, what would happen if you could disobey their rules.
The game tells the story of Stanley, an average man who finds solace in his simple mundane office job. However on one particular day it appears that all his co-workers have suddenly disappeared. Guided by the narrator, Stanley must step out of the safety of his little cubical and begin his adventure to find out what exactly is going on.
At first glance it might seem easy to categorise this as another artsy "walk 'em up" in the vein of something like Dear Esther or Proteus. It has a simple setting, lots of long-winded narration, not much to interact with and of course no jump or weapons, so what exactly do you do in The Stanley Parable? Well, essentially you make decisions. This is because the driving force behind the game is that of "choice". You decide HOW you play the game, and the game responds accordingly. And these decisions may appear simple, left or right? Over there? Over here? Touch that?
Meanwhile you're guided by the soothing sound of 'the narrator' voiced brilliantly by British voice actor Kevan Brighting! The narrator attempts to lead you to successfully complete the game by advising you which path to take as well as narrating the inner monologue of the troubled protagonist Stanley. And it's through this narration that the game achieves a level of hysterical self awareness and brilliant charm very similar to the Portal series. This dynamic narration will react to the decisions you make, often breaking the fourth wall to talk to you directly. And should you decide not to listen to these directions and "disobey" the resulting dialogue and consequences can easily spiral out of control into the strange and surreal.
But to say anymore would no doubt ruin your experience of The Stanley Parable as no two play throughs are really the same. And multiple play throughs are inevitable in a game that encourages you to poke and prod at its structure, almost everyone I know who've played this walked away from this game with a different story to tell.
Depending on how your experience plays out, at some stage or another you will no doubt be forced to return to Stanley's office to once again set out to look for your co-workers, and it's here that you might decide to stop playing the game and that's totally fine, but in my experience, once you've been presented with so many variables, it's very hard to resist that urge to go back and try out every possible deviation, especially when they can alter the game so radically beyond your expectations.
And this kind of thinking is just so refreshing, I found myself laughing with confusion and disbelief because every time I pushed the game, it would push back. I guess the only disappointing moment was when I came to the stark realisation that the game couldn't possibly live up to the illusion of infinite choice. However this was more bitter sweet, as I soon came to the realisation that any game that gave me this feeling of absolute freedom, if only for the briefest moment in time, was truly remarkable.
The Stanley Parable might not be for everyone, but in my opinion it should be played by everyone. It's a hilarious experiment in psychology and non-linear game design that will probably teach you more about yourself as a gamer than you might want to know.

This game is the definition of funky... In a good way, of course.
I never did like the MOBA genre of games, and this at first glance looked like another cookie cutter MOBA. One of my biggest gripes with DOTA and LoL is the click-to-move style of control. I never found it fun, kinda a personal issue. As someone with 1000+ hours in Spiral Knights, this WASD click-to-attack hacky-n-slashy style was a really welcome concept.
Alongside that, you can choose Battlerites during the game to further funkify stuff. It reminds me a lot of the mutation system in Nuclear Throne.
Aaaaaaand, on top of it all, there is no way to change character/champion/hero/god/battledude once you enter a game. Therefore, there is no real "rock paper scissors" aspect this game, and as such, you can feel free to main whatever character you like, without people complaining that you aren't "countering" someone.
Games are short and sweet, or short and sour. If you're reking the enemy, you'll win quick. If they're reking you, it's over quick. It's great because you're not locked into a 50+ minute game with completely incompetent dweeberonis.
But, as much as I like this game, I'll highlight some flaws/cons:
-Some abilities feel a bit off, such as Croak(my main)'s swords/daggers having a bit shorter of a range than I feel they should. It's almost like the swords are longer than the actual attack radius. This is more of a quality of life thing, all things considered.
-Maps are very same-y. Pretty much all maps have the exact same layout, the only difference being the way you enter. I'm sure they'll add more variety in the future, however.
-Game mode restricted. So far I've only really found the head-to-head arena gamemode, which makes me think it's the only one in the game. While it is perfectly fine, and definitely fun, I feel like the game could use some more variety.
Tl;dr: It's a great game, fun to play, it's different, the characters are interesting. Lacks a bit in the variety department, but its a fairly new game and it's early access, so I'm sure they'll spice things up in the future.
Verdict: This is an early access game? Couldn't tell. 9/10

If you like being berated, toyed with, and manipulated by a faceless omniscient being, then this is the game for you. Also you might need to take a look at any possibly abusive relationships you might previously or currently be in, but that's really your business, not mine.
The odd thing about this game is that the "best" (IE happiest) ending is by far the easiest and quickest to obtain; you just do as the narrator commands you to and it will be over in about five minutes.
The FUN (and entire point of the game) comes from looking for all the different ways you can subvert that narrative and spite the narrator, to go off-course and be scolded for it.  Essentially, you get to let out the defiant child in all of us, who does things they know they aren't supposed to do just to get a reaction out of their authority figures.
Yes, the game is incredibly short (You can experience 100% of the sights, dialogue, and secrets in about 3 hours), but it's an experience you won't regret; think of it like a gourmet chocolate bar. A chocolate bar that calls you fat while you eat it.

Is it a MOBA? No.
No laning or farming to gain exp/gold to "become powerful" enough to fight. No item system to force-synergise your spells. No team mates feeding during laning, destroying your efforts of becoming farmed/levelled enough to participate in fights.
Just skill here, kids. Scoop out all of the early-game detritus of a MOBA and add those sweet, sweet teamfights that you farm and level for but in a more concentrated form. No levelling or farming required here, you start as the best you can possibly be and so do your enemy. Battlerites alter abilities but their general use remains similar. If you lose, it is because your team lacked the skill to win.
Hard to throw blame in circumstances like these.
Positioning is crucial. Did you use that large jump move to enter combat? Well now it is on cooldown and you're without an escape mechanism if the proverbial hits the fan. Are you being too cautious? Well now you are too far from the fight to effectively deal damage or support your allies.
Reflexes are crucial. Do you activate your counter in the hopes an enemy will clumsily attack you? Are you that enemy, and will you clumsily attack or see the counter animation and cancel your movement? Are you the healer watching the scenario unfold, and can you effectively shield/heal as required when the event resolves?
Hand-eye coordination is crucial. Can you hit an opponent consistently at various distances and speeds with differing projectiles and aoe vectors? Can you do this with the knowledge they could counter, leap, teleport or just plain change direction at any time? The potential for mindgames is great here.
If you have the patience to learn and the above has interested you, this game....is crucial. I've played almost 20 hours and witnessed no community toxicity. The graphics and sound are great, no oversaturation of particle effects to make the game cluttered, and the developers are on the ball with updates and general community activity.
"...wait, he's only played ~20 hours?"
Yes, and I am still learning myself. But be sure to check back. I'm hooked. That ~20 hours is only going to rise and rise....

Dive wrecks in a diving bell looking for sunken treasure , harpoon whales and sharks from the small rowboat on your ship , take out assasination missions , take down royal frigates and their escorts, search for booty on remote islands, take part in gambling minigames.Break into smuggler caves and rob them of their ill gotten riches. Anything that you can think of that is piratey and its in here for you to do.

Fantastic looking game with some amazing boss fights. It's challenging but fair most of the time. The level design and soundtrack are fantastic.
- Let's start with the biggest problem: the tons of running. You will spend half of your time backtracking to the boss or your lost points. It`s normal to backtrack 4 minutes just for a 2 minute boss fight over and over again. Wanna go back to the city? 5 - 10 min. Lost right before a savepoint? Theres no running past enemies most of the time so better do the whole 20 min area again. Wanna retry a jumping challenge? 5-10 min backtracking. Go to the Bank? 5 min. Oh, and don't forget farming. Never seen a game treating the players time with such disrespect.
- The way the game is designed you have a strange difficulty curve. It starts of perfectly fine and turns quite hard one third trough. After that it only gets easier. I even killed the last 5 bosses by facetanking them. The last endgame content is difficult again. Those mid game weapon upgrades are way too overpowered. Such open worlds need some sort of scaling or weaker upgrades. Otherwise some content has to get too easy near the end. But never dying removed the backtracking which made the game extremly enjoyable.
- They have put an unaccessible secret into nearly every room. There are dozens of places you need to remeber but no map marker feature. I can't think of any game needing this more than this one.
- Shops are all over the place without any reason other than to let the player backtrack even more. This is really cheap playtime inflation.

- I finished the games story and i have to disagree with most reviews. They praise the story way above what it actually is. Sure, it's good and sometimes really charming but not the holy once in a lifetime revelation some describe it as.

- Having no save point near Crystallised Mound is stupid. Acient basin and Deepnest could use some more save points and stag stations too. Crystal cave needs a stag station, the Hive or Kingdom`s Edge too.
They actually added one new stag station in the acient basin. A step in the right direction. The new teleport ability helps a bit too but is given way to late into the game. Hope these weren´t the last backtracking fixes. At least two more patches to go.
- Steam forums are always more or less bad but HK forum takes the crown. 95% of all responses are pure garbage. Look at the subreddit if you need help.
Honestly, all negative points could be forgiven if it wasn´t for the insane amount of backtracking. Imagine having to stare at a blank wall for 20 minutes after every fight in street fighter. That`s what this game feels like. If you don`t mind that at all, go ahead and buy it. It`s a really good game otherwise.
More benches and bench teleporting (or just more stag stations). Bam 10/10 game of the year.
Since a comment showed that people don`t get my review heres some clarification. I have no personal problem with the difficulty. I love frustrating boss fights. Some parts of the game are just unfair which is bad game design but i don`t mind it that much. I`ve spend most of my time playing with mindless boring running. No challenge, no skill, just mundane and stale running. Originally this was done mostly in old games as a way to strech game time. This outdated design decision should be buried and forgotten.

Lets start with the Pros:
-Fully fleshed out ship warfare.  If you enjoyed the ship battles in AC:III Then you need to get this game.  Seriously... it's great
-Huge explorable map.  Relatively soon after the introduction after you get your ship, the world is your oyster.  The further south you go the harder the ships get, so be careful.
-COLLECTIONS, COLLECTIONS, COLLECTIONS.  You have Animus fragments, messages in a bottle, treasure maps that you must collect and then lead you to treasure, sea shanties for your crew that they actually sing, and various wildlife for you to exterminate to make yourself look cooler, oh and the Mayans left some stuff laying around.
-The atmosphere is absolutely amazing.  The shanties mentioned before are actually sung really well and makes your pirate ship come alive.  Cities feel lifelike and there is plenty to do on the high seas.
-Oh yah... this is Assassins Creed.  There are two different types of Assassin style missions.  Pirating assassinations, and the Creed assassinations.  So get out there and kill some people.
-If you have a tablet PC you can further enhance your experience by downloading the app that aids you while you're within the game.  This app will load up the full map and you can mark things on the map on your tablet and it will mark it in your game.  It will also track your overall progress, load up your treasure maps instantly if you're on an island that relates to that map, and manage your fleet of ships even if you're off line.  This is one of the first games I have played where  the mobile app for the game actually provides great functionality.  If you do not have a tablet you can load it on your mobile phone as well.
-Legendary ships provide a great challenge for the mastery of your vessel in combat.
-Without giving too much away the story and its characters are all absolutely fantastic and is on par with AC:II story telling.
So the Cons
-Get stuck on random stuff sometimes when free running
-Weird issue when loading in and seeing your ship in either; A. Massive pit in the ocean.  B. Popping up from the bottom of the ocean.  C. Doing a reverse titanic and unsinking itself.   Its pretty rare that it does this, but its still pretty funny.
-Boat variety is a bit lacking.  There is only five classes of ships you will ever see in the game, plus the unique legendary ships.  The Man O' War's can put up a good fight though, especially if they have help.
-Similar to Watch_Dogs the PC optimization is quite awful so heres a pro tip:
1. Turn off in game Vsync, and set the Physx Particles to Low.
2. Turn on Adaptive Vsync through your Nvidia control panel and voila... enjoy your many pirating adventures.
Overall the game is quite wonderful and I would rank it up there with ACII in terms of game play.

The narrator will often make you chuckle. It's worth pursuing every ending of the game, simply to hear his commentary.
You'll probably play through most of the endings in less than five hours, but the uniqueness of this game makes it worth its money. I'd recommend it to people looking for a game that will make them laugh and that doesn't require a lot of effort.

Shadow warrior is a throw-back to more old-school FPS games like Quake or Duke Nukem 3D - But with updated graphics, great voice acting, really enjoyable characters and a remarkably sad story to it.
At the surface level, Shadow Warrior may seem just like a mindless FPS game with some swordplay until you get into the later parts of the game - Where it becomes apparent what the lore actually is and the story unfolds in a major way.
I won't spoil it - But it's safe to say that the story is touching and a very clever take on Chinese folklore.
As for the gameplay - The controls are generally solid except for when performing special moves (Quick prompts of the same keys - Which leads to confusion on the games interpetation part/Is very frustrating). The game has a good flow and there are plenty of secrets well hidden throughout the levels to keep you scouring the levels for them.
Some of the levels are however, poorly designed. Some of the later levels simply serve to be very, very annoying in the way of clouding vision and generally being constructed in a form of "Dragged out" way. This is however, a small blemish on the overall great level design and enjoyment of the game overall - But should still be duly noted so that your enjoyment overall is not spoiled.
There's not much else to say about this game ; especially not the boss battles. While epic in size and you tend to fight something much larger then you ; it's still in the sense of Doom. You shoot it until it dies ; It's not easy per-say and yes, there is skill but the logic here is not mindblowing.
Would i recommend this game? Not at full price point. At a steam-sale ; yes.

Okay this is kind of a First Look Review.
I am four hours in.
So far it is what it promissed. An immensely beautifull, atmospheric and challenging game.
Right now though it seems to have a bit of a pacing problem because of two points.
The first point is that games difficulty picks up REALLY sudden and sharp with certain enemys AND unfortunate placed safepoints. [With that i do NOT mean the first boss. I'd argue there are harder, REGULAR characters after that.]
Consider i only say that because of the safepointplacements (wich are iron benches) that had me trace back a looong way and the open way the game is done wich can cause you to miss some safepoints.
The second point is the pacing. Four hours in, i have bought out the first traders complete stock. [That trader sells mapmarkers wich is a bit odd and feels fillery for a lack of better wording. The compass i can clearly understand but markers for certain things like traders, quicktravelpoints and other characters, really?]
Four hours in i also have gotten One Spell (a kind of fireball) and one Pin (pins are this games skillsystem) that gives you more energy (for spells and healing) for slain enemys. That. Is. It.
[Actually i got two Pins but that one doesn't turn up in the Pin System for use so i have no idea what is up with that and the game has not explained anything about that.]
Let us talk about what this game gameplay wise has to offer:
Mapicons [wich i needed to buy so the mapsystem is using them wich is kind off silly and as i mentione feels fillerry but wich i already have all bought.]
The Maps [This system is VERY obnoxious. The world is parted into several Subregions, wich is fine so far. However, in every region you NEED to find the guy drawing maps so you can buy one from him, Until you have done NONE of the region that you have NOT the map of will not be filled in by the game, wich is stupid especially when you had to intitally buy a feather from the Mapshop that says you need it to draw the map. This is just silly. In similar games if the game has a system like that, it draws the map while you explore but gives you the WHOLE map when you find a vendor or machine or whatever that gives you a map. The way it is done here it hampers you exploration because you are more or less walking around without knowing where you are or where you really have been before. I do not personally have a big problem with that. But i have also played games like this since the SNES. But even i have ran in circles trough similar looking areas already until i had the map and i am pretty sure for other players this can be a problem.]
Pins [These pins you can find and activate. To activate you pin them onto a number off Buttons wich ae basically slots. Different Pins require a varying amount of these Buttons/Slots]
Buttons/Slots [at the beginning you have three slots wich are more or less imidiately filled up by the first Pins you get with hin the first half an hour or so wich leads to the conclusion that you can upgrade the amount of Slots.]
Spells [Your first Spell, a kind of white energy fireball, you also get within that first half an hour.]
Since then i that was it. That is three and a half hours where i explored a whole lot of the world without finding too much of these elements that change up the gameplay.
I found several Quicktravelstations, three maps and the variety of enemys is refreshingbut i hope i get some new toy to play with soon because until now it was a lot of challenge and no payoff.
The worst problem though could become the fact that there are places that are made for a later coming back when you have found the necessary Skillspins. However these are without markings on the map and the individual room on the map are not detailed enough (they only show the general shape of the outer walls, if that makes sense) that i am not sure i can be bothered to track allof themdown later, whenver i find the "walljump" or "fly for a bit" powers.
What i DID find though is litterally twothousand of the currency of this game and NOTHING to spend it on.
Sp far i can onlöy recommend it despite these flaws because the combat feels fresh and impactfull and the charming optics and haunting atmosphere carries this game with ease.
I will change and add to this review when i am deeper in.

Shadow Warrior is a first-person shooter computer game developed by Flying Wild Hog and published by Devolver Digital for the PC. It is a reboot of the 1997 game of the same name developed by 3D Realms.
The original Shadow Warrior was made on the Build Engine, which was made popular by the infamous Duke Nukem 3D back in 1997. At that time, it was considered (at least in my opinion)
merely a Duke clone with a slightly different Oriental settings peppered with juvenile oriental stereotype types of humor.
This remake however is really a whole different ball game. Its funny to see how the long delayed Duke Nukem Forever stumbled and fell flat on it's face in today's world, while Shadow Warrior instead feels very fresh and actually very entertaining.
The game is around 15 hours long, with a surprisingly deep and sometimes emotional story. While it will certainly not win any awards for the plot, it definitely adds alot to the overall game.
Graphics wise, Shadow Warrior really shines, with beautiful virtual pagodas, pavilions, with shimmering koi ponds accentuated with the smooth swaying of cherry blossoms. The whole
game looks absolutely stunning and is a visual joy.
Sound and music are appropriately meaty, with every slice and boom being crisp and clear. Music consists of a mixture of modern Rock with a touch of traditional Japanese instruments and this is especially exhillarating to hear during intense combat situations.
The game also includes a level up system of sorts where you will be able to spend points upgrading your character and he definitely gets alot more powerful the more points you spend. Its a pity then however that there is no way to respec the points that are used, so you might want to take note of that.
Gameplay wise, the game makes heavy use of Old-School shooter mechanics. Levels are fairly linear and alot of sections will require some backtracking to obtain either a key or to fulfill whichever objectives before a new path will open to you. Despite this, Shadow Warrior never feels too old-school. The level designs are very organically and naturally done and this of course is helped alot by its fantastic visuals as mentioned.
Combat feels fast and visceral, but I felt alot of encounters have a very "Hoard Mode" feel to them. Most of the time, enemies will charge at you en-masse, and you will do alot of backtracking while simultaneously either shooting them and slicing them with the sword.
Speaking of the sword, this has got to be the BEST use of the sword I have ever encountered in a first person shooter. It is powerful, fast and easy to use. In fact, I personally use the sword almost 90% of the time as it really feels very badass to be able to slice and dice thru the enemy.
Downsides, I felt that the main bosses while visually very stunning, were very standard affairs. Its the usual "Shoot at the shining pieces of armor then proceed to shoot the exposed part over and over again." Every boss has this same mechanic. Some variations would have been welcome.
In fact, the hardest enemy I faced in the game were a couple of sub-bosses that charged at you and their only weak spot was a section at their back. The hardest fight has got to be the last big horde at one of the last chapters of the game, where you will face 3 waves of enemies.
Overall Rating: 8.0 / 10
I certainly enjoyed my time during the game. An excellent reboot and a very triumphant return of Shadow Warrior. This game is how Duke Nukem Forever should have been.

Ubisoft has done it again. I bought this game at a later date to get it at a lower price and in the hopes that all the bugs and wrinkles would be ironed out.
I don't need to complete that paragraph, do I?
I bought the game mainly for the multiplayer, and haven't played the single-player beyond the first island, so this review won't be going into that. I am sure it also has its share of annoyances. In any case, I was hoping that Ubisoft would have learned from all the ♥♥♥♥ups of the past, but no.
There are three kinds of bugs: the first kind is the one you can live with. The other kind is one that prevents you from playing, something that is often a mercy.
The third kind is the kind that is tantalizing, something you think you could ignore... but no. It is there, ♥♥♥♥ing up your day, all the time in the most frustrating ways possible.
I don't get angry at games. Except... Assassin's Creed Multiplayer.
The MP is a mess of connection and server-side issues. For example, for me the leveling mechanism does not work properly, and I will be rewarded with in-game skill point currency I am due if I am very lucky during a particular session. Then there are the constant matchmaking and connection issues that plague the game itself. We live in the far-flung future of 2014, and Ubisoft still hasn't figured out how to program a multiplayer game that doesn't ♥♥♥♥ with you at random.
I tried to reset my password at the Ubisoft support site, but even their password reset system is bugged, because they ♥♥♥♥ed up their recaptcha system by providing two obligatory fields when the captchas themselves are just providing single-word Googlemaps address numbers nowadays.
This is a good time to mention the time I discovered that when registering into Ubisoft-something-or-other the system would glady accept a password with space characters--and then not accept passwords with spaces in them when logging in, making you question your sanity as you desperately try to figure out why all your passwords don't work.
This mess of frustration is just a culmination of Ubisoft's philosophy of tossing out a new game every year and trying to monetize the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of it in the meanwhile, all the while ignoring the glaring problems their games have as they migrate on to their next project: their grandest, most vast ♥♥♥♥ up to date, whenever that is.
I am reasonably certain that the Abstergo Credit bug is because you can now buy microtransaction currency for real money. The systems for preventing abuse are also ♥♥♥♥ing everything up for everyone else. Some people have even reported not getting their microtransaction rewards, which is the only reason why I don't think Ubisoft is preventing normal in-game currency collection to sell Erudito credits.
As the multiplayer component of an AC game dies out as each new titles in the series come out, I wish that the multiplayer could be divorced from the single player in order to give it the time it needs to mature and to keep a steady long-time player base. As it is, though the MP is a beautiful, beautiful game, it is beautiful in the way that a sick person dying of consumption in some old Gothic novel is beautiful: pale, doomed and breaking my heart.

I got to say, pretty good Metroidvania Game with fair bosses, great combat, good soundtrack and some decent platforming sections in the game. Although one has to say that while the story is pretty great and the characters are quite beatifully drawn, at most times the dialogue is pretty average, not bad but nothing to really write home about. Though it gets slightly better once you unlock an item to read the thoughts of npcs and bosses, which adds a little bit of depth to the mystery sorrounding the Hallownest which this game resides in. As with any Metroidvania, this game features a variety of abilties, some of which are combat only and others which help to discover new paths for finding collectibles or advancing in the story.
There are a bunch of zones, all filled with unique enemies, loretidbits and collectibles for you to discover, two central collectibles are the charms which can be equipped and give you a number of different bonuses like the ability to dash more often, heal quicker or deal more damage to name a few, as well as little green worms called grubs, which are cute as ♥♥♥♥, pardon my language. Collecting the grubs lands you rewards like money, charms and more. To help you around the zones, there is a map maker in every zone which sells you an incomplete map of the zone, the undiscored paths, so to speak will be drawn in after you've explored them and visited a bench to draw them in.
Some people report some fps drops here and there, which i haven't encountered in all my playthroughs so far. Although i had a few freezes after sitting on benches, which purpose I've explained previously. I assume this is because the game saves and draws newly discovered locations onto the map at the same time. No matter, that was only a minor discomfort for myself and really shouldn't deter you from purchasing and enjoying this game.
All in All, one of the best metroidvania games I've played in a looooong time and probably one of the top contenders for Game of the Year 2017.

Shadow Warrior is a first-person shooter computer game developed by Flying Wild Hog and published by Devolver Digital for the PC. It is a reboot of the 1997 game of the same name developed by 3D Realms.
The original Shadow Warrior was made on the Build Engine, which was made popular by the infamous Duke Nukem 3D back in 1997. At that time, it was considered (at least in my opinion)
merely a Duke clone with a slightly different Oriental settings peppered with juvenile oriental stereotype types of humor.
This remake however is really a whole different ball game. Its funny to see how the long delayed Duke Nukem Forever stumbled and fell flat on it's face in today's world, while Shadow Warrior instead feels very fresh and actually very entertaining.
The game is around 15 hours long, with a surprisingly deep and sometimes emotional story. While it will certainly not win any awards for the plot, it definitely adds alot to the overall game.
Graphics wise, Shadow Warrior really shines, with beautiful virtual pagodas, pavilions, with shimmering koi ponds accentuated with the smooth swaying of cherry blossoms. The whole
game looks absolutely stunning and is a visual joy.
Sound and music are appropriately meaty, with every slice and boom being crisp and clear. Music consists of a mixture of modern Rock with a touch of traditional Japanese instruments and this is especially exhillarating to hear during intense combat situations.
The game also includes a level up system of sorts where you will be able to spend points upgrading your character and he definitely gets alot more powerful the more points you spend. Its a pity then however that there is no way to respec the points that are used, so you might want to take note of that.
Gameplay wise, the game makes heavy use of Old-School shooter mechanics. Levels are fairly linear and alot of sections will require some backtracking to obtain either a key or to fulfill whichever objectives before a new path will open to you. Despite this, Shadow Warrior never feels too old-school. The level designs are very organically and naturally done and this of course is helped alot by its fantastic visuals as mentioned.
Combat feels fast and visceral, but I felt alot of encounters have a very "Hoard Mode" feel to them. Most of the time, enemies will charge at you en-masse, and you will do alot of backtracking while simultaneously either shooting them and slicing them with the sword.
Speaking of the sword, this has got to be the BEST use of the sword I have ever encountered in a first person shooter. It is powerful, fast and easy to use. In fact, I personally use the sword almost 90% of the time as it really feels very badass to be able to slice and dice thru the enemy.
Downsides, I felt that the main bosses while visually very stunning, were very standard affairs. Its the usual "Shoot at the shining pieces of armor then proceed to shoot the exposed part over and over again." Every boss has this same mechanic. Some variations would have been welcome.
In fact, the hardest enemy I faced in the game were a couple of sub-bosses that charged at you and their only weak spot was a section at their back. The hardest fight has got to be the last big horde at one of the last chapters of the game, where you will face 3 waves of enemies.
Overall Rating: 8.0 / 10

I stopped playing Zelda because I was so obsessed with this game.
Every jump and every strike feels responsive. The combat starts off basic yet fun, and as you get more abilities you'll be dashing and wall-jumping all over the place, against some tough but fair bosses, in a style that reminded me of Megaman Zero of all things.
There is a lot of focus on exploration. For each zone, you don't get a map until you find the cartographer. Even then, he sells you an incomplete map, and your map updates only at save points. This makes you explore a lot in 'the dark' based only on your orientation. Although some people might not like that, I loved it. If you disable your marker location you even get an extra ability slot, as a reward for those who don't need it.
The story takes from Dark Souls at first, giving you bits of lore on a dripfeed. After seeing the credits the first time, I was satisfied but confused as to what was going on. There is more to the game than just the final boss though, and I kept getting surprised by the amount of new zones I was finding AFTER having beaten the final boss. The finale was grandiose and left a lasting impression on me.
Do I even need to mention the great hand-drawn art and beautiful music?
Now that I'm done, I can go play Zelda again. And you should go buy Hollow Knight.
Edit: Also the DLC is awesome and fixes the few minor flaws I had with this game.

I've got 19 hours in and I highly recommend this game.  The experience is as close to Super Metroid as I've ever had in a title like this.  I've been playing games for about 25 years, so at this point i'm super picky with boring formulas, or lazy design, or mechanics that are laborious.  This game has surprised me because i've been getting used to being more disappointed with my game purchases.
Here's why i love it.  It has thick, otherworldly atmosphere driven by incredibly detailed environments and beutiful music.  Open world, extremely non-repetetive map with areas that weave in and out of one another... constantly finding surprises and discovering multiple connections to different zones.  Tons of secrets.
The game encourages you to make thoughtful use of your tools. You have lots of choices as to what you equip, but limiting active ability slots keeps it challenging, and fosters experimentation so it's never boring.
The fighting is great because the controls are tight and the monster movement and attack patterns are interesting and tough for the most part.  The bosses are amazing to look at and to fight.  The characters are mysterious and likeable.  The illustration style is amazing, with beautiful light and particle effects layered in. Its so good.  I can't praise it enough.  If you like video games get it... if you like Super Metroid and the well-crafted Castlevania titles.
I'll add to this review if i find more to complain about, but for now, this is where i'm at, and i'm super happy.

Just plain awesome! I fear that this game is going to be underated and under-played. When Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon tried to take a successful FPS and add a new theme and write in wise-cracks they failed miserably. And where they failed, Shadow warrior succeeds. Characters are well developed and everything just feels right. Lo Wang is admirable with his rapid fire wit and it is going to be a long time before we see another character like this. What makes him understandable and easy to appreciate is that he doesnt take himself seriously at all.
Graphics are nice and none of the levels feel unfinished or rushed (so far-Im only on Chapter 9). The playability factor is pretty incredible. Most veterans of FPS will immediately feel at home in these levels but even the newcomer doesnt have to be intimidated. Anyone who does not play hardcore FPS games usually hesitates when it comes to buying those games and for good reason. But the newcomer does not have to fear Shadow Warrior. By the time you finish the first level the moves are second nature.
My only complaint is that a lot of the levels are fairly dark and they hide a lot of great work that was put into the level design. Luckily you have a flashlight at all times and I find myself having to keep it on. Not sure why they did this. Turning up the brightness or gamma does not really help because then it throws the rest of the colors and lighting off.
The real genius behind Shadow Warrior is that they were able to keep the game focused between sword and gun play and the sword really shines. Any FPS with guns usually only has melee in as an after thought; not much is ever paid attention to it nor does it ever feel like the melee is balanced or even fits in the game. This game makes you want to use youir sword as much as possible. The balancing is truly amazing and shows they didnt just take the task lightly. Bethesda should learn from them if they create a Dishonored 2...as well as countless other publishers.
Overall Score: 9/10 (easily)
Purchase Price: $8.99 (Amazon sale. Would not recomend paying $40 for it but $30 and below is not a bad deal)

I have never loved a game as much as this one in all my time of playing games.  The artwork is wonderfully done, the music is absolutely beautiful.
The game is very well designed, the world, despite not giving you complete freedon to roam immediately due to it's identity as a metroidvania type game, it is not completely linear.  You can find a path through the ruins of the Kingdom of Hallownest in a number of ways depending on the way you play.
The game world is beautifully designed, and the story of the world is not something that's handed to you on a plate, it must be pieced together through the experience of game events and dialogue from the many (well characterized) NPCs that you meet along your journey.
The game also presents a good level of difficulty.  Even if you find the normal mode of playing through the game too easy, there is a permadeath mode which becomes available after your first game completion, which I had a blast playing through.
The design of the secrets in the world is very intuitive, thanks in part to the well designed sound landscape of the game.  There are both breakable walls and nonexistant walls in the game.  The breakable walls are visually different than the normal walls if you pay attention to the surroundings, and the location of nonexistant walls which are obscured by elements in the forground are often easily identifiably.  On top of that, quite a few secrets are findable simply by following sound.  Secrets such as the collectible grubs as well as dropped items have distinct sounds so that you can infer their location and try to find them in a more localized area once you have heard their telltale sound cues.
The boss fights in the game are also a lot of fun, partly due to the tight controls and combat system.  There is also room for you to change your character to find your own combat style due to the charms you can find in the world to augment your abilities.
Overall this game was a wonderful experience, and I'm certainly not ready to put it down yet.  On top of all that, it's only 15$!  Which, in my opinion, is an absolute steal given the massive size of the game world.  It took me about 45 hours in total to complete my first 100% playthrough, and another 40 or so to complete the 100% on the permadeath mode and get all of the achievements.  The fact that I paid 15$ for this experience is frankly absurd, and I would reccommend it to anybody who is a fan of platforming, beautiful art, or just a vast ruined world and story to explore.
I am very glad that I found this wonderful experience.

There's quite a few unfinished games in my Steam library, exponentially larger than games that I have actually competed. I don't know if this is because I don't have enough time anymore to finish games, or if the games haven't really drawn me in enough to pull me away from doing other activities or playing GMod/TF2 with friends, or a combination of both. Despite all of these factors, something about Shadow Warrior made me want to finish the whole thing, and it was surely worth it.
Let's start off with one of the first things you notice as you boot up Shadow Warrior for the first time: The visuals are pretty damn good. Obviously, if your PC contains a good graphics card, chances are that pretty much every game looks fairly good. Luckily for me (and anyone else with a similar GPU), I was able to crank all settings up to their highest at 1080P on my GTX 770 and still get good framerates around 60FPS, although of course at times it was lower, and higher. Running on max settings this game looks really cool, with all particle effects enabled and physics at their finest, you can truly experience this game the way it is meant to be. Usually turning on all the graphics switches to the max doesn't actually benefit gameplay, but since those options are inlcuded in the video settings, I would consider it an aid to gameplay, since the game doesn't feel the same without dismembered demons flying all about. The only times that I had an issue with performance with this game is on the CPU side of things. In my PC, I have an FX-6350 OC'd to 4.4GHz. This may not be the most impressive processor by a long shot, but it is still a fair bit better than the average Steam user, and I believe that it caused low FPS in some areas because in said areas, turning the graphics all the way down to low made no impact on my performance. However, these occurances were not all too common, and I didn't even notice too much in fights because the action is so intense. Just make sure you have a good processor to play this game, as it has been proven that it is very CPU intensive, especially with a bunch of enemies on the screen.
While the visuals are very nice, the gameplay is what makes the game, and in this regard, Shadow Warrior nails it. The main weapon in the game, as you may have guessed, is Lo Wang's katana, and using it just may be the most fun I have ever had with a sword in a video game. Combat is very fast pace and brutal, with no blocking or defense besides an optional power that reduces damage taken (not entirely) and reduces movement speed, so you're going to be sprinting, slashing, and shooting. Speaking of powers, there are a bunch in the game to mix up the hack and slash action, and they are activated in an odd way. You need to tap either W,A,S,or D key twice depending on the power, and then hold left or right mouse click until the power is charged or done channeling. It's strange at first, but you get used to it surprisingly quickly, and looking back at the combat, it seems the most efficient way of doing things. And yes, there are quite a few guns in this game. While I almost always defaulted to my sword to take down my foes, there were a few minor bosses that I was able to defeat more easily with a gun, and on the major bosses the sword isn't even a viable option until the end of the game. Combat is definitely this game's strong suit, and it was executed perfectly.
Finally, we come to the narrative of the game. I will start off by saying while the game has a fairly decent plot, you really should not play it just for the story mode. The generally overview of the story follows Lo Wang on his quest to kill a bunch of demons to stop them from destroying the world, and on the way getting the Nobitsura Kage, the worl'd most powerful sword. The narrative isn't all that compelling, and sometimes I would altogether not have a clue on why I was at a certain area because I was too focused on dicing up demons into tiny pieces, but the story isn't that hard to follow and wraps up pretty nicely in the end. What the narrative does excel at is comedy. There are jokes all over the majority of the game, usually coming from Lo Wang, and quite a few will make you chuckle. Even as the tone of the narrative gets more serious towards the end of the game, you will still find in-game fortune cookies that contain a snarkly line within, the the devs still manage to fit in a quick joke every once in a while.
Overall, Shadow Warrior is a great game. The visuals, while not on the same level as Crysis 3, are still really good, the combat is superb, and the narrative is pretty strong for a hack-n'-slash fighting game and fits in some decent jokes to lighten up the mood. Also, the game lasts pretty long, on normal difficulty it took me around 13 hours to complete while finding as many pickups as I could and exploring the maps fairly thoroughly, and there are more difficulties and a horde mode to enjoy as well. FINAL VERDICT: 8.75/10, a great, gorey game to play, and a must have if you're an action game junkie.

Im not really great at writing detailed reviews (this also being my first!) so i will keep this short and simple - if you like metroidvanias/ 2d platformers then get this game, it is worth every penny they are charging. it looks great, sounds great and plays great.
i have played ALOT of metroidvania games and this would have to be one of the best (ori and salt and sanctuary being my favourites) - the world itself is insanely interesting and detailed and will inspire you to uncover as much of it as possible. the controls are tight and precise and platforming challenges are rewarding and never tedious. the variety of enemies/traps is also decent so far, each requiring a unique strategy to overcome, requiring some thought and patience before each encounter. there is some character progression in the form of new powers (obtained by finding them around the map) and charms (which can be bought at the shop or found around the map), but not so much that you get stuck in menus for extended periods of time like final fantasy, which keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting and adds a nice, comfortable layer of depth.
Some cons:
-no new weapons that i have seen, you only get the nail/sword thing and I've not come across any upgrades for that yet either. I'd like to see a few different types with different abilites and attack animations, or at the very least mods for the base weapon to add new attacks (if they exist forgive me, i guess i just havent uncovered them yet).
-enemies respawn too quickly, i am a huge fan of the dark souls system (which this game has clearly taken inspiration from) where they would only respawn when you rested. this makes exploration much more fun, and makes it less tedious running back through areas youve already been to.
-a stamina system, such as that in salt and sanctuary, would have been nice to add a little more depth and strategy to the combat and exploration.
all in all id rate this 9/10 - the developers have created a beautiful, unique and interesting world that will only encourage you to uncover all of its secrets, which is complimented by some fantastic gameplay. Bottom line: BUY THIS GAME!

Well, with my first playthrough of the game almost complete (missing half a mask, but that's really it, got everything else), I think now is the time to make my review. Now, I could go on for hours about this game and all of its elements, and how well crafted this game is from top to bottom. However, this game is best played through blind. If you're interested in this game, do not, I repeat, DO NOT look up a playthrough or walkthrough of any kind.
This game is all about exploration, in a very similar vain to Legend of Zelda, particularly either the original NES game or the more recent Breath of the Wild. Once you complete the very first section of the game before entering the hub, Dirtmouth, Hollow Knight unties your leash and expects you to figure out everything. That may sound bad on paper, but this game's level design 100% compliments this open nature. If you can reach it, you can go there. Now, there is TECHNICALLY a bit of linearity at the very start when you're expected to get your first movement ability, but aside from that, you are free to go as you please, with the only real limitation of where to go being if you're willing to put in the effort. It does get really hard at some points, but the game is balanced in that you are able to beat the challenges set before you if you know how to play properly. It's never cheap
Hollow Knight is easily the most gorgeous game I've seen in a long time. The hand drawn 2D artstyle really makes the game pop, and there's always something new to look at wherever you go. The soundtrack is also really good, having purchased it myself, and it's one of the few OSTs where I actually enjoy almost every single track, rather than a select few.
My only issue with the game is, as I said, the fact that it's a game best played blind. Once I beat this game, I will never be able to experience this game like I did in my first playthrough, which is saddening to me; my first playthrough of this game was my best experience with any game in years. I'll never forget the fear, happiness, sadness, and dread I felt throughout my first adventure, and it makes me so sad knowing that the game will never feel the same in a future playthrough.
If you're interested in this game, BUY IT! Either on Steam or the upcoming Switch port. Whatever the case, you will NOT regret it! Just PLEASE go in blind; this game will not be as fulfilling if you see a playthrough beforehand.
Its free and takes up no hard drive space, so all you have to loose is your time.

A strong return to form after AC3, Black Flag is the full pirate experience. From exciting ship battles and badass swordplay, Black Flag is as much a pirate game as it is an AC game, but that's for the best. It gives the franchises a much needed shake-up, without sacrificing the mayhem and murder that made AC so fun to begin with. Did I mention the game has a suite of brilliantly performed sea shanties to collect and sing at sea? Trust me, it's a selling point.
Unfortunately, my only lasting criticism of this game is its performance. Despite being an absolute stunner visually, Black Flag suffers from some unfortunate optimisation issues, even months after launch. Good luck getting this thing to run at a solid 60fps with v-sync enabled, even with a high-end rig. The game also takes a huge performance hit with Nvidia exclusive PhysX effects enabled, and they seem barely worth the trouble. A dissapointing blemish on an otherwise fantastic game.

This game is hands down the best Metroidvania I've ever played, nothing even compares. Everything from the smooth punishing combat to the stunning hand painted environments had me in constant glee from the moment I started up the game. How the lore is presented and the goal of the game is very reminiscent of Dark Souls, which made me so much more involved with the story and fate of the game world. The boss fights were all very satisfying, even the easier ones had my praise due to just how animated and unique every fight was. The pacing for unlocking abilities and upgrades felt perfect, and a lot of the things you can find are hidden away or guarded well, so every new upgrade or ability I'd find always made me feel accomplished.
Another big selling point is just how much game there is. The game is bigger then the average Metroidvania, somehow it had both quality and quantity. After my first run of the game, getting the harder ending and acquiring 100% of the items, I had just about 30 hours clocked in to that save. It was more than worth the $15.
Not only is this my favorite Metroidvania of all time, I'd dare say it's my favorite game of all time, or at the very least it's up there. If you can handle difficulty and vagueness not far off from what Dark Souls does, I'd highly recommend this game to you.

A brilliant game that makes me go crazy. The game is endless possibilities and outcomes. Stanley is an office worker who has to discover what happened to his coworkers and why he suddenly feels like a person with emotions and meaning. The narrator pushes the story and makes the game actually quite humourous. As the story goes on, and you either obey or disobey him, different things will happen. The narrator will restart the game. Glitches will happen. The narrator will take you on other games because you just don't happen to like his. It's very creative, and there are so many outcomes and possibilities, I often forget I'm playing "The Stanley Parable". The game is, in its sense, what we do as humans, and some people as gamers. We push buttons mindlessly. The narrator tries to get Stanley (you) to understand he follows orders like a robot, all the while scolding you when you take a wrong turn or push the wrong button. Brilliant concept.

A little bit of mixed feelings for this game but  here goes:
To give an overall feel for the game (in a nutshell) Shadow Warrior 2013 = PainKiller + Hard Reset.  Very old school mob shooter.  Kill the mobs, wait for the big boss, look for secrets, repeat.  Add a few lines of humor and you have Shadow Warrior.  Now I'm really not a fan of that style of shooter but like anything else there are good ones in that genre i.e.: Painkiller.  This game is no PK...but it tries....
Loved the maps, the environment, gritty and very creepy.  Awesome textures, lighting, I thought the game looked great.  I felt like I was playing HardReset with a new paint job.  So similar were the two (same developer of course) had it not been for the weapons SW could almost pass for a HR mod.  Explosions everywhere (like everywhere, anything explodes hence the Hard Reset reference lol)
Awesome.  Lot's of weapons, lots of upgrades, one of my favorite parts of the game.  The sword play is fantastic lol.  Lot's of really cool and interesting moves.  Despite all the heavy weapons it's the Katana that leaves you with that satisfied feeling.
This gets a bit tricky.  Very smooth  FPS, good controls and handling.  However the specialty moves I found to be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to deal with.  On the upside you can build up your skill trees (Weapons, Skills and Powers).  The downside is alot of them get activated using key combos.  I can't tell you what a giant pain in the♥♥♥♥♥that is in the heat of battle.  For one thing there's like 8 different ones and I found myself fumbling and mashing my keyboard to death and many times just not getting the right combos to work.  Also I could'nt figure out any way to customize that part of it.  I feel lucky that I use the standard WSAD layout which is really the best one to use in conjunction with the key combos.  If you're a guy who uses the arrow keys to move around I promise you will have a very difficult time using the key combos.
Also the game was too old school.  Too many boss types that take forever to take down and after awhile it gets old and boring.  You have the medium bosses  that are a bit of a drag and then the big bosses which will take a good 15+ minutes to take down.  Either way there is no weapon or style that takes down the medium bosses right away and absolutely nothing for the big bosses, you have no choice and have to do your time to get through it.  Due to the goofy key combos and high resilience of the the bosses I found it to be more of chore than a challenge, especially in hard mode which was how I played the game.
All in all if it was fun and I do recommend it, however I have to say the fact that I paid a very reduced price for this game allowed for a better review.  Make sure to warm up your fingers, between the many boss fights and kooky key combos you may walk away with slight case of carpal tunnel syndrome.

A little bit of mixed feelings for this game but  here goes:
To give an overall feel for the game (in a nutshell) Shadow Warrior 2013 = PainKiller + Hard Reset.  Very old school mob shooter.  Kill the mobs, wait for the big boss, look for secrets, repeat.  Add a few lines of humor and you have Shadow Warrior.  Now I'm really not a fan of that style of shooter but like anything else there are good ones in that genre i.e.: Painkiller.  This game is no PK...but it tries....
Loved the maps, the environment, gritty and very creepy.  Awesome textures, lighting, I thought the game looked great.  I felt like I was playing HardReset with a new paint job.  So similar were the two (same developer of course) had it not been for the weapons SW could almost pass for a HR mod.  Explosions everywhere (like everywhere, anything explodes hence the Hard Reset reference lol)
Awesome.  Lot's of weapons, lots of upgrades, one of my favorite parts of the game.  The sword play is fantastic lol.  Lot's of really cool and interesting moves.  Despite all the heavy weapons it's the Katana that leaves you with that satisfied feeling.
This gets a bit tricky.  Very smooth  FPS, good controls and handling.  However the specialty moves I found to be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to deal with.  On the upside you can build up your skill trees (Weapons, Skills and Powers).  The downside is alot of them get activated using key combos.  I can't tell you what a giant pain in the♥♥♥♥♥that is in the heat of battle.  For one thing there's like 8 different ones and I found myself fumbling and mashing my keyboard to death and many times just not getting the right combos to work.  Also I could'nt figure out any way to customize that part of it.  I feel lucky that I use the standard WSAD layout which is really the best one to use in conjunction with the key combos.  If you're a guy who uses the arrow keys to move around I promise you will have a very difficult time using the key combos.
Also the game was too old school.  Too many boss types that take forever to take down and after awhile it gets old and boring.  You have the medium bosses  that are a bit of a drag and then the big bosses which will take a good 15+ minutes to take down.  Either way there is no weapon or style that takes down the medium bosses right away and absolutely nothing for the big bosses, you have no choice and have to do your time to get through it.  Due to the goofy key combos and high resilience of the the bosses I found it to be more of chore than a challenge, especially in hard mode which was how I played the game.
All in all if it was fun and I do recommend it, however I have to say the fact that I paid a very reduced price for this game allowed for a better review.  Make sure to warm up your fingers, between the many boss fights and kooky key combos you may walk away with slight case of carpal tunnel syndrome.

I've got 19 hours in and I highly recommend this game.  The experience is as close to Super Metroid as I've ever had in a title like this.  I've been playing games for about 25 years, so at this point i'm super picky with boring formulas, or lazy design, or mechanics that are laborious.  This game has surprised me because i've been getting used to being more disappointed with my game purchases.
Here's why i love it.  It has thick, otherworldly atmosphere driven by incredibly detailed environments and beutiful music.  Open world, extremely non-repetetive map with areas that weave in and out of one another... constantly finding surprises and discovering multiple connections to different zones.  Tons of secrets.
The game encourages you to make thoughtful use of your tools. You have lots of choices as to what you equip, but limiting active ability slots keeps it challenging, and fosters experimentation so it's never boring.
The fighting is great because the controls are tight and the monster movement and attack patterns are interesting and tough for the most part.  The bosses are amazing to look at and to fight.  The characters are mysterious and likeable.  The illustration style is amazing, with beautiful light and particle effects layered in. Its so good.  I can't praise it enough.  If you like video games get it... if you like Super Metroid and the well-crafted Castlevania titles.
I'll add to this review if i find more to complain about, but for now, this is where i'm at, and i'm super happy.

Shadow Warrior is a retro-inspired reboot of the original Shadow Warrior classic from 1997.
Story is pretty well-written for a game of this type.  The humor is light-hearted and witty and avoids being overly immature.  The banter between Lo Wang and Hoji is excellent and the game has enough great "Wang" jokes to fill a book.
The game has a lot of content.  There are 17 large, but linear levels with a good amount of secrets and easter eggs to discover.  The campaign took me roughly 20 hours to complete on normal difficulty.  Once you get through the campaign there are options that open up for an EX playthrough where you get to playthrough again and keep all of your upgrades as well as an Expert playthrough where you start from scratch and get no savepoints mid-level.  There was also a free Survival Mode added in by the developers post-release so there is definitely a lot of value here for the money.
Combat flowed very smooth and was nicely varied.  Shadow Warrior follows a Serious Sam style gameplay where enemies can come in large groups and cover is largely irrelevant.  You get a good number of weapons added to your arsenal as you progress through the game and can carry all of them with you.  The combat also has a fantastic melee element with the katana that you start the game with.  I found the katana to be the main weapon of choice throughout the game, as it seemed a bit overpowered compared to the guns, and the "Kill Bill" style dismemberments and decapitations were very satisfying.
There is also a nice progression and upgrade system that adds even more to the combat system.  You can train skills and obtain KI powers that allow Lo Wang to move faster, heal himself better and gain special combat abilities and special combos.  You can also upgrade each of the games weapons to make them even more effective.
Overall I was surprised at how good this game was.  It managed to sufficiently modernize the classic Shadow Warrior while keeping true to the old-school FPS style gameplay.  In this regard Shadow Warrior was able to accomplish what Duke Nukem Forever was not able to.  If you are a fan of old-school, fast paced FPS action with a satirical sense of humor then I highly recommend this game.

I have never loved a game as much as this one in all my time of playing games.  The artwork is wonderfully done, the music is absolutely beautiful.
The game is very well designed, the world, despite not giving you complete freedon to roam immediately due to it's identity as a metroidvania type game, it is not completely linear.  You can find a path through the ruins of the Kingdom of Hallownest in a number of ways depending on the way you play.
The game world is beautifully designed, and the story of the world is not something that's handed to you on a plate, it must be pieced together through the experience of game events and dialogue from the many (well characterized) NPCs that you meet along your journey.
The game also presents a good level of difficulty.  Even if you find the normal mode of playing through the game too easy, there is a permadeath mode which becomes available after your first game completion, which I had a blast playing through.
The design of the secrets in the world is very intuitive, thanks in part to the well designed sound landscape of the game.  There are both breakable walls and nonexistant walls in the game.  The breakable walls are visually different than the normal walls if you pay attention to the surroundings, and the location of nonexistant walls which are obscured by elements in the forground are often easily identifiably.  On top of that, quite a few secrets are findable simply by following sound.  Secrets such as the collectible grubs as well as dropped items have distinct sounds so that you can infer their location and try to find them in a more localized area once you have heard their telltale sound cues.
The boss fights in the game are also a lot of fun, partly due to the tight controls and combat system.  There is also room for you to change your character to find your own combat style due to the charms you can find in the world to augment your abilities.
Overall this game was a wonderful experience, and I'm certainly not ready to put it down yet.  On top of all that, it's only 15$!  Which, in my opinion, is an absolute steal given the massive size of the game world.  It took me about 45 hours in total to complete my first 100% playthrough, and another 40 or so to complete the 100% on the permadeath mode and get all of the achievements.  The fact that I paid 15$ for this experience is frankly absurd, and I would reccommend it to anybody who is a fan of platforming, beautiful art, or just a vast ruined world and story to explore.
I am very glad that I found this wonderful experience.

Hollow Knight is a Metroidvania game heavily inspired by Dark Souls.  So with that said, know that this game can be very challenging.  I'll keep this review short and spoiler free.
Gameplay - The combat is very fluid in that your melee attacks can be used in 4 directions and are very quick, so you can land precise hits.  Much like Dark Souls, the game can be brutal with enemies/bosses being relentless, as well as platforming challenges you'll face.  In place of souls you'll earn Geo, which you can gain through killing enemies and using the Geo to purchase items/upgrades.  When you die, like in any Souls game, you'll have to go back to where you last died and recover your Geo.  Exploration is a little different than most Metroidvania games.  Although you do have a map system so you can keep track on where you are, the game will not keep track of where you have been, and upon entering a new area, you'll have to find a map to somewhat point you in the right direction, unless you have a good memory.  So, I found myself lost alot, not knowing where or which way to go.  So it will come down to preference here, as there will be alot of backtracking but not remembering where that certain place was that you can now access.  I actually loved it, since it encouraged exploration, and for me, to enjoy the visuals and music.  All in all, very polished gameplay.
Visuals - Absolutely gorgeous.  I believe the visuals where hand drawn, which is incredibly impressive.  Alot of detail went into the environments, each having a different aesthetic and atmosphere.  Animations for enemies/NPCs are fantastic as well.  Not much to say, beautiful game.
Sound/Music - I was blown away by the music, ranging from ambient to just haunting.  The music is beautiful, all that can really be said.
Story - The story isn't laid out in front for you.  Much of the story is fragmented, and you'll have to piece them together through item descriptions, NPCs, other ways to decipher whats going on.  Although vague, overall the story is pretty good.
Content - Lots of hidden stuff for you to find, and sometimes you'll miss it completely if you don't pay attention.
Hollow Knight was a fantastic experience and fun throughout.  I don't have any gripes with the game as I thought all my deaths where completely my fault.  If you're a sucker for Metroidvania games like I am, I implore you to pick up this game.  You won't regret it.

I'll start off by saying I really enjoyed this game. If you like to play by yourself, and with a Wang, this game is for you. This game captures the old school feel well, without trying too hard. Unless you're impatient, this should last you about 15-20 hours minimum.
Lo Wang is a likeable lead character, and his buddy Hoji, while annoying at first, becomes very charming. You may roll your eyes at the start when you meet the two of them, but they quickly grew on me.
The combat in this game is very fluid and full of action. The pacing is simplistic, and straight forward, with lots of secrets to explore if that's what you're interested in. You can upgrade Lo Wang himself, his abilites, and his weapons as well. The guns give you all the basics with a few extras. All the guns can be upgraded with bonus abilities, which adds a little spice to the arsenal, but none of them felt very satisfying to use. Not to say they were bad, just rather plain. The Crossbow is the exception, which I felt was most enjoyable once you upgraded it.
The sword play and health system are notably good IMO. Sword combat is strong and mixes well with the guns, with neither one being obviously better than the other. The health system allows you to regenrate a percentage of your total health using a healing ability, which doesn't stop you from firing your guns or swinging your sword. You can also upgrade your max health, and med kits allow you to heal above your max health giving you some bonus HP.
The difficulty is something I took issue with though. I played on Hard for 99% of the game, and most of it was fairly manageable. It felt like I was playing something that would be considered "Normal" most of the time. Every now and then however, I found myself facing a part that had a huge spike in difficulty. It's not that the game is too hard, it just gets wildly inconsistent in difficulty throughout.
I'd give it a solid 8/10. $40 is a bit much for this game ($20 being my ideal price), especially since it has no multiplayer, no co-op, and it lacks notable replay value. To their credit, they did later put in a free mode called Survival, where you fight endless monsters. Though, without co-op, or any real point to it, it's more of a time waster when you don't have enough time to commit to something else. Still, they added free content, and gives a little more life blood to the game.
That all said, they did a good job with this one, and because of that I am going to check out Hard Reset, and hope they continue to make games.

I'll start off by saying I really enjoyed this game. If you like to play by yourself, and with a Wang, this game is for you. This game captures the old school feel well, without trying too hard. Unless you're impatient, this should last you about 15-20 hours minimum.
Lo Wang is a likeable lead character, and his buddy Hoji, while annoying at first, becomes very charming. You may roll your eyes at the start when you meet the two of them, but they quickly grew on me.
The combat in this game is very fluid and full of action. The pacing is simplistic, and straight forward, with lots of secrets to explore if that's what you're interested in. You can upgrade Lo Wang himself, his abilites, and his weapons as well. The guns give you all the basics with a few extras. All the guns can be upgraded with bonus abilities, which adds a little spice to the arsenal, but none of them felt very satisfying to use. Not to say they were bad, just rather plain. The Crossbow is the exception, which I felt was most enjoyable once you upgraded it.
The sword play and health system are notably good IMO. Sword combat is strong and mixes well with the guns, with neither one being obviously better than the other. The health system allows you to regenrate a percentage of your total health using a healing ability, which doesn't stop you from firing your guns or swinging your sword. You can also upgrade your max health, and med kits allow you to heal above your max health giving you some bonus HP.
The difficulty is something I took issue with though. I played on Hard for 99% of the game, and most of it was fairly manageable. It felt like I was playing something that would be considered "Normal" most of the time. Every now and then however, I found myself facing a part that had a huge spike in difficulty. It's not that the game is too hard, it just gets wildly inconsistent in difficulty throughout.
I'd give it a solid 8/10. $40 is a bit much for this game ($20 being my ideal price), especially since it has no multiplayer, no co-op, and it lacks notable replay value. To their credit, they did later put in a free mode called Survival, where you fight endless monsters. Though, without co-op, or any real point to it, it's more of a time waster when you don't have enough time to commit to something else. Still, they added free content, and gives a little more life blood to the game.
That all said, they did a good job with this one, and because of that I am going to check out Hard Reset, and hope they continue to make games.
