Well it's definately the best Assassin's Creed game to date but has some very bizarre problems.
I'll get the bad stuff out of the way first: the melee combat is horrendous. It relies on the same mechanic that the previous AC games have utilized, aswell as the Arkham series of games, however enemies do not have a "health bar" of sorts, instead your character uses a series of animations which, when finished, will kill the enemy. The trouble with this is that if the animation is interupted for whatever reason, you will have to start all over again with the enemy that you were fighting... and these kill animations can take a looooooooong time to execute. The amount of times I've sliced open and enemy's neck then plunged my sword through his heart only to be struck by another enemy from behind, glitch over scenery or be nudged by an ally, only for the enemy which should be dead just to step back a few paces ready to fight me again just because I didn't get the last part of the animation in before I was interupted, is rediculous.
The guns are cool though and the instant take downs are usually fine, but I try to avoid melee combat when possible because of the reasons above.
As usual the one-button-wonder parkour can be very glitchy at times especially because the same button is held down in order to sprint.
I also find the missions unfuriating at times, especially as many of them involve you tailing a target not to kill them but to eavesdrop on them. As you follow them at close proximity through their merry journey, they often walk through restricted areas and the very second you are spotted you lose the mission and have to start right from the beginning again.
Ubisoft really fancies themselves as portraying their games in a more historically accurate way, but that's only if the fate of the real historical characters can compliment their make believe protagonist. The stories of people such as Black Beard, Captain Kidd and the Gentleman Pirate are sometimes so off course from reality that you wonder why Ubisoft even bothers to make such a claim. Overall, the portrayals are pretty good though, and the voice acting is, for the most part, superb. The main character, Edward Kenway, is a Welsh Pirate, voiced by a real Welshman. Black Beard clearly has a Bristol accent. No dodgy, misplaced American accents covered in a fake cockney accent here just because they got an A-list Hollywood celebrity in to boost the sales. I love it.
The water looks fantastic. The boats handle pretty well and going to and from ship mode and assassin mode is pretty seamless. The world is huge and you will be able to navigate most of the carribean in an open world with plenty to do; some of it good, some not as good, most of it optional. The ship combat is very good, though like anything, it gets repetitive when you have to do it as much as you have to. The story is ok, but being a history aficionado, I find some of the innaccuracies hard to swallow. Over all though, interesting; infact I found myself often jumping from main mission to main mission just to see what happens next.
My verdict on this game is that it is a great game but has some serious, almost unforgivable flaws. Definately worth it as there is plenty to do but if you are anything like me, the good times can sometimes be ruined by terrible ideas and strange events which really shouldn't be there.
To summarize: This game has the best water that I have yet seen in any game. It feels almost real in the way it behaves and moves. The ship combat is good, assassinations are still fun but the missions can be very annoying at times and historical accuracy is way off. There is plenty to do but melee combat is painfully bad and should be avoided whenever possible.
The question I have for this game, is did it really have to be part of the Assassin's Creed franchise? I would have fared better on it's own as a pure game about piracy and because of this suffers from having to fit into a paradigm and could never really reach it's full potential and feels very out of place.
7/10 - Great game and worth the cost, but has some unfuriating problems that I cannot believe made it into release. Through all it's bells and whistles it's a generic Ubisoft game, but definately their best AC yet despite the fact that it would have been better as a stand alone game.

I have never loved a game as much as this one in all my time of playing games.  The artwork is wonderfully done, the music is absolutely beautiful.
The game is very well designed, the world, despite not giving you complete freedon to roam immediately due to it's identity as a metroidvania type game, it is not completely linear.  You can find a path through the ruins of the Kingdom of Hallownest in a number of ways depending on the way you play.
The game world is beautifully designed, and the story of the world is not something that's handed to you on a plate, it must be pieced together through the experience of game events and dialogue from the many (well characterized) NPCs that you meet along your journey.
The game also presents a good level of difficulty.  Even if you find the normal mode of playing through the game too easy, there is a permadeath mode which becomes available after your first game completion, which I had a blast playing through.
The design of the secrets in the world is very intuitive, thanks in part to the well designed sound landscape of the game.  There are both breakable walls and nonexistant walls in the game.  The breakable walls are visually different than the normal walls if you pay attention to the surroundings, and the location of nonexistant walls which are obscured by elements in the forground are often easily identifiably.  On top of that, quite a few secrets are findable simply by following sound.  Secrets such as the collectible grubs as well as dropped items have distinct sounds so that you can infer their location and try to find them in a more localized area once you have heard their telltale sound cues.
The boss fights in the game are also a lot of fun, partly due to the tight controls and combat system.  There is also room for you to change your character to find your own combat style due to the charms you can find in the world to augment your abilities.
Overall this game was a wonderful experience, and I'm certainly not ready to put it down yet.  On top of all that, it's only 15$!  Which, in my opinion, is an absolute steal given the massive size of the game world.  It took me about 45 hours in total to complete my first 100% playthrough, and another 40 or so to complete the 100% on the permadeath mode and get all of the achievements.  The fact that I paid 15$ for this experience is frankly absurd, and I would reccommend it to anybody who is a fan of platforming, beautiful art, or just a vast ruined world and story to explore.
I am very glad that I found this wonderful experience.

Hollow Knight is a Metroidvania game heavily inspired by Dark Souls.  So with that said, know that this game can be very challenging.  I'll keep this review short and spoiler free.
Gameplay - The combat is very fluid in that your melee attacks can be used in 4 directions and are very quick, so you can land precise hits.  Much like Dark Souls, the game can be brutal with enemies/bosses being relentless, as well as platforming challenges you'll face.  In place of souls you'll earn Geo, which you can gain through killing enemies and using the Geo to purchase items/upgrades.  When you die, like in any Souls game, you'll have to go back to where you last died and recover your Geo.  Exploration is a little different than most Metroidvania games.  Although you do have a map system so you can keep track on where you are, the game will not keep track of where you have been, and upon entering a new area, you'll have to find a map to somewhat point you in the right direction, unless you have a good memory.  So, I found myself lost alot, not knowing where or which way to go.  So it will come down to preference here, as there will be alot of backtracking but not remembering where that certain place was that you can now access.  I actually loved it, since it encouraged exploration, and for me, to enjoy the visuals and music.  All in all, very polished gameplay.
Visuals - Absolutely gorgeous.  I believe the visuals where hand drawn, which is incredibly impressive.  Alot of detail went into the environments, each having a different aesthetic and atmosphere.  Animations for enemies/NPCs are fantastic as well.  Not much to say, beautiful game.
Sound/Music - I was blown away by the music, ranging from ambient to just haunting.  The music is beautiful, all that can really be said.
Story - The story isn't laid out in front for you.  Much of the story is fragmented, and you'll have to piece them together through item descriptions, NPCs, other ways to decipher whats going on.  Although vague, overall the story is pretty good.
Content - Lots of hidden stuff for you to find, and sometimes you'll miss it completely if you don't pay attention.
Hollow Knight was a fantastic experience and fun throughout.  I don't have any gripes with the game as I thought all my deaths where completely my fault.  If you're a sucker for Metroidvania games like I am, I implore you to pick up this game.  You won't regret it.

Shadow Warrior is said to be a remake of the 1997 game, but in reality it's something completely unreal in its infinite awesomeness. It resembles the Serious Sam 3, Bulletstorm and Hard Reset games a lot, however this one is something much more, as it took what was good in previous games and removed what wasn't really working out and blended it into this masterpiece.
The first thing that stands out is the katana, as none of those games had a deep melee combat system, seeing something this polished and advanced, gives you ability to vary your playstyle and experiment with diffirent abilities of your character, you can use quick slashes, charged attacks, special moves like 360 spin with a blade or energy wave slash and mix it with secondary abilites such as healing, creating force shield or stun, you can even throw shurikens without changing weapons!
At first the other weapons seem to be not as fun, but every single of them can get 3-4 upgrades turning them into serious death machines. With explosive shots in the bigger groups or automatic rains of fire at the distant enemies, you should always be able to handle diffirent situations. Also, the accurate revolver or crossbow can easily destroy barrels, electric fans (which bursts into clouds of thunders, electrocuting everyone in their range. HILARIOUS!),cars or scooters to deal enviromental damage without wasting explosive ammo. Possibilities are many, and nearly always fun ( Note:don't dash from the stairs ).
Enemies too are varied, simple rushing demons, shooting ones, flying ones, shielded ones, kamikaze ones+ 3 tougher minibosses: a necromancer summoning skeletons, a tank who enrages the minions and a ram, who can only be damaged from his back. All require diffirent approach, especially on higher difficulties, where you tend to be punished for your mistakes. Big bosses though were a bit repetitive in my opinion, as you just shoot at their weak spots till they drop, bleh.
Surprisingly, this game also has a plot and even more of a surprise-this plot is pretty good. We play as a mercenary with a peculiar name Lo Wang, hired by some millionaire who wants to get a sword of the demons, as expected- everything goes wrong: you are caught, the blade is lost and on top of that, world is now attacked by hordes of demons. One of those demons however appears not hostile, yet extremely rude. Now as a charming companion talking inside your head, he tells you about the realm of the demons, allowing you to understand why exactly are they on earth and what does it have to do with the sword you've lost. Thanks to him the game is filled with pretty humorous argues betwen him and the protagonist, many times containing references to the popculture.
Level design is truly genious, it's full of secrets, boxes with loot (ammo or money for upgrading weapons) and fortune cookies, containing short jokes for your reading pleasure. And they are not some boring labs or generic hallways, they are mainly open areas, with lakes, bamboo and cherry trees, statues, palaces, lanterns, bridges or even waterfalls. The graphics are beautiful and worked with decent fps on high settings, while running on windows xp. Thats right! This game IMO looks just as good as bf3 and works on dx9 without any graphical features lost.

3 out of 5 for the genre.
The Bad
-The game reaks of tediousness. The compass showing where you are on the map that metroid for nes had is somehow a special feature and basically sacrifice an equipment slot to have it. Removing features like maps (gotta find conifer first and hope you came in the easy way even though thier is no indication of it),  map position, a  true fast travel system (stags are better than nothing but certain places you have to hoof it a far way); doesnt make the game hard it makes it annoying.
-You NEED a map/guide.( I used a map after playing the game about 15+ hours because i was just not figuring out where i needed to go) I beat certain bosses without abilities that if i would have had them at the time of the fight would have made them a ton easier (aka double jump). The lack of directions or even knowing where certain nesccary abilities are can make the game frustrating when you are trying to beat certain areas. With the lack of directions or clues to certain items you will almost likly never figure them out on your own (cough mushroom cough). Hive and Hiveblood are pladces and items that if the player is not paying close attention in one vertical leap area they will most likely never encounter that area.
-Visabilty. I know I know that this game gets the OMG its pretty award but places like deepnest were more difficult because half the screen can't be seen. In a platforming game where you need close to super meat boy precision you cannot have fuzzy, or unseen obstacles. (looking at you white palace those saw blades are close in color to the background and it makes it hard to judge exactly where you need to be also the forground will sometimes put images overtop of the charector and landscape making items unseen or atleast muddeling up the veiw). As I was looking at this review before positng I mean come on the head is the part of the Playable Charector that typically gets hit and the head it white, background white, blade white. Contrast is needed in some of these areas. Also platforms in certain areas where also obscured by how they looked in perspective to the background or foreground.
-OPTIMIZATION. I have no clue how a 2d sidescrooling game is having a pleathera of stuttering and lagging issues but the hitch in the water is getting rediculous. Failed champion is impossible due to the fact that I lose half a second when he does special moves. Getting hit also causes stuttering (which ends up making me lose mulitple hearts for one mistake). When certain creatures die thier animation also slows the game. opening the map when you have a high completion rate can slow down or crash the game. when certian minions enter the arena the stutering can happen. any new kill or completion of the hunter journal causes lag.
The Good
-Some of the boss fights are very well done, fun, intricate, and rewarding when you beat them.
-The controlls and platforming are solid with the exceptions of lag or stuttering
-The game does provide a good atmosphere (deepnest did feel creepy)
-Once you know where you need to go the game does have good flow and the platforming can be very smooth
Final thoughts
Personally I would buy the game once it goes on sale. By then it should have it optimization issues fixed and most likly dealt with some of the tediousness.

Shadow Warrior is a reimagining of the classic first person shooter by 3D Realms in 1997. The Story is a prequel to the original game. You play as Lo Wang who is ordered by his boss Orochi Zilla to get a sword known as the Nobitsura Kage. However obtaining this sword is easier said than done since you attacked by an assortment of demons on your journey. You are helped along the way by a demon named Hoji who tells you the sword is capable of slaying immortals and is anathema to demons. The dialogue between both Lo Wang and Hoji is extremely good and makes a lot of references to certain films and video games. The story is ok but nothing to brag about, it keeps the game going whilst telling a few jokes but it’s mostly forgettable.
If you were expecting it to be an old school shooter then you aren’t going to find this game. Instead you go from arena to arena fighting enemies and being scored. It can be more easily compared to Painkiller than any other franchise. You have a choice of nine weapons. Some make their return from the original game such as the sword and sub machinegun and some new weapons such as the crossbow and a double barrel shotgun. The sword is the best weapon in the game since it’s extremely responsive, visceral, powerful and just plain fun to use. The guns, whilst feeling underpowered at first do hold themselves up one you upgrade them by using the in-game currency which is just known as ‘money’.  The upgrades vary from giving you a larger magazine size too having awesome ones like upgrading your double barrel shotgun into a quad barrel shotgun. There are also certain skills you can acquire to give you more health, money, ammo, a new weapon, new moves with your sword and many more. Finally there are four powers in the games which vary such as healing two thirds of your hp, knocking enemies back, launching enemies into the air and making a shield to protect yourself. Each power can be upgraded to make them more useful in combat.
The enemies in the game vary from demons running at you and attacking you, protecting themselves with shields whilst shooting fireballs, flying in the air whilst shooting fireballs, rolling green goo and have it explode in your face and many more. You can also pick up body parts from demons such as their hearts which kill some of the enemies which surround you. There are also human enemies too but there extremely weak and don’t become a real threat until the last few chapters in the game.
The graphics are pretty good, there are a lot of different locations such as small towns too snowy mountains which all look great. The atmosphere and lighting effects are good throughout each level and fit the overall theme of the game.
Shadow Warrior is an extremely good game. Sure it doesn’t have a very good story and it’s not old school either but the gameplay keeps you engaged and makes you want to carry on playing the game. Highly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of first person shooters.

Hollow knight is a very well-drawn 2d metroidvania, with solid combat mechanics, an interesting and mysterious story, bunches of collectables, atmospheric music, and enough challenge to keep people coming back to it.
Full disclosure: I was part of the kickstarter, one of the low-tier backers. But I can honestly say now that I regret giving such a small amount.
I thoroughly enjoyed the experience of Hollow Knight, and I'm currently enjoying the various challenges it has to offer. The extra modes, as well as hidden bosses and optional content, is a treasure trove of interesting content and difficult challenges. Piecing the story together was also quite fun- don't spoil it for yourself!
At heart, the game is one of pure discovery. Exploring the dead lands of Hallownest, asking questions, and perhaps even finding the answers. It's a game of interest, curiosity, and a somber setting. The art, which is gorgeous and dreary and occasionally sinister, will captivate you. The atmosphere will draw you in. The battles will keep you engaged, and the scenery will keep you on your toes. You explore, not to accomplish some arbitrary goal, but to see what there is to see, and find your own reasons to continue.
That's not to say that Hollow Knight is perfect, though. As of right now, there are some framerate issues (that have been mercifully minor) as well as a few- heh- bugs. But as it stands, the majesty of the experience far outweighs the small annoyances, and the developers have been hacking away at the problem since launch. Even as it is now, it's well worth the money.

Over all this game is a fun experience and if you ever see it on sale its a no brainier to pick up.

Hollow Knight was a complete surprise for me. I had never even heard of it till it released and showed up on the front page of the store. What I got was a Metroidvania with a truly beautiful hand drawn 2D style that's reminiscent of Tim Burton's works and a similar but different take on the 'creepy cute' look that The Binding of Isaac has. The game draws inspiration from the Souls series with its bleak atmosphere, vague lore, take on death, and an utterly MASSIVE interconnected world, complete with a fascinating bunch of...bugs. Yes, the theme is bugs. Notice I said bugs instead of insects because like any good creepy game, there needs to be arachnids and the design all works superbly well. Christopher Larkin's score acts as the perfect accompaniment to this dreary and haunting world.
If that wasn't enough, the animation is fluid and dynamic, whether it's the excellent traversal options when platforming or the tons of enemy types from the polished combat. My favorite thing, however, is the exploration. I reiterate, Hollow Knight is a huge sprawling game and you'll definitely need a map or two. There's something deeply satisfying about going whichever way you want in the world and then acting as your own cartographer as you venture ever further...and venture you will. The world is as rich in content as its charm and character.
Now you could make the argument that Hollow Knight isn't wholly original and you wouldn't really be wrong. Its influences are obvious but the game is so well done and polished that it stands out, despite its need or want of innovation. Technically, the game can stutter some, although in the some 40 hours I've played, the hitches might have cost me one full life total, if that. Hollow Knight, where do you even start with a game like this?
Every now and then, a game comes along that has been designed from the heart. Every aspect lovingly crafted, every encounter carefully planned, the sort of game where in the moment to moment gameplay, you can feel the amount of work, effort and painstaking care that was poured into creating such an amazing piece of art.
Hollow Knight is one of those games.
I can say with absolute honesty that Hollow Knight didn't just grab my attention, it stole it. As someone who followed the development of the game from a distance, to actually play for myself was a surreal experience, and even going in with expectations set from what I'd seen, Hollow Knight absolutely floored me.
Firstly, the artstyle and worldbuilding is absolutely gorgeous, though that doesn't do it justice. The amount of subtle details that go into every single environment is phenomenal. Each area feels like its own world, and though some do borrow from the same gloomy theme, the design of each individual area is unique enough to keep the adventure feeling fresh.
The game design also does a stellar job of making you feel both completely lost and absolutely driven at the same time - There's no one to guide you, no waypoints or directions, you're cast down into the world of Hollow Knight with nothing but a battered old nail and your wits, yet the world design urges you in certain directions, introduces you to details about the world that cleverly embed themselves in your mind, giving you reason to return later. Nothing about Hollow Knight feels forced, the adventure is purely in your hands, which is one of the game's best points.
But what's a world without sound? Hollow Knight's sound design, from the pitter-patter of tiny legs to the sweeping strikes of your nail, everything sounds vividly real. You might not pay much heed to the sound of that lamp-post that unfortunately stood between you and that shambling Husk as it clanks to the ground, but it adds so much to the world. As for the soundtrack, it's utterly entrancing. Every moment is arranged in such a way that it accentuates the gameplay flawelessly. Combat feels so much more visceral when the music reacts to how dangerous a moment you're in, creating tension and a sense of rush that the game would sorely miss otherwise.
The flow of Hollow Knight's combat is equally impressive. With only one weapon, you'd be forgiven for assuming that the combat boils down to 'slash the enemy until it stops moving', but the true beauty stems from its simplicity. Almost each and every enemy that stands between you and your goal has to be dealt with in its own unique way, and while some enemies share similar traits, each has at least one aspect that sets them apart from the rest. and that's just the basic mooks.
Boss fights in Hollow Knight, with the exception of one or two, feel perfectly balanced. A lot of work has gone into ensuring that these fights end with the player feeling that there's something they can do better, that the fight wasn't lost due to cheap mechanics or a lack of control. In fact, every single boss in Hollow Knight can be defeated without using a single movement ability, with the exception of one.
If I had more time to plan out this review, (Which has been a purely off-the-cuff opinion spurred after glancing through Steam's page for Hollow Knight and remembering that reviews actually exist), I'm sure there's more that I could write about and harp over. Hollow Knight is a simple game at its core, but absolutely more than the sum of its parts, and for $15, it's an ridiculously, positively insanely low price. I'd have paid $40 for this game, maybe even more. It's criminal that this game is so cheap!
My one sole complaint, and this could be more a personal hardware issue than a game flaw, is the presence of occasional hitches and stutters during gameplay. Uncommon as they may be, they always seemed to occur at inopportune times.
tl;dr, if you're a fan of metroidvania games, you're doing yourself a horrendous disservice by not at least giving this game a shot. It's about 30 hours long to boot!

Watching the Assasin's Creed franchise evolve has been quite a ride. The first game was an interesting new IP that never quite hit the mark due to some uninspired design-choices that cause a lot of mundane repetition. The second game was the most excellent kind of sequel: the kind that refines the great parts, abandones the bad ones, progresses the storyline and is a little better than the sum of its parts. Since AC2, I have loved the universe UbiSoft has created with these games.
After having put Ezio to bed with AC:Revelations, we moved across an ocean in AC3 and saw the United States in its infancy through the eyes of Connor. Not since the release of Ocarina of Time for my Nintendo 64 in 1998 had I been as hyped for a game - and unfortunately, I found it deeply flawed. I won't go into the main reasons here, but I pretty much decided I was done with the franchise. AC4:Black Flag was not something I was interested in trying.
And then it was featured in one of Steams' legendary sales. I picked it up on a whim, and was blown away. For action/RPG fans with a penach for exploring, Black Flag is the ultimate pirate-game. Exploring a vast region of sea and land with your crew is a delight, and I couldn't stop scavanging until my ship was loaded with booty. The storyline takes a HUGE upturn from the (rather dreary) Desmond-focused narrative of past games, and it is all the better for it.
My only regret is that the game might be a little too rooted in its Assassin's Creed framwork. The engine, the setting, the experience would not have been diminished if it was presented as a whole new IP with no attachment to AC. In fact, the AC-brand might be the only thing holding it back, since it might keep some people from jumping in for fear of missing out on the story so far. Hopefully UbiSoft finds a way to reuse some of its assets for a whole new Pirate-adventure IP free from the conflict of Assassins vs Templars.
Until then; Hoist the sails, load the cannons and sharpen your sword for a great adventure that stands amongst the best the franchise has ever been.

It's like a MOBA in that it's a top down, you select a hero, and you fight other heroes. But:
- There's no point and click abilities.
- Your "autoattacks" are also skillshots.
- Almost every ability that has a cooldown is situational.
- There is no RNG elements to the gameplay.
- Fog of war vision is not shared between allies.
- Killing the enemy team is the only way to win the game.
- There's no grinding for gear
- There's nothing you can unlock outside of game that makes the game easier.
- If you lose a large amount of health it's difficult to regain all of it.
- You control your character with WASD
These are not pros or cons, these are just the facts. If you enjoy most of the above you might enjoy this game.
Moving on to my opinions on the game.
Pros:
- I consider almost everything in the above list to be a positive.
- Almost every character is considered viable.
- 20 bucks unlocks every character forever right now.
- It will be going free to play.
Before I move on to cons keep in mind that some of these are only because it happens to be in Early Access.
Cons:
- Character balance is out of wack. As of writing this Poloma is considered undeniably strong and Rook is considered weak.
- Once it goes free to play we don't know if a similar pack for all the characters will be available.
- The rating system used is not the greatest, there are even screenshots floating around of people losing rank despite winning the game.
- The lobby UI needs a lot of work.
- There is no unranked matchmaking queue.
- 2v2 and 3v3 share a rating.

After some tweaking this game runs wonderful, at a solid 60fps. This game is just gorgeous. Man, rarely have I witnessed such a beautiful game. The water, the islands, the details. You have to see it in motion to truly appreciate it. Some of the faces, on the other hand, still need some work. Graphically speaking these are still the weakest, just like all the previous AC games.
I think anyone has played an AC game before so they need no explanation as far as gameplay is concerned. There have been some changes this time, in a positive way. First, there's the sea, it's open for exploration right from the beginning (some (side) missions have to be unlocked first though, like diving). And second, the Abstergo/real life missions are short, which is a big improvement (I'd still like to see it entirely removed, however).
Black Flag is a huge game. Completing the story will take roughly 20-25 hours I think and doing literally everything can take anywhere between 75-100 hours. It is
big. And it's all very fun to do as well, partially thanks to the sunny setting which absolutely brightened my mood on dark, cloudy days. I wish I had the time to 100% it but my priorities are a bit different in comparison to most of the other gamers out there (I like to finish as many games as possible).
Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag is back after the mediocre ACIII and it's bigger and better than ever. I thought I was done with the franchise after the last couple of games but if Unity can even match this one I'll gladly take back those words.

The Stanley Parable (2013) is a Source game based off the original 2011 mod release. Just like its predecessor, you play as Stanley in a world where you're, to put it bluntly, trying to figure out what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on.
A lot of content was added since the 2011 release. More endings, smoother graphics, and the narrator is overall more clever than ever. You can spend endless hours in this game trying to find every single possible ending.
This is a game where you can see the full extent of your decisions. And some of them are quite terrifying in concept.
Overall, The Stanley Parable is an excellent title, although short. It is worth a full price purchase of $15, and definitely worth a buy if it is on sale.
The only flaw this game has is that some endings feel very unsatisfying and empty. It is kind of disappointing that at some points of the endings, your choice isn't allowed any more. This can take from the game and leave you wondering more what if's. This aside, it is a solid release.
Pros:
-> Great dialogue, thanks to the narrator's witty writing.
-> Runs on The Source Engine and will run amazing on pretty much any hardware, no matter the date.
-> Very thought-provoking endings.
-> Nice detail.
-> Has decent replay ability, for the dialogue and so you can see how far your choices can reach.
Cons:
-> Short. Expect to put around 10 hours into this game.
-> Some endings feel empty.
-> Player choice sometimes feels like it was forgotten about in some endings.

Hollow Knight was a complete surprise for me. I had never even heard of it till it released and showed up on the front page of the store. What I got was a Metroidvania with a truly beautiful hand drawn 2D style that's reminiscent of Tim Burton's works and a similar but different take on the 'creepy cute' look that The Binding of Isaac has. The game draws inspiration from the Souls series with its bleak atmosphere, vague lore, take on death, and an utterly MASSIVE interconnected world, complete with a fascinating bunch of...bugs. Yes, the theme is bugs. Notice I said bugs instead of insects because like any good creepy game, there needs to be arachnids and the design all works superbly well. Christopher Larkin's score acts as the perfect accompaniment to this dreary and haunting world.
If that wasn't enough, the animation is fluid and dynamic, whether it's the excellent traversal options when platforming or the tons of enemy types from the polished combat. My favorite thing, however, is the exploration. I reiterate, Hollow Knight is a huge sprawling game and you'll definitely need a map or two. There's something deeply satisfying about going whichever way you want in the world and then acting as your own cartographer as you venture ever further...and venture you will. The world is as rich in content as its charm and character.
Now you could make the argument that Hollow Knight isn't wholly original and you wouldn't really be wrong. Its influences are obvious but the game is so well done and polished that it stands out, despite its need or want of innovation. Technically, the game can stutter some, although in the some 40 hours I've played, the hitches might have cost me one full life total, if that. There are ongoing patches for the performance and the like but it wasn't something I considered problematic or detrimental to the experience.
Hollow Knight snuck up on me and it is simply my favorite of its genre that I've ever played. In a year that has already had some fantastic quality in gaming so far, Hollow Knight rises above.

Hollow Knight, where do you even start with a game like this?
Every now and then, a game comes along that has been designed from the heart. Every aspect lovingly crafted, every encounter carefully planned, the sort of game where in the moment to moment gameplay, you can feel the amount of work, effort and painstaking care that was poured into creating such an amazing piece of art.
Hollow Knight is one of those games.
I can say with absolute honesty that Hollow Knight didn't just grab my attention, it stole it. As someone who followed the development of the game from a distance, to actually play for myself was a surreal experience, and even going in with expectations set from what I'd seen, Hollow Knight absolutely floored me.
Firstly, the artstyle and worldbuilding is absolutely gorgeous, though that doesn't do it justice. The amount of subtle details that go into every single environment is phenomenal. Each area feels like its own world, and though some do borrow from the same gloomy theme, the design of each individual area is unique enough to keep the adventure feeling fresh.
The game design also does a stellar job of making you feel both completely lost and absolutely driven at the same time - There's no one to guide you, no waypoints or directions, you're cast down into the world of Hollow Knight with nothing but a battered old nail and your wits, yet the world design urges you in certain directions, introduces you to details about the world that cleverly embed themselves in your mind, giving you reason to return later. Nothing about Hollow Knight feels forced, the adventure is purely in your hands, which is one of the game's best points.
But what's a world without sound? Hollow Knight's sound design, from the pitter-patter of tiny legs to the sweeping strikes of your nail, everything sounds vividly real. You might not pay much heed to the sound of that lamp-post that unfortunately stood between you and that shambling Husk as it clanks to the ground, but it adds so much to the world. As for the soundtrack, it's utterly entrancing. Every moment is arranged in such a way that it accentuates the gameplay flawelessly. Combat feels so much more visceral when the music reacts to how dangerous a moment you're in, creating tension and a sense of rush that the game would sorely miss otherwise.
The flow of Hollow Knight's combat is equally impressive. With only one weapon, you'd be forgiven for assuming that the combat boils down to 'slash the enemy until it stops moving', but the true beauty stems from its simplicity. Almost each and every enemy that stands between you and your goal has to be dealt with in its own unique way, and while some enemies share similar traits, each has at least one aspect that sets them apart from the rest. and that's just the basic mooks.
Boss fights in Hollow Knight, with the exception of one or two, feel perfectly balanced. A lot of work has gone into ensuring that these fights end with the player feeling that there's something they can do better, that the fight wasn't lost due to cheap mechanics or a lack of control. In fact, every single boss in Hollow Knight can be defeated without using a single movement ability, with the exception of one.
If I had more time to plan out this review, (Which has been a purely off-the-cuff opinion spurred after glancing through Steam's page for Hollow Knight and remembering that reviews actually exist), I'm sure there's more that I could write about and harp over. Hollow Knight is a simple game at its core, but absolutely more than the sum of its parts, and for $15, it's an ridiculously, positively insanely low price. I'd have paid $40 for this game, maybe even more. It's criminal that this game is so cheap!
My one sole complaint, and this could be more a personal hardware issue than a game flaw, is the presence of occasional hitches and stutters during gameplay. Uncommon as they may be, they always seemed to occur at inopportune times.
tl;dr, if you're a fan of metroidvania games, you're doing yourself a horrendous disservice by not at least giving this game a shot. It's about 30 hours long to boot!

It's like a MOBA in that it's a top down, you select a hero, and you fight other heroes. But:
- There's no point and click abilities.
- Your "autoattacks" are also skillshots.
- Almost every ability that has a cooldown is situational.
- There is no RNG elements to the gameplay.
- Fog of war vision is not shared between allies.
- Killing the enemy team is the only way to win the game.
- There's no grinding for gear
- There's nothing you can unlock outside of game that makes the game easier.
- If you lose a large amount of health it's difficult to regain all of it.
- You control your character with WASD
These are not pros or cons, these are just the facts. If you enjoy most of the above you might enjoy this game.
Moving on to my opinions on the game.
Pros:
- I consider almost everything in the above list to be a positive.
- Almost every character is considered viable.
- 20 bucks unlocks every character forever right now.
- It will be going free to play.
Before I move on to cons keep in mind that some of these are only because it happens to be in Early Access.
Cons:
- Character balance is out of wack. As of writing this Poloma is considered undeniably strong and Rook is considered weak.
- Once it goes free to play we don't know if a similar pack for all the characters will be available.
- The rating system used is not the greatest, there are even screenshots floating around of people losing rank despite winning the game.
- The lobby UI needs a lot of work.
- There is no unranked matchmaking queue.
- 2v2 and 3v3 share a rating.

Hollow knight is a very well-drawn 2d metroidvania, with solid combat mechanics, an interesting and mysterious story, bunches of collectables, atmospheric music, and enough challenge to keep people coming back to it.
Full disclosure: I was part of the kickstarter, one of the low-tier backers. But I can honestly say now that I regret giving such a small amount.
I thoroughly enjoyed the experience of Hollow Knight, and I'm currently enjoying the various challenges it has to offer. The extra modes, as well as hidden bosses and optional content, is a treasure trove of interesting content and difficult challenges. Piecing the story together was also quite fun- don't spoil it for yourself!
At heart, the game is one of pure discovery. Exploring the dead lands of Hallownest, asking questions, and perhaps even finding the answers. It's a game of interest, curiosity, and a somber setting. The art, which is gorgeous and dreary and occasionally sinister, will captivate you. The atmosphere will draw you in. The battles will keep you engaged, and the scenery will keep you on your toes. You explore, not to accomplish some arbitrary goal, but to see what there is to see, and find your own reasons to continue.
That's not to say that Hollow Knight is perfect, though. As of right now, there are some framerate issues (that have been mercifully minor) as well as a few- heh- bugs. But as it stands, the majesty of the experience far outweighs the small annoyances, and the developers have been hacking away at the problem since launch. Even as it is now, it's well worth the money.

I was initially rather skeptical with AC4, especially after playing AC3 which I did not particularly like. Well, AC4 Black Flag changes all that. From the first moment of the game, players are immersed in a wide open area (the sea basically). Several notable things are the vastness of the areas to explore, the cities, the oceans, the forts, the missions, etc. I spent about 60 hours completing the main storyline, plus accumulating the Mayan and Templar outfit, and also upgrading the Jackdaw.
What differentiates AC4 from its predecessor is that players need to upgrade Jackdaw as much as the main character (sometimes more of Jackdaw than the main character). However, just a minus for me is that, there are too many distractions between main missions, although.... all those are pretty rewarding as well.
Storyline is also rather interesting. Players get to see Edward develop, in both character and personality so I think that's interesting. Control is smooth and easy to understand.
Overall, Ubisoft has done a great job in building the details of this game. For both the universe of Edward Kenway as well as the real life character we are playing. The details are just stunning and rather interesting, especially when players get to see Assassin's Creed stuff on the work table. Lastly, while sailing or exploring large open areas can be boring/ monotonous at times, the pirates songs are pretty nice and keep players company on those long voyage. I haven't even fully beaten this game (I just got to a fairly pivitol point in the story) and I've put over 20 hours into it. This game is MASSIVE! It features charming and well done hand drawn art. This game is considered part of the "Metroidvania" genre of gaming. This game will give you tons of hours of enjoyment exploring the world created by people who obviously put amazing amounts of detail into each area. Just when you think you've discovered it all... BAM! New areas just pop up in your face!
The games cast of NPC's are all very diverse and intriguing, and the story itself, while not having finished it yet, is very interesting and rather deep. The lore will keep you immersed along with the fantastic enviroments and beautiful music and ambience.
The best thing is this game doesn't hold your hand. It teaches you the basics and helps you learn through enemy placements and level design, each area progressively becoming more difficult where you put what you learned from previous areas to the test. There are upgrades that do allow you to go to certain areas, but for the most part you're totally free to explore the world without any overbearing narrative or waypoints. You're given total control on where you want to go. There's even ways to sequence break with enough skill and resourcefulness.
It feels like a bit of Dark Souls mixed in with Metroidvania and the entire package is just amazing. I can't praise this game enough. It's not that it does anything new to the Metroidvania genre, but there are some things that aren't seen or done as often. What really makes the game is the immersion. It's like the classic Metroid for the NES and Super Metroid on the SNES. It takes the best attributes of the genre with a unique penatly system for dying that isn't too brutal or too easy, much like Dark Souls.
The bosses all have patterns you can learn, and are designed very well. One boss fight in particular was incredible with how it teaches you the fight. There are tons of enemies and things to find and collect. You can find and buy charms that enhance your abililties, such as increased melee range, less soul energy spent for magic spells and even one that makes you smell like dung! (Not joking it's actually useful too)
Honestly if you love Metroidvania and exploration and deep immersion, I highly reccomend playing this game. It's price of 14.99 with this level of depth and content is almost a steal. It's so cheap and it offers a deeper experience then games that cost twice as much! Seriously though, give it a try. You can always refund it if it doesn't turn out to be your cup of tea after all, but if you love adventure and Metroidvania, you won't be dissapointed.

I have never reviewed a game before but I followed Hollow Knight for a month before release because I saw the trailer that made me think of rogue legacy, but this is a metroidvania not a rogue like and I am in love. Some say "Oh joyous day another 2D metroidvania just what we need"...but WAIT. It is not just another clone and here's why.
Art and Atmosphere 5/5
PROS:
The hand drawn art already makes it fantasticly unique, but pleasant voices added to characters and enemies is a plus. The atmospheric elements from the backgrounds and foregrounds with colors and hints of symbolism make you feel connected to the character in each area as if it were the first time exploring. Then the wonderful orchestrated music always chips in to give you all the more reason to brave the new pathways in the good times and bad times.
CONS:
The parallax scrolling in Unity is glitchy at times but only noticeable in tiny corners of caves where a layer is clipping through another and only identifiable by a player with an eagle eye. The thick borders around characters make them look as if they were nothing special of hand drawn compared to pencil and paper look and feel, but it is easily forgivable knowing it helps them stand out among the borderless background and foreground. The concept art for this game is amazing, and you should check it.
Replayability and Length 4.5/5
PROS:
This game is LONG so be prepared for countless hours to be sunk, and it is highly replayable because there is enough content to make each playthrough vastly different. To achieve 100% takes the amount of time as 1/2 of the main storyline, which already alone takes an extremely long time to finish ~30 hours for me. I have been playing for two weeks now many hours each day. I saw vastly different zones and that drew me in hoping to uncover some sort of mystery in each area. The map is huge and you are may finish the game without ever visiting awesome areas if you don't explore enough, and the game is best when you play blindly without looking up the map online.

CONS:
There is a lot of backtracking that can be forgivable however because there are elements that change throughout each area when you go back to revisit different zones. Certain characters might be in zones you have once visited or change their dialogue once you progress further in the story and they tend to provide subtle clues and additions to the storyline. The map serves as a huge element to this game, so after you know where everything is, you can expect your desire to play the game over again to diminish. This is why you do not look up the map and where to go next because spoilers will kill this game. Also the abscense of unlockable characters to play as is slightly more dissapointing seeing as some characters look so fun to play as and would make replaying so much more worth.
Gameplay 4/5 (Platforming and Mechanics)
PROS:
This is what I have been looking for after playing Dark Souls and Nioh because I am addicted to punishing yet rewarding gameplay with the beautiful atmosphere and storyline that is introduced through gameplay and subtle atmospheric elements by exploration. Another great aspect, exploration is highly rewarded in this game as expected of a metroidvania. The learning curve is like that of dark souls, whereas you are given a poopy starter kit and combat relies on sheer skill but as you collect currency in the form of geo you have the option to upgrade your equip and abilities. And as you learn the art of the nail, your weapon, with upgraded equipment, spells, and a gemcraft-like charm system that give you unique bonuses and abilities combat skill will pay off against tougher enemies. The game does a fantastic job teaching you how to conquer hard enemies without pointing it out so obviously. Also...I bought this game soul-ely :-) for the bosses because I am a fanatic for epic boss battles, and I was not dissapointed. There are over 30 boss fights with uniquely voiced enemies and each one vastly unique in making you play the dodge-hit-dodge mechanic game. This game's platforming is also a breath of fresh air...to master the 2D mechanics of platforming once again clenching my butt cheeks like I did many years ago playing Super Mario Bros with highly rewarding hidden items at the end of the hard platforming courses. Many new skills you obtain constantly introduces new platforming challenges in areas, but each area is well designed to help you master each new skill and there are many opportunities to fail fast but learn quickly in a sense.

CONS:
The game will force you to learn hard mechanics to progress, so this fact may turn some players mid way through the game. Dying to a boss means you have to backtrack through enemies and terrain to re battle but there is ALWAYS a shortcut hidden around, so if you feel like the backtracking is getting ridiculous, there is probably a shortcut you are missing. Platforming can be an issue because jumping is variable based on how hard you mash the button on a ps4 controller/key on a keyboard. There are many times when the jump falls short of the platform and I die because I pressed 0.0001 oz per square inch of pressure too little or much...Also, when you die, you are not always taken to the most logical respawn point, which at times I believe may be a bug; accidental pun...:-). For example, I may have traversed a tough platforming course, and then I die to an enemy after reaching the other side and landing for 2 seconds, which normally means I will respawn where I landed safely, but it takes me all the way back to the beginning even though I did go from what appeared to be Point A to Point B successfully. This just seemed too unforgiving even for bug souls. Enemy attacks also continue moving/firing even after you kill them, which is lame and unreal. You can literally die, respawn and get spawn killed by a projectile that was fired out of frame 3 seconds ago before you died.
Last thing I wanted to mention is the fact that I was dissapointed that there is a weapon slot in the inventory, but there are no new weapons to find throughout the game that could have added a hugely unique addition to combat. Instead Hollow Knight gets new magic bearing skills and same weapon upgrades to do more damage. There are some really cool nail/sword users in the game that would have been more fun to beat if I hadn't had been able to just blast them to smitherines with magic from a safe distance. Soul Magic definitely becomes too OP when used against cool sword bearing enemies with unique mechanics for sword on sword combat, but when the game actually requires you to fight enemies with magic, it becomes a nightmare trying to land a hit because they are the dodgiest ♥♥♥♥♥ in the game. A throwable lance or shield would have been interesting on some bosses and maybe enemy weapons could have been obtainable or useable for a limited time.
My advice is to not let the difficulty of this game scare you away. You don't want to miss a sweet and mysterious storyline of a kingdom left behind with dark undertones and lessons of the past and underlying themes that define your character and beautifully written musical scores, a journey that will bring you memorable friends, foes, and others all cast in an amazing game with phantasmal art direction. This game will woop your butt, butt :-) the payoff is so so crunchy sweet like one of those crickets in a lollipop candy. TRY IT!!!
I hope this review helps anyone looking to purchase Hollow Knight and I hope to see more great content from Team Cherry in the future...maybe some DLC for this game even? L:
Until then,

This game contains loads of distilled Dark Souls essence, processed into a solid and lovely hand-drawn 2D metroidvania with beautiful atmospheric musical accompaniment. The desolateness of the world, your quest as the chosen hollow, peculiar NPCs, and epic bossfights are merely a few of the parallels.
In my opinion, it stands out positively in several points compared with the genre precursor Ori and the blind Forest.
It definitely provides more content and a larger world to explore; you will need at least 30 hours to fully complete your first playthrough (which puts some AAA titles to shame). The battles as well as the platforming parts feel more appropriate; there are no unfair one-hit-death situations like Ori does have in its chasing sequences. Everything comes down to your own ability and skill, every death is your own culpability and will be a teaching.
Altogether Hollow Knight is an absolute must-buy if you are into this kind of games. Games made with heart, passion, and obsession to detail.

Forward: I've been playing this game in offline mode so my hours haven't been officially logged, but I've probably put close to 30-40 hours in at the time of this review.
This game competes for the best Assassin's Creed title to date since AC II. And AC II is in my top 10 games of the past 20 years.
First off, the gameplay. This game definitely take a bit of a change from the AC titles of old that put emphasis (ish) on stealth. You're a pirate with two swords. And four pistols. And a lot of other tools in your arsenal. If there's no stealth bonus for the particular mission you're playing, or the game doesn't require you to stay hidden, it's actually to your advantage to go in guns blazing and swords flashing. You'll get the job done quicker and if you're even moderately okay at countering enemy attacks, it's possible to get through the entire game without taking a single point of damage to Edward. Pretty cool. The kill animations are also pretty satisfying, so bonus for that too.
The climbing animations are fantastic as well. Scaling tall buildings in mere seconds has never felt so good. That 5 story church tower over there? You can climb it in probably 6 seconds. Edward climbs fast, and his agility is definitely a focal point of his animations.
The story. I haven't finished it yet, but I think I'm probably 80ish percent done. The story is probably the second best part of this game. As is AC's trademark, there are famous people integrated quite well, and you can actually develop feelings towards these different characters, including Edward. Without saying much, it is a long story in comparison to the previous AC titles because of.....
The sailing. The naval mechanics of this game are EXTREMELY well done. This alone could have sold this game. The camera angles look good and aren't crazy, and changing the angle is as simple as can be. The ship you sail on, the Jackdaw, comes with plenty of weapons too, and changing which weapon you fire is as simple as changing the camera angle. The story takes so long because it's absolutely essential you upgrade your ship to progress. Edward upgrades come last (unless it's crafting. Those don't cost reales), Jackdaw upgrades are hugely important.
Basically, 9.5/10

I haven't even fully beaten this game (I just got to a fairly pivitol point in the story) and I've put over 20 hours into it. This game is MASSIVE! It features charming and well done hand drawn art. This game is considered part of the "Metroidvania" genre of gaming. This game will give you tons of hours of enjoyment exploring the world created by people who obviously put amazing amounts of detail into each area. Just when you think you've discovered it all... BAM! New areas just pop up in your face!
The games cast of NPC's are all very diverse and intriguing, and the story itself, while not having finished it yet, is very interesting and rather deep. The lore will keep you immersed along with the fantastic enviroments and beautiful music and ambience.
The best thing is this game doesn't hold your hand. It teaches you the basics and helps you learn through enemy placements and level design, each area progressively becoming more difficult where you put what you learned from previous areas to the test. There are upgrades that do allow you to go to certain areas, but for the most part you're totally free to explore the world without any overbearing narrative or waypoints. You're given total control on where you want to go. There's even ways to sequence break with enough skill and resourcefulness.
It feels like a bit of Dark Souls mixed in with Metroidvania and the entire package is just amazing. I can't praise this game enough. It's not that it does anything new to the Metroidvania genre, but there are some things that aren't seen or done as often. What really makes the game is the immersion. It's like the classic Metroid for the NES and Super Metroid on the SNES. It takes the best attributes of the genre with a unique penatly system for dying that isn't too brutal or too easy, much like Dark Souls.
The bosses all have patterns you can learn, and are designed very well. One boss fight in particular was incredible with how it teaches you the fight. There are tons of enemies and things to find and collect. You can find and buy charms that enhance your abililties, such as increased melee range, less soul energy spent for magic spells and even one that makes you smell like dung! (Not joking it's actually useful too)
Honestly if you love Metroidvania and exploration and deep immersion, I highly reccomend playing this game. It's price of 14.99 with this level of depth and content is almost a steal. It's so cheap and it offers a deeper experience then games that cost twice as much! Seriously though, give it a try. You can always refund it if it doesn't turn out to be your cup of tea after all, but if you love adventure and Metroidvania, you won't be dissapointed.

Support hero Sirius however has a dodge and a counter that even teleports him to a new place, oh did i mention he has an AOE petrify that lasts for 3.4 secs? Also his standard attack can infilct weaken which reduces healing and DAMAGE for 50% over 2.5 secs (Up to 3.5 secs). Pick a hero and fight in an arena against other players.  That's the main premise of Battlerite, and while that might not sound that exciting the game's core mechanics and balance is well done.
You pick a hero (15 total at the moment), choose 3v3 or 2v2, and jump almost instantly into a game.  At the start of each round you pick a Battlerite (which is a buff for your abilities that lasts in each concurrent round).  You spawn on the left side of the arena and head straight to the middle and fight over middle control. Each game is a bo5, and each round doesn't last too long.  Games are quick so it's easy to fix and understand your mistakes.
The mechanics of Battlerite are neat, and play like a fighting game. You have energy and health, and as you get hit you lose some of your max health.  Poking is very important in Battlerite.  In the middle of the arena is an orb which when burst open gives energy and some lost max health back. Energy is used for your ultimate (which cost 100%), and a lesser ability that is pretty strong (which cost 25%).  Each hero also has two EX abilities, similar to a fighting game.   These 2 upgraded abilities cost a varying amount of energy and make a skill stronger. Each hero also has a mount + mount speedbost.  The mount has a small channel time, so you can use it to get around the arena and get straight into the action at the start of each round.
Overall, Battlerite feels and plays like a completed game.  The game's future looks bright, and I'd gladly recommend it to anyone who enjoys PVP battles.  Even if you are casual as hell, the game offers a lot of fun and is easy to understand.   With only more content to come, it's a great purchase.

I have never reviewed a game before but I followed Hollow Knight for a month before release because I saw the trailer that made me think of rogue legacy, but this is a metroidvania not a rogue like and I am in love. Some say "Oh joyous day another 2D metroidvania just what we need"...but WAIT. It is not just another clone and here's why.
Art and Atmosphere 5/5
PROS:
The hand drawn art already makes it fantasticly unique, but pleasant voices added to characters and enemies is a plus. The atmospheric elements from the backgrounds and foregrounds with colors and hints of symbolism make you feel connected to the character in each area as if it were the first time exploring. Then the wonderful orchestrated music always chips in to give you all the more reason to brave the new pathways in the good times and bad times.
CONS:
The parallax scrolling in Unity is glitchy at times but only noticeable in tiny corners of caves where a layer is clipping through another and only identifiable by a player with an eagle eye. The thick borders around characters make them look as if they were nothing special of hand drawn compared to pencil and paper look and feel, but it is easily forgivable knowing it helps them stand out among the borderless background and foreground. The concept art for this game is amazing, and you should check it.
Replayability and Length 4.5/5
PROS:
This game is LONG so be prepared for countless hours to be sunk, and it is highly replayable because there is enough content to make each playthrough vastly different. To achieve 100% takes the amount of time as 1/2 of the main storyline, which already alone takes an extremely long time to finish ~30 hours for me. I have been playing for two weeks now many hours each day. I saw vastly different zones and that drew me in hoping to uncover some sort of mystery in each area. The map is huge and you are may finish the game without ever visiting awesome areas if you don't explore enough, and the game is best when you play blindly without looking up the map online.

CONS:
There is a lot of backtracking that can be forgivable however because there are elements that change throughout each area when you go back to revisit different zones. Certain characters might be in zones you have once visited or change their dialogue once you progress further in the story and they tend to provide subtle clues and additions to the storyline. The map serves as a huge element to this game, so after you know where everything is, you can expect your desire to play the game over again to diminish. This is why you do not look up the map and where to go next because spoilers will kill this game. Also the abscense of unlockable characters to play as is slightly more dissapointing seeing as some characters look so fun to play as and would make replaying so much more worth.
Gameplay 4/5 (Platforming and Mechanics)
PROS:
This is what I have been looking for after playing Dark Souls and Nioh because I am addicted to punishing yet rewarding gameplay with the beautiful atmosphere and storyline that is introduced through gameplay and subtle atmospheric elements by exploration. Another great aspect, exploration is highly rewarded in this game as expected of a metroidvania. The learning curve is like that of dark souls, whereas you are given a poopy starter kit and combat relies on sheer skill but as you collect currency in the form of geo you have the option to upgrade your equip and abilities. And as you learn the art of the nail, your weapon, with upgraded equipment, spells, and a gemcraft-like charm system that give you unique bonuses and abilities combat skill will pay off against tougher enemies. The game does a fantastic job teaching you how to conquer hard enemies without pointing it out so obviously. Also...I bought this game soul-ely :-) for the bosses because I am a fanatic for epic boss battles, and I was not dissapointed. There are over 30 boss fights with uniquely voiced enemies and each one vastly unique in making you play the dodge-hit-dodge mechanic game. This game's platforming is also a breath of fresh air...to master the 2D mechanics of platforming once again clenching my butt cheeks like I did many years ago playing Super Mario Bros with highly rewarding hidden items at the end of the hard platforming courses. Many new skills you obtain constantly introduces new platforming challenges in areas, but each area is well designed to help you master each new skill and there are many opportunities to fail fast but learn quickly in a sense.

CONS:
The game will force you to learn hard mechanics to progress, so this fact may turn some players mid way through the game. Dying to a boss means you have to backtrack through enemies and terrain to re battle but there is ALWAYS a shortcut hidden around, so if you feel like the backtracking is getting ridiculous, there is probably a shortcut you are missing. Platforming can be an issue because jumping is variable based on how hard you mash the button on a ps4 controller/key on a keyboard. There are many times when the jump falls short of the platform and I die because I pressed 0.0001 oz per square inch of pressure too little or much...Also, when you die, you are not always taken to the most logical respawn point, which at times I believe may be a bug; accidental pun...:-). For example, I may have traversed a tough platforming course, and then I die to an enemy after reaching the other side and landing for 2 seconds, which normally means I will respawn where I landed safely, but it takes me all the way back to the beginning even though I did go from what appeared to be Point A to Point B successfully. This just seemed too unforgiving even for bug souls. Enemy attacks also continue moving/firing even after you kill them, which is lame and unreal. You can literally die, respawn and get spawn killed by a projectile that was fired out of frame 3 seconds ago before you died.
Last thing I wanted to mention is the fact that I was dissapointed that there is a weapon slot in the inventory, but there are no new weapons to find throughout the game that could have added a hugely unique addition to combat. Instead Hollow Knight gets new magic bearing skills and same weapon upgrades to do more damage. There are some really cool nail/sword users in the game that would have been more fun to beat if I hadn't had been able to just blast them to smitherines with magic from a safe distance. Soul Magic definitely becomes too OP when used against cool sword bearing enemies with unique mechanics for sword on sword combat, but when the game actually requires you to fight enemies with magic, it becomes a nightmare trying to land a hit because they are the dodgiest ♥♥♥♥♥ in the game. A throwable lance or shield would have been interesting on some bosses and maybe enemy weapons could have been obtainable or useable for a limited time.
My advice is to not let the difficulty of this game scare you away. You don't want to miss a sweet and mysterious storyline of a kingdom left behind with dark undertones and lessons of the past and underlying themes that define your character and beautifully written musical scores, a journey that will bring you memorable friends, foes, and others all cast in an amazing game with phantasmal art direction. This game will woop your butt, butt :-) the payoff is so so crunchy sweet like one of those crickets in a lollipop candy. TRY IT!!!
I hope this review helps anyone looking to purchase Hollow Knight and I hope to see more great content from Team Cherry in the future...maybe some DLC for this game even? L:
Until then,

So, after i played some hours, i can say that i really enjoyed playing Battlerite.
The abilities feel good, the characters show great diversity, the fights are fun and intense, the rounds are quick.
Battlerite is very competitive and with every game you are trying to improve your skills more and more, dodge more attacks and ultis, support your teammates, play mind games with the ennemies. A Match takes about 5 to 15 minutes (my experience). You are able to chose between 2 vs 2 games or 3 vs 3 games. It's pure PvP. "Feeding" an ennemy is impossible, there's no ingame shop to buy better items during the match. After every round every player is able to chose one upgrade for his character, so you can adjust your character in every new game.
I know that Battlerite is Early Acess, but i still wanna write down the negative things. I hope those will be patched in the future.
- There's no option to lower or higher your mouse sensitivity. This option should be very important in such a fast game, because some people prefer lower or higher mouse sensitivity. You really need to "aim" in Battlerite.
- AFK's. I saw that there is a report button after every match. I just hope that the developers deal with this problem. I'm having an AFK like every 5th game. Why? Because it's very easy to just click the join button and idle a whole match. People are doing this to level up there characters (for each level you get ingame money to buy cosmetics or chests. at some levels you get chests right away. You can open those chests to get some new cosmetics or Avatars. You don't need to buy keys for real money to open those chests, like we know from other games). Players abuse the possibility to idle whole matches. I just hope they are getting banned for some days for doing this.
- Adding a possibilty to enable "Instant-Casts" in the options would be great too, but it's not one of the most important things for this game. It would be still a nice feature to add this.
Nontheless it's a great game for this Early Stage, i hope to see a lot more Characters and Arenas in the future.

Simply wonderful.
This game contains loads of distilled Dark Souls essence, processed into a solid and lovely hand-drawn 2D metroidvania with beautiful atmospheric musical accompaniment. The desolateness of the world, your quest as the chosen hollow, peculiar NPCs, and epic bossfights are merely a few of the parallels.
In my opinion, it stands out positively in several points compared with the genre precursor Ori and the blind Forest.
It definitely provides more content and a larger world to explore; you will need at least 30 hours to fully complete your first playthrough (which puts some AAA titles to shame). The battles as well as the platforming parts feel more appropriate; there are no unfair one-hit-death situations like Ori does have in its chasing sequences. Everything comes down to your own ability and skill, every death is your own culpability and will be a teaching.
Altogether Hollow Knight is an absolute must-buy if you are into this kind of games. Games made with heart, passion, and obsession to detail.

A quick note for the undecided...
Hollow Knight models its world and mechanics similarly to Metroidvania style games that we all know and love, but I feel it can be easily misunderstood by overlooking its core combat mechanic. Enemies have combo attacks, you do not, so you have to learn how to sting like a bug. It requires you to know your enemies and when you must precisely strike. Your knight actually recoils back when striking foes so landing a hit also incorporates a dodge mechanic. It can be easy to want to over complicate the game's design by importing your own expectations taught to you from familiar titles.
You won't rip through the map like a bashing forest sprite. You won't up your arsenal to overcome Dracula's forces. You won't charge your beam cannon to blast weak points on bosses. You are a small, calculated bug. The power of observation influences your decisions and you will have a bad time if you panic.
Master this idea and you'll be ready to explore a game full of charm, fun, secrets and suprises.

08/05/2014 EDIT:
Dungeon Defenders isn't quite what it used to be, as amazing as it is. What I mean is, the community isn't the same. I'm sure there'll be plenty to disagree, but various times I've tried for games, I've come up with very few. It's a shame, but I suppose all good things must come to an end, at least for me.
I have some excellent memories of this game, and even with the online situation being somewhat less than it was, I still absolutely recommend it. The vast trading, all the trophies, enormous amount of gear to collect, the sheer amount of tactics and co-operation, ... there's just too much for me to possibly encapsulate in a few paragraphs of text.
I don't play this game anymore, ... I don't really play much of anything anymore, but I do remember--just about--a few things that were negatives about this game:
1. The community could sometimes be a bit harsh, but there were also more than enough friendly, helpful players, at least in my experience. Trading could be rough, but it was fun and rewarding, once I figured it all out.
2. Unfortunately, there were quite a few hacked items floating around, which was an incredibly disheartening thing for me. I was disgusted when I "got" my very first hacked sword, ... I was completely oblivious, thinking it was just really cool, ... although my Spidey senses were tingling, I guess I just didn't want to believe it, until people happily pointed it out. I dumped the sword and was quite peed off. Still, I didn't find it to be TOO excessive, such as in Torchlight II, in which I just found no sense of achievement, amongst people that are basically God. I like to share my accomplishments and yes, I can be competative, so cheaters with online games like this are a negative for me.
3. Performance, even on a powerful rig, was a problem, pretty much down to the game itself, not a hardware thing. Still, the game runs well, the last few times I launched it and tested split-screen on King's Game, something that used to lag like a ♥♥♥♥♥. I'm quite pleased with the performance, nowadays, but I still think it's not very good, I guess I just got used to it. An oversight worth, ... looking over.
If it's still anything like I remember, and it's your kind of genre, then definitely get it.
NOTE: I'd avoid this game like the plague, if you only have Linux, as it simply doesn't work properly on it. Google "can't collect gems on Dungeon Defenders Linux" or something to that effect, and you'll see why it's basically unplayable.
If you have any questions, feel free to ask. It has been a long time, but I still remember bits and pieces.

Hollow Knight is an incredible game. It's enormous, looks and sounds fantastic and the gameplay, too, is excellent. I would easily rate it 10/10 if not for the lack of difficulty options.
If you're good at hard games, buy Hollow Knight now. No need to read on. The rest of this review is for everybody else.
It's not very clear from the store page description just how "challenging" Hollow Knight is. Make no mistake, this game is right up there with Dark Souls (forum search: "Hollow Knight vs Dark Souls 3"). Even still, the game is so appealing that it draws you in and won't let you go. You feel compelled to push on and beat each boss because the game is just so well made and the satisfaction of making progress is kind of addictive.
But we all have our limits. After 93 hours, I managed to 100% Hollow Knight and get the true ending, but the boss battles took a LOT of attempts. Sure, it may be rewarding to conquer a challenge after such effort, but that doesn't make it enjoyable. I would have much rather played an easier version of the game, than struggle through it like an idiot.
I understand that this was the intention of the developers and that an Easy mode would somehow cheapen the accomplishment of beating the game on "Normal", but at the very least, Team Cherry need to put a warning label on it so people like me don't buy it and rate it down. As it is, I can't recommend something that I consider too difficult to be enjoyable.

This game is an absolute masterpiece. I expected it to be good, but I didn't realise it would be this good.
In terms of gameplay people are comparing it to Dark Souls. Yes, there are some elements there, but it's more of a metroidvania than a Souls game. Like a Souls game though it does provide the perfect amount of challenge, the right kind of challenge: each enemy or boss is cleverly designed and you have to solve it like a puzzle until you fully understand how to counter its attacks and defences.
This strange underground world of insects is beautifully presented and it comes deep with lore and mystery. The artwork is a delight for the senses, both the sound and the visuals. The hand-drawn animations are gorgeous beyond compare: I was beginning to think that anything without pixel-style graphics was hideous, but this game proves that non-pixel non-retro 2D games can be stylish and beautiful (compare with the character designs from Salt & Sanctuary for example). Everything from the characters to the environments, it's all highly detailed. At times I have just paused with wonder and disbelief as I take in the surroundings and the emotional classical soundtrack, every scene is like watching a bitter-sweet painting.
I'm struggling to find anything to criticise about the game. Admittedly the game is full of bugs..but it's meant to be! (A bad joke, you know, bugs aka insects?).
The game is also deep and long: a huge dark world to explore full of mysteries and secrets. I give this game my full recommendation. I would have happily pay more than twice the asking price for this; it's worth $30 at the very least. If you don't grab this game you're missing out on a truly unique masterpiece.
